chunks.title: Adaptation (method)
chunks.text: Adaptation (method) التكييف · A very free rewriting; some specialists see it as a new text, not a translation. 4.1

chunks.title: Adaptation (procedure)
chunks.text: Adaptation (procedure) التكييف · Replacing a cultural situation with a familiar one. 4.2

chunks.title: Addition
chunks.text: Addition · الإضافة · Adding words or information that the reader needs. 4.3

chunks.title: Approximation
chunks.text: Approximation · التقريب · Rendering the meaning of the source text as closely as possible in the target language, knowing that an exact match is impossible. 1.1

chunks.title: Audio description
chunks.text: Audio description · الوصف الصوتي · A spoken description of what happens on screen, for blind and partially sighted viewers. 10.1

chunks.title: Audiovisual translation (AVT)
chunks.text: Audiovisual translation (AVT) الترجمة السمعية البصرية · Translating texts that combine words, images and sound, such as films and video games. 10.1

chunks.title: Bilingual dictionary
chunks.text: Bilingual dictionary · معجم ثنائي اللغة · A dictionary that gives equivalents in another language. 8.1

chunks.title: Borrowing
chunks.text: Borrowing · الاقتراض · Taking a word from the source language as it is. 4.2

chunks.title: Calque
chunks.text: Calque · النسخ · Translating each part of an expression literally; also called loan translation (Section 8.3). 4.2

chunks.title: Censorship
chunks.text: Censorship · الرقابة · Removing or changing content that is considered unacceptable. 10.2

chunks.title: Client
chunks.text: Client · العميل · The person or organisation that asks for a translation. 1.2

chunks.title: Collocation
chunks.text: Collocation · التلازم اللفظي · Words that naturally go together; the company a word keeps. 3.1

chunks.title: Collocations dictionary
chunks.text: Collocations dictionary · معجم المتلازمات · A dictionary of the natural word partners of a language. 8.1

chunks.title: Commissioned translator
chunks.text: Commissioned translator · مترجم بتكليف · A translator who translates a text at someone else’s request. 1.1

chunks.title: Communicative purpose
chunks.text: Communicative purpose · الغرض التواصلي · What the translation is for: to inform, persuade, instruct or entertain. 1.2

chunks.title: Compensation
chunks.text: Compensation · التعويض · Making up for an effect lost in one place by creating a similar effect elsewhere. 4.3

chunks.title: Concept
chunks.text: Concept · المفهوم · An idea that a word or term stands for. 6.2

chunks.title: Connotation
chunks.text: Connotation · المعنى الإيحائي · The extra feeling or association a word carries. 2.2

chunks.title: Context
chunks.text: Context · السياق · Everything around a word or text that helps us understand it: the surrounding words and the wider situation. 2.3

chunks.title: Cultural approximation
chunks.text: Cultural approximation · التقريب الثقافي · Bringing the source text’s cultural meaning as close as possible to the target reader. 6.1

chunks.title: Cultural substitution
chunks.text: Cultural substitution · الاستبدال الثقافي · Replacing a cultural reference with one that is familiar to the target reader. 4.3

chunks.title: Culture-bound term
chunks.text: Culture-bound term · مصطلح ذو خصوصية ثقافية · A reference to something from one culture, such as a food or a holiday. Also called a culture-specific item (Section 6.1). 10.2

chunks.title: Culture-specific item
chunks.text: Culture-specific item · عنصر ذو خصوصية ثقافية · A word, custom or reference that belongs to one culture. 6.1

chunks.title: Denotation
chunks.text: Denotation · المعنى المعجمي · The basic, dictionary meaning of a word. 2.2

chunks.title: Descriptive translation
chunks.text: Descriptive translation · الترجمة الوصفية · Paraphrasing a source expression by describing its meaning. Also called explanatory translation (الترجمة الشرحية, Chapter 13). 6.2

chunks.title: Dialect
chunks.text: Dialect · اللهجة العامية · The everyday spoken Arabic of a country or region. 5.1

chunks.title: Dialogue list
chunks.text: Dialogue list · قائمة الحوار · A written script of everything said in a film, given to the translator. 10.2

chunks.title: Domestication
chunks.text: Domestication · التوطين · Making a translation feel local to the target reader. Venuti's term, against foreignisation. 4.3

chunks.title: Localisation
chunks.text: Localisation · الأقلمة · Adapting a product to a market — language, format, law, culture. Often called التوطين too, which is why this entry exists: that word is already Venuti's domestication. 7.2

chunks.title: Draft
chunks.text: Draft · المسوّدة · The first version of a translation. 9.1

chunks.title: Dubbing
chunks.text: Dubbing · الدبلجة · Replacing the original dialogue with recorded dialogue in the target language. 10.1

chunks.title: Equivalence
chunks.text: Equivalence · التكافؤ · A match between a source-language expression and a target-language expression. 2.4

chunks.title: Equivalence (procedure)
chunks.text: Equivalence (procedure) التكافؤ · Describing the same situation with a completely different expression, often an idiom or a proverb. 4.2

chunks.title: Explanatory translation
chunks.text: Explanatory translation · الترجمة الشرحية · Explaining a word or expression that has no equivalent. 4.3

chunks.title: Field
chunks.text: Field · المجال · The subject area of a text, such as politics, health or law. 7.1

chunks.title: Figurative language
chunks.text: Figurative language · اللغة المجازية · Language used in a non-literal way to create an image or effect. 3.3

chunks.title: Foreignisation
chunks.text: Foreignisation · التغريب · Keeping the foreign flavour of the source text. 4.3

chunks.title: Form
chunks.text: Form · الشكل · The structure of language: a word, phrase, clause, sentence or text. 2.1

chunks.title: Formal equivalence
chunks.text: Formal equivalence · التكافؤ الشكلي · Keeping the form of the original: passive for passive, verb for verb. 2.4

chunks.title: Free translation
chunks.text: Free translation · الترجمة الحرّة · Keeping the message but not the form; also called loose translation. 4.1

chunks.title: Functional equivalence
chunks.text: Functional equivalence · التكافؤ الوظيفي · Using a target-language expression that serves the same function, whatever its form. 2.4

chunks.title: Functional translation
chunks.text: Functional translation · الترجمة الوظيفية · Translating with a target-language expression that has the same function. 4.3

chunks.title: Genre
chunks.text: Genre · الجنس النصّي · A kind of text with its own rules, such as a news report, a contract or a poem. 7.1

chunks.title: Hallucination
chunks.text: Hallucination · الهلوسة · Invented or false content produced by an AI tool, such as facts that are not in the source text. 8.4

chunks.title: Homonymy
chunks.text: Homonymy · المشترك اللفظي · One word with several meanings that are not related. 2.3

chunks.title: Ideational equivalence
chunks.text: Ideational equivalence · التكافؤ الفكري · Giving only the basic idea, in plain words. 2.4

chunks.title: Ideology
chunks.text: Ideology · الأيديولوجيا · A set of beliefs that shapes how people describe events. 7.3

chunks.title: Idiom
chunks.text: Idiom · التعبير الاصطلاحي · A fixed expression whose meaning is not the sum of the meanings of its words. 3.2

chunks.title: Simultaneous interpreting
chunks.text: Simultaneous interpreting · الترجمة الفورية · Rendered while the speaker is still speaking, from a booth. One mode of الترجمة الشفوية, not another name for it. The lag behind the speaker is called the décalage. 1.1

chunks.title: Consecutive interpreting
chunks.text: Consecutive interpreting · الترجمة التتابعية · Rendered after the speaker pauses, from notes and memory. Also written التتبعية and التعاقبية. The notes carry structure, numbers, names and links — not words. 1.1

chunks.title: Sight translation
chunks.text: Sight translation · الترجمة المنظورة · A written text read out in the other language on the spot. Also الترجمة بالنظر. Written input, spoken output, which is why it belongs to interpreting rather than translation. 1.1

chunks.title: Whispered interpreting
chunks.text: Whispered interpreting · الترجمة الهمسية · Simultaneous interpreting delivered in a low voice beside one or two listeners, with no booth and no equipment. Known in the profession by its French name, chuchotage. 1.1

chunks.title: Relay interpreting
chunks.text: Relay interpreting · الترجمة المرحلية · Interpreting through a third language, when no interpreter has both of the ones needed. The middle booth is the pivot, and every error in it is inherited by everyone downstream. 1.1

chunks.title: Remote interpreting
chunks.text: Remote interpreting · الترجمة الفورية عن بُعد · Interpreting delivered over a platform, by video or telephone, with the interpreter not in the room. A working arrangement rather than a mode, and it shortens the handover intervals. 1.1

chunks.title: Interpreting
chunks.text: Interpreting · الترجمة الشفوية · Transferring spoken language into another language — the term that covers the whole activity, as against الترجمة التحريرية, written translation. Its modes are الترجمة الفورية, rendered while the speaker is still speaking; الترجمة التتابعية, rendered from notes once the speaker pauses; الترجمة المنظورة, a written text read out in the other language; and الترجمة الهمسية, whispered to one or two listeners. The spelling الشفوية is also current — both restore a different dropped letter from شفة — and you will meet it in UN usage. 1.1

chunks.title: Justification
chunks.text: Justification · التبرير · The reason why a translation choice is right. 9.3

chunks.title: Lexical creation
chunks.text: Lexical creation · التوليد المعجمي · Coining new target-language words for items with no direct equivalent. 8.3

chunks.title: Literal translation
chunks.text: Literal translation · الترجمة الحرفية · Keeping the original words, changing only what grammar requires; also called modified literal translation (الترجمة الحرفية المعدّلة). 4.1

chunks.title: Loaded word
chunks.text: Loaded word · كلمة مشحونة · A word that carries a judgement, positive or negative. 7.3

chunks.title: Loan translation (calque)
chunks.text: Loan translation (calque) النسخ · Translating the parts of a compound word one by one. 8.3

chunks.title: Machine translation (MT)
chunks.text: Machine translation (MT) الترجمة الآلية · Translation done by software, such as online translation tools or AI chat tools. 8.4

chunks.title: Macro context
chunks.text: Macro context · سياق الموقف (الخارجي) The wider situation: the author, audience, time, place and circumstances of a text. 2.3

chunks.title: Meaning
chunks.text: Meaning · المعنى · The idea that a form expresses. 2.1

chunks.title: Mental draft
chunks.text: Mental draft · المسوّدة الذهنية · A first idea of the translation that you form while reading the text. 1.2

chunks.title: Metaphor
chunks.text: Metaphor · الاستعارة · A comparison without “as” or “like”; using a word in a non-basic meaning. 3.3

chunks.title: Micro context (co-text)
chunks.text: Micro context (co-text) السياق اللغوي (الداخلي) The words and sentences immediately around a word. 2.3

chunks.title: Modern Standard Arabic (MSA)
chunks.text: Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) الفصحى المعاصرة · The Arabic of newspapers, laws and education. 5.1

chunks.title: Modulation
chunks.text: Modulation · التطويع · Expressing the same idea from another point of view. 4.2

chunks.title: Monolingual dictionary
chunks.text: Monolingual dictionary · معجم أحادي اللغة · A dictionary that explains words in the same language. 8.1

chunks.title: Neologism
chunks.text: Neologism · اللفظ المستحدث · A new word, or an existing word given a new meaning. 8.3

chunks.title: Omission
chunks.text: Omission · الحذف · Leaving out words that are unnecessary in the target language. 4.3

chunks.title: Polysemy
chunks.text: Polysemy · تعدّد المعنى · One word with several meanings that are related. 2.3

chunks.title: Post-editing
chunks.text: Post-editing · التحرير اللاحق · A human correcting and improving machine translation output, lightly or fully. 8.4

chunks.title: Proverb
chunks.text: Proverb · المثل · A traditional saying that gives advice or states a truth. 3.2

chunks.title: Register
chunks.text: Register · المستوى اللغوي · How formal or informal the language is. 5.1

chunks.title: Revision
chunks.text: Revision · المراجعة · Checking a translation against the source and correcting it. 9.1

chunks.title: Risk
chunks.text: Risk · الخطر · The chance that a choice causes a problem, and how serious it would be. 9.2

chunks.title: Risk management
chunks.text: Risk management · إدارة المخاطر · Spending more effort where a mistake could cause more harm. 9.2

chunks.title: Risk matrix
chunks.text: Risk matrix · مصفوفة تقييم المخاطر · A table of possible risks, how serious they are, and what to do. 9.2

chunks.title: Self-initiated translator
chunks.text: Self-initiated translator · مترجم بمبادرة ذاتية · A translator who chooses a text to translate on their own initiative. 1.1

chunks.title: Sentence meaning
chunks.text: Sentence meaning · معنى الجملة · What the words of a sentence say. 2.2

chunks.title: Simile
chunks.text: Simile · التشبيه · A comparison that uses “as” or “like”. 3.3

chunks.title: Skopos theory
chunks.text: Skopos theory · نظرية الغاية · The idea that the purpose of a translation decides how it is translated. 10.1

chunks.title: Source text (ST)
chunks.text: Source text (ST) النص المصدر · The original text that you translate. 1.1

chunks.title: Speaker meaning
chunks.text: Speaker meaning · مقصد المتكلم · What the speaker really means by saying it. 2.2

chunks.title: Specialised dictionary
chunks.text: Specialised dictionary · معجم متخصص · A dictionary for one field, such as law or medicine. 8.1

chunks.title: Subtitling
chunks.text: Subtitling · السترجة / الترجمة المرئية · Showing a written version of the dialogue, usually at the bottom of the screen, together with important on-screen text and song lyrics. 10.2

chunks.title: Taboo language
chunks.text: Taboo language · اللغة المحظورة · Words that a society or religion forbids or restricts, such as swear words. 10.2

chunks.title: Target audience
chunks.text: Target audience · الجمهور المستهدف · The people who will read the translation. 1.2

chunks.title: Target text (TT)
chunks.text: Target text (TT) النص الهدف · Your translation. 1.1

chunks.title: Term
chunks.text: Term · المصطلح · A word or expression that names a concept in a special field. 8.2

chunks.title: Term list
chunks.text: Term list · قائمة المصطلحات · A list of the approved terms for a project, with their translations. 8.2

chunks.title: Termbase
chunks.text: Termbase · قاعدة بيانات المصطلحات (بنك المصطلحات) A database of terms and information about them. 8.2

chunks.title: Terminologist
chunks.text: Terminologist · المصطلحي (خبير المصطلحات) A specialist who collects, describes and records the terms of a field, and sometimes standardises them, in one or more languages. 8.2

chunks.title: Terminology
chunks.text: Terminology · علم المصطلح (المصطلحية) The study, collection and management of specialised terms; also the set of terms used in one field. 8.2

chunks.title: Terminology guide
chunks.text: Terminology guide · دليل المصطلحات · A document that tells translators which terms to use for a client. 8.2

chunks.title: Text
chunks.text: Text · النص · Any piece of language, written or spoken, that forms a complete message: from a one-word sign to a whole book. 7.1

chunks.title: Text analysis
chunks.text: Text analysis · تحليل النص · Breaking down and studying a text before translating it. 7.1

chunks.title: Text type
chunks.text: Text type · نمط النص · A group of texts that share one main function: to inform, to express or to persuade. 7.2

chunks.title: Tone
chunks.text: Tone · النبرة · The writer’s attitude: neutral, critical, friendly, straightforward. 7.1

chunks.title: Translation
chunks.text: Translation · الترجمة · Transferring meaning from one language into another. In a narrow sense, written translation (الترجمة التحريرية), as opposed to interpreting. 1.1

chunks.title: Translation brief
chunks.text: Translation brief · موجز الترجمة · The client’s instructions for a translation: who it is for, what it is for and any other requirements. 1.2

chunks.title: Translation commentary
chunks.text: Translation commentary · التعليق على الترجمة · A text that explains the problems in a translation and justifies the solutions. 9.3

chunks.title: Translation procedure
chunks.text: Translation procedure · إجراء الترجمة · A technique for translating a word, phrase or sentence. 4.2

chunks.title: Translation strategy
chunks.text: Translation strategy · استراتيجية الترجمة · A planned solution to a translation problem. 4.3

chunks.title: Transliteration
chunks.text: Transliteration · النقل الصوتي · Writing the sounds of a word in the letters of another language. 6.2

chunks.title: Transposition
chunks.text: Transposition · الإبدال · Changing the word class, for example a noun into a verb. 4.2

chunks.title: Verbal sentence
chunks.text: Verbal sentence · الجملة الفعلية · A sentence that starts with a verb. 5.1

chunks.title: Voice-over
chunks.text: Voice-over · التعليق الصوتي · Recording a translation over the original voice, which can still be heard quietly. 10.1

chunks.title: Word order
chunks.text: Word order · ترتيب الكلمات · The order of the subject, verb and object in a sentence. 5.1

chunks.title: Restricted collocation
chunks.text: Restricted collocation · التلازم المقيَّد · A collocation in which one word accepts only a small set of partners, such as ارتكب جريمة (to perpetrate a crime). 3.1

chunks.title: Bound collocation
chunks.text: Bound collocation · التلازم المغلق · A collocation in which one word appears with only one partner, such as حرب ضروس (a fierce war). 3.1

chunks.title: Corpus
chunks.text: Corpus · الذخيرة اللغوية · A large electronic collection of real texts that can be searched to see how words are actually used. 3.1

chunks.title: False friend
chunks.text: False friend · الصديق المخادع · An expression that looks like one in the other language but means something different, such as فقد أعصابه (to lose one’s temper) and to lose one’s nerve. 3.2

chunks.title: Binomial
chunks.text: Binomial · المزاوجة · A fixed pair of words joined by “and” or “or”, such as null and void or الصالح والطالح. 3.4

chunks.title: Phrasal verb
chunks.text: Phrasal verb · الفعل العباري · An English verb with a particle whose meaning often cannot be worked out from its parts, such as take off. 3.4

chunks.title: Compound
chunks.text: Compound · الكلمة المركّبة · Two or more words that work as one word, such as handbag; Arabic usually uses an إضافة instead. 3.4

chunks.title: Dynamic equivalence
chunks.text: Dynamic equivalence · التكافؤ الديناميكي · Nida’s term for translating so that the new readers respond to the message as the original readers did (equivalent effect). 2.4

chunks.title: Diglossia
chunks.text: Diglossia · الازدواجية اللغوية · The coexistence of a standard variety (الفصحى) and spoken dialects (العامية) of one language, used in different situations. 5.2

chunks.title: Idiolect
chunks.text: Idiolect · اللهجة الفردية · The personal way of speaking of one individual. 5.2

chunks.title: Accent
chunks.text: Accent · اللكنة · A way of pronouncing a language that is typical of a region or group. 5.2

chunks.title: Neutral term
chunks.text: Neutral term · المصطلح المحايد · A word that is not marked as belonging to one region, used when translating for readers across the Arab world. 5.2

chunks.title: Transcription
chunks.text: Transcription · النقل الصوتي · Writing the sounds of a word in another script, rather than its letters. 6.2

chunks.title: Action verb
chunks.text: Action verb · فعل حركي · A verb that names an activity, such as walk, read or look. Opposite: stative verb. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Adjunct
chunks.text: Adjunct · مُلحَق ظرفي · An optional adverbial that adds information, such as always or carefully. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Adverbial phrase
chunks.text: Adverbial phrase · شبه جملة ظرفية · A group of words doing the work of an adverb, such as with a knife or tomorrow morning. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Affective meaning
chunks.text: Affective meaning · المعنى الانفعالي · The feelings or attitude a speaker shows (affection, disapproval), or the effect an utterance has on the listener. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Agent
chunks.text: Agent · الفاعل الحقيقي · In a passive sentence, who or what made the action happen (John in ‘The dinner was prepared by John’). Classical Arabic does not state it. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Alliteration
chunks.text: Alliteration · الجناس الاستهلالي · Repeating the same sound at the start of several words in a row. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Allusive meaning
chunks.text: Allusive meaning · المعنى الإلماحي · Meaning a word calls up by echoing another text or tradition, such as المُخَضْرَمون. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Anaphora
chunks.text: Anaphora · التكرار الاستهلالي / الإحالة · Repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive clauses or lines for effect (rhetorical anaphora); also pronouns referring back to earlier words (grammatical anaphora). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Antithesis
chunks.text: Antithesis · الطباق والمقابلة · A contrast of ideas or words set in a balanced, parallel construction. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Antonym
chunks.text: Antonym · الضدّ · A word with the opposite meaning, such as night and day. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Apposition
chunks.text: Apposition · البدل · A noun phrase placed after another to describe it, with no linking word: ‘This jacket, a hand-me-down, …’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Archaism
chunks.text: Archaism · اللفظ المهجور · An old or obsolete word or form; in legal English, aforesaid, heretofore, witnesseth. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Associative meaning
chunks.text: Associative meaning · المعنى الترابطي · Expectations attached to a referent, as when people assume a nurse is a woman. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Assonance
chunks.text: Assonance · السجع الصوتي · Repeating the same vowel sounds in words close together: ‘Thy kingdom come, thy will be done.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Asyndeton
chunks.text: Asyndeton · حذف أدوات العطف · Leaving out conjunctions between coordinated words, phrases or clauses. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Attitudinal meaning
chunks.text: Attitudinal meaning · المعنى الموقفي · The speaker’s attitude to the referent, shown through word choice (for example derogatory terms). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Causative verb
chunks.text: Causative verb · فعل سببي · A transitive verb that makes something happen, such as raise or persuade; Arabic often uses جَعَلَ. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Code-switching
chunks.text: Code-switching · التناوب اللغوي · Moving between two or more languages within the same stretch of speech or text. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Coherence
chunks.text: Coherence · الاتساق الدلالي · The thematic consistency that makes a text a connected whole rather than a string of unrelated sentences. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Cohesion
chunks.text: Cohesion · الترابط النصي · The links between parts of a text made by devices such as conjunctions, pronouns and repetition. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Collocative meaning
chunks.text: Collocative meaning · المعنى التلازمي · Meaning a word takes from the words it regularly appears with. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Communicative translation
chunks.text: Communicative translation · الترجمة التواصلية · Translation close to free translation, rendering source expressions with the culturally appropriate equivalents for the situation. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Concord
chunks.text: Concord · المطابقة · Agreement between the subject and the form of the verb, in number (and in Arabic in gender). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Copula
chunks.text: Copula · الفعل الرابط · A linking verb such as be, seem, become or remain, followed by an adjective, not an adverb (‘This is nice’, not ‘nicely’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Cultural transposition
chunks.text: Cultural transposition · النقل الثقافي · Replacing source culture-specific items with target ones: أَثْلَجَ قُلُوبَنا, ‘our hearts have been warmed’; Romeo and Juliet, قيس وليلى. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Ellipsis
chunks.text: Ellipsis · الحذف · Leaving out a word the reader can supply, such as a repeated subject: ‘He bought the ice-cream and (he) gave it to us.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Euphemism
chunks.text: Euphemism · التلطيف · Replacing a harsh or offensive expression with a milder one, as when ‘Piss off!’ becomes إمشي (‘Go!’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Exegetic translation
chunks.text: Exegetic translation · الترجمة التفسيرية · Translation that adds information not in the source to explain concepts to the target reader. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Explicitation
chunks.text: Explicitation · التصريح · Making explicit in the translation what is only implied in the source; the opposite is implicitation. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Generalization
chunks.text: Generalization · التعميم · Translating a term with a more general one, such as chair and seat both as كُرْسِيّ. The opposite is particularization. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Gisting
chunks.text: Gisting · الترجمة الإجمالية · A rough outline translation that shows what a text is about, often to decide whether a full translation is worth commissioning. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Hyperbole
chunks.text: Hyperbole · المبالغة · Exaggeration for emphasis or rhetorical effect. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Superordinate (hyperonym)
chunks.text: Superordinate (hyperonym) اللفظ العامّ · A word whose meaning is broader and includes another’s: flower is the superordinate of rose. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Interlinear translation
chunks.text: Interlinear translation · الترجمة بين السطور · An almost morpheme-for-morpheme rendering printed with the source; with grammatical notes it is called a gloss. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intertextuality
chunks.text: Intertextuality · التناص · The way texts link to other texts, through allusion, imitation or a shared genre. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intralingual translation
chunks.text: Intralingual translation · الترجمة داخل اللغة · Translation within one language, often paraphrase (Jakobson’s ‘rewording’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Interlingual translation
chunks.text: Interlingual translation · الترجمة بين اللغات · Translation between two languages or varieties (Jakobson’s ‘translation proper’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intersemiotic translation
chunks.text: Intersemiotic translation · الترجمة بين أنظمة العلامات · Translation between sign systems, such as words into film or music, or a red light ‘meaning’ stop. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Inversion
chunks.text: Inversion · التقديم والتأخير · Moving a word or phrase to a new position in the sentence, usually for target-language style. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Jargon
chunks.text: Jargon · لغة الاختصاص · The specialized vocabulary of a profession, differing from the standard language only in its terms. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Lexicalized metaphor
chunks.text: Lexicalized metaphor · الاستعارة المعجمية · A metaphor so settled that dictionaries list it, such as the grim reaper. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Litotes
chunks.text: Litotes · التلطيف بالنفي · Understatement that denies the opposite for emphasis: ‘She’s not the cleverest person I ever met.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Metonymy
chunks.text: Metonymy · المجاز المرسل / الكناية · Using one word for another it suggests: ‘a man of the cloth’ for a priest; أَهْل البَيْت for the Prophet’s family. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Modal verb
chunks.text: Modal verb · الفعل الناقص للجهة · A verb expressing possibility, necessity or obligation: will, must, shall, should, can, may, might. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Mood
chunks.text: Mood · صيغة الفعل · A category of the verb: indicative (statements), imperative (commands), subjunctive (doubt, supposition). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Onomatopoeia
chunks.text: Onomatopoeia · المحاكاة الصوتية · Words that imitate natural sounds. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Oxymoron
chunks.text: Oxymoron · الجمع بين المتناقضين · A seeming paradox made by joining contradictory words, such as ‘the honest thief’. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Pattern repetition
chunks.text: Pattern repetition · تكرار الأوزان · Repeating Arabic word patterns for rhetorical effect: التَّطْبِيل والتَّزْمِير. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Pleonasm
chunks.text: Pleonasm · الحشو · Using superfluous or redundant words. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Reflected meaning
chunks.text: Reflected meaning · المعنى المنعكس · When one sense of a polysemous word colours how its other senses are understood. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Reinforcement
chunks.text: Reinforcement · التعزيز · Adding a target-language item that strengthens a source item: ‘among the group’, مِنْ ضِمْنِ الفِرْقة. The opposite is condensation. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Theme and rheme
chunks.text: Theme and rheme · المبتدأ والخبر (الموضوع والمحمول) The theme is what a clause is about, usually placed first; the rheme is what is said about it (also topic and comment). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Root repetition
chunks.text: Root repetition · الجناس الاشتقاقي · Arabic device of placing words from the same root close together: تخليص الإبريز في تلخيص باريز. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Semantic repetition
chunks.text: Semantic repetition · الترادف التوكيدي · Using near-synonyms together, common in Arabic (المَحْل والمَجاعة والمَسْغَبة), but in English mostly kept to fixed pairs like ‘last will and testament’. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Slang
chunks.text: Slang · اللغة العامية الدارجة · A variety differing from the standard in grammar and vocabulary, used by one section of a speech community. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Social meaning
chunks.text: Social meaning · المعنى الاجتماعي · What words show about relationships and roles, such as the Arabic plural ‘you’ used as a mark of respect. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Sociolect
chunks.text: Sociolect · اللهجة الاجتماعية · The variety shared by a social group, such as ‘the Queen’s English’. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Stative verb
chunks.text: Stative verb · فعل الحالة · A verb that names a state, such as know or remain, and is not normally used in progressive forms. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Tautology
chunks.text: Tautology · تحصيل الحاصل · Repeating the same idea in different words. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Text function
chunks.text: Text function · وظيفة النص · What a text is for (to sell, instruct, inform); it should be specified when a translation is commissioned. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Thematic meaning
chunks.text: Thematic meaning · المعنى الموضوعاتي · Meaning that comes from the order in which information is presented. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Translation loss
chunks.text: Translation loss · الفقد في الترجمة · Anything of the source that does not survive in the translation, at grammatical, semantic, cultural or intertextual level. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Translation by omission
chunks.text: Translation by omission · الترجمة بالحذف · Leaving source elements out of the translation; also called concentration or economy. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Translation by addition
chunks.text: Translation by addition · الترجمة بالإضافة · Including elements not in the source; also called dissolution or amplification. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Anuvad
chunks.text: Anuvad · أنوفاد · The Sanskrit word for translation, still used in modern Indian languages: ‘saying after’, a temporal image rather than the spatial ‘carrying across’ (Trivedi). Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Invariant core
chunks.text: Invariant core · النواة الثابتة · What all translations of a work have in common: its stable semantic elements, as opposed to the variants of expression (Popovič). Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Semiotic transformation
chunks.text: Semiotic transformation · التحويل السيميائي · Replacing the signs of a message with signs of another code while keeping its invariant information (Ludskanov). Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Linguistic untranslatability
chunks.text: Linguistic untranslatability · استحالة الترجمة اللغوية · When the target language has no lexical or syntactic substitute for a source item; usually solved by restructuring (Catford). Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Cultural untranslatability
chunks.text: Cultural untranslatability · استحالة الترجمة الثقافية · When the target culture lacks a feature of the source situation, such as a Finnish or Japanese ‘bathroom’ (Catford). Bassnett argues it is present in every translation. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Loss and gain
chunks.text: Loss and gain · الفقد والكسب · Some meaning is always lost in translation, but a translator can also enrich or clarify a text. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Metaphrase
chunks.text: Metaphrase · الترجمة الحرفية (درايدن) Dryden’s term for turning an author word by word and line by line. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Paraphrase (Dryden)
chunks.text: Paraphrase (Dryden) الترجمة بتصرف · Dryden’s ‘translation with latitude’, sense for sense: his preferred middle way. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Imitation (Dryden)
chunks.text: Imitation (Dryden) المحاكاة · Dryden’s term for a translation that departs from the original as the translator sees fit. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Sense-for-sense translation
chunks.text: Sense-for-sense translation · الترجمة بالمعنى · Rendering meaning rather than words: Cicero and Horace’s non verbum de verbo, followed by St Jerome. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Vertical and horizontal translation
chunks.text: Vertical and horizontal translation · الترجمة الرأسية والأفقية · Translation from a prestige language such as Latin into the vernacular (vertical) versus between languages of equal standing (horizontal) (Folena). Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Visibility
chunks.text: Visibility · ظهور المترجم · Venuti’s term: fluent translation hides the translator, while foreignizing translation makes their work visible. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Rewriting
chunks.text: Rewriting · إعادة الكتابة · Lefevere’s view of translation, alongside criticism, anthologies and adaptation, as one of the ways most readers meet literature. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Cultural turn
chunks.text: Cultural turn · المنعطف الثقافي · Bassnett and Lefevere’s 1990 shift of attention to the context, history and conventions surrounding translation. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Polysystem theory
chunks.text: Polysystem theory · نظرية الأنظمة المتعددة · Even-Zohar’s idea that cultures translate according to need: young or unsettled literatures translate more, established ones less. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Ostranenie (making strange)
chunks.text: Ostranenie (making strange) التغريب الأسلوبي · The Russian Formalist device of deliberately ‘thickening’ language to sharpen perception. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Translation unit
chunks.text: Translation unit · وحدة الترجمة · The stretch of text a translator works with at one time; the whole text is the prime unit. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Performability
chunks.text: Performability · قابلية الأداء · In theatre translation, keeping the rhythms and ‘gestural text’ an actor needs, not just the words. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Minimax
chunks.text: Minimax · مبدأ الحد الأدنى والأقصى · Levý’s principle that translators choose the solution giving the most effect for the least effort. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Pure language
chunks.text: Pure language · اللغة الخالصة · Benjamin’s idea that translation brings out a hidden language that echoes the original. Bassnett (2014)

chunks.title: Common Law
chunks.text: Common Law · القانون العام (الأنجلوسكسوني) A legal system built from judges’ decisions and precedent (England, the USA, Canada, Australia; Oman’s system has roots in it). Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Civil Law
chunks.text: Civil Law · القانون المدني (اللاتيني) A legal system based on codified statutes, rooted in Roman law (continental Europe; Algeria, Morocco, Syria and Tunisia alongside Islamic law). Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Court of Cassation
chunks.text: Court of Cassation · محكمة التمييز / النقض / التعقيب · The highest court in several Arab states (a French calque): Kuwait, Jordan and the UAE say التمييز, Egypt and Syria النقض, Tunisia التعقيب. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Court of First Instance
chunks.text: Court of First Instance · المحكمة الابتدائية · The court that first hears a case; Jordan says محكمة البداية, Lebanon محكمة الدرجة الأولى. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Power of attorney
chunks.text: Power of attorney · سَنَد التوكيل · A document authorizing someone (an attorney-in-fact, وكيل) to act for another. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Notary public
chunks.text: Notary public · كاتب العدل · An official who certifies documents; in the Maghreb a عَدْل does similar work. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Affidavit
chunks.text: Affidavit · إقرار مشفوع باليمين · A written statement sworn to be true; a declarative legal text. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Prescriptive legal text
chunks.text: Prescriptive legal text · النص القانوني المُلزِم · A text that imposes obligations with sanctions: constitutions, treaties, laws, contracts. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Metalegal text
chunks.text: Metalegal text · النص الواصف للقانون · A text about the law (textbooks, articles) that is not itself a legal instrument. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Doublet (legal)
chunks.text: Doublet (legal) الثنائيات القانونية · A fixed legal pair of near-synonyms (null and void; terms and conditions), usually one word in Arabic (باطل; شروط). Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Shall (legal)
chunks.text: Shall (legal) صيغة الإلزام · In legal English, an obligation (like must), never a future; Arabic often uses a plain imperfect. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Performative do
chunks.text: Performative do · فعل الأداء · The non-emphatic ‘do’ of legal English (‘We the People … do ordain’); not translated into Arabic. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Recognized translation
chunks.text: Recognized translation · الترجمة المعتمدة · An official translation that later texts must follow, such as Oman’s ‘Ministry of Legal Affairs’ for وزارة الشؤون القانونية. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Whereas clause
chunks.text: Whereas clause · «لمّا كان» A preamble clause giving the grounds for a legal act; Arabic opens each with لمّا كان / ولمّا كان. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: In compliance with
chunks.text: In compliance with · عملاً بـ · The usual Arabic rendering of this legal phrase, not any of the dictionary verbs for ‘comply’. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Waqf / habs
chunks.text: Waqf / habs · وقف / حبس · A religious endowment: وقف in the Mashriq, حبس in North Africa; often borrowed as waqf. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Idda
chunks.text: Idda · العِدّة · The legally prescribed waiting period before a woman may remarry; paraphrased or borrowed in translation. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Mahr
chunks.text: Mahr · المَهْر · The dowry paid to the bride in an Islamic marriage contract. Husni & Newman (2015), ch. 3

chunks.title: Action verb
chunks.text: Action verb · فعل حركي · A verb that names an activity, such as walk, read or look. Opposite: stative verb. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Adjunct
chunks.text: Adjunct · مُلحَق ظرفي · An optional adverbial that adds information, such as always or carefully. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Adverbial phrase
chunks.text: Adverbial phrase · شبه جملة ظرفية · A group of words doing the work of an adverb, such as with a knife or tomorrow morning. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Affective meaning
chunks.text: Affective meaning · المعنى الانفعالي · The feelings or attitude a speaker shows (affection, disapproval), or the effect an utterance has on the listener. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Agent
chunks.text: Agent · الفاعل الحقيقي · In a passive sentence, who or what made the action happen (John in ‘The dinner was prepared by John’). Classical Arabic does not state it. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Alliteration
chunks.text: Alliteration · الجناس الاستهلالي · Repeating the same sound at the start of several words in a row. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Allusive meaning
chunks.text: Allusive meaning · المعنى الإلماحي · Meaning a word calls up by echoing another text or tradition, such as المُخَضْرَمون. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Anaphora
chunks.text: Anaphora · التكرار الاستهلالي / الإحالة · Repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive clauses or lines for effect (rhetorical anaphora); also pronouns referring back to earlier words (grammatical anaphora). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Antithesis
chunks.text: Antithesis · الطباق والمقابلة · A contrast of ideas or words set in a balanced, parallel construction. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Antonym
chunks.text: Antonym · الضدّ · A word with the opposite meaning, such as night and day. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Apposition
chunks.text: Apposition · البدل · A noun phrase placed after another to describe it, with no linking word: ‘This jacket, a hand-me-down, …’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Archaism
chunks.text: Archaism · اللفظ المهجور · An old or obsolete word or form; in legal English, aforesaid, heretofore, witnesseth. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Associative meaning
chunks.text: Associative meaning · المعنى الترابطي · Expectations attached to a referent, as when people assume a nurse is a woman. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Assonance
chunks.text: Assonance · السجع الصوتي · Repeating the same vowel sounds in words close together: ‘Thy kingdom come, thy will be done.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Asyndeton
chunks.text: Asyndeton · حذف أدوات العطف · Leaving out conjunctions between coordinated words, phrases or clauses. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Attitudinal meaning
chunks.text: Attitudinal meaning · المعنى الموقفي · The speaker’s attitude to the referent, shown through word choice (for example derogatory terms). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Causative verb
chunks.text: Causative verb · فعل سببي · A transitive verb that makes something happen, such as raise or persuade; Arabic often uses جَعَلَ. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Code-switching
chunks.text: Code-switching · التناوب اللغوي · Moving between two or more languages within the same stretch of speech or text. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Coherence
chunks.text: Coherence · الاتساق الدلالي · The thematic consistency that makes a text a connected whole rather than a string of unrelated sentences. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Cohesion
chunks.text: Cohesion · الترابط النصي · The links between parts of a text made by devices such as conjunctions, pronouns and repetition. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Collocative meaning
chunks.text: Collocative meaning · المعنى التلازمي · Meaning a word takes from the words it regularly appears with. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Communicative translation
chunks.text: Communicative translation · الترجمة التواصلية · Translation close to free translation, rendering source expressions with the culturally appropriate equivalents for the situation. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Concord
chunks.text: Concord · المطابقة · Agreement between the subject and the form of the verb, in number (and in Arabic in gender). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Copula
chunks.text: Copula · الفعل الرابط · A linking verb such as be, seem, become or remain, followed by an adjective, not an adverb (‘This is nice’, not ‘nicely’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Cultural transposition
chunks.text: Cultural transposition · النقل الثقافي · Replacing source culture-specific items with target ones: أَثْلَجَ قُلُوبَنا, ‘our hearts have been warmed’; Romeo and Juliet, قيس وليلى. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Ellipsis
chunks.text: Ellipsis · الحذف · Leaving out a word the reader can supply, such as a repeated subject: ‘He bought the ice-cream and (he) gave it to us.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Euphemism
chunks.text: Euphemism · التلطيف · Replacing a harsh or offensive expression with a milder one, as when ‘Piss off!’ becomes إمشي (‘Go!’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Exegetic translation
chunks.text: Exegetic translation · الترجمة التفسيرية · Translation that adds information not in the source to explain concepts to the target reader. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Explicitation
chunks.text: Explicitation · التصريح · Making explicit in the translation what is only implied in the source; the opposite is implicitation. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Generalization
chunks.text: Generalization · التعميم · Translating a term with a more general one, such as chair and seat both as كُرْسِيّ. The opposite is particularization. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Gisting
chunks.text: Gisting · الترجمة الإجمالية · A rough outline translation that shows what a text is about, often to decide whether a full translation is worth commissioning. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Hyperbole
chunks.text: Hyperbole · المبالغة · Exaggeration for emphasis or rhetorical effect. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Superordinate (hyperonym)
chunks.text: Superordinate (hyperonym) اللفظ العامّ · A word whose meaning is broader and includes another’s: flower is the superordinate of rose. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Interlinear translation
chunks.text: Interlinear translation · الترجمة بين السطور · An almost morpheme-for-morpheme rendering printed with the source; with grammatical notes it is called a gloss. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intertextuality
chunks.text: Intertextuality · التناص · The way texts link to other texts, through allusion, imitation or a shared genre. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intralingual translation
chunks.text: Intralingual translation · الترجمة داخل اللغة · Translation within one language, often paraphrase (Jakobson’s ‘rewording’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Interlingual translation
chunks.text: Interlingual translation · الترجمة بين اللغات · Translation between two languages or varieties (Jakobson’s ‘translation proper’). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Intersemiotic translation
chunks.text: Intersemiotic translation · الترجمة بين أنظمة العلامات · Translation between sign systems, such as words into film or music, or a red light ‘meaning’ stop. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.text: Inversion · التقديم والتأخير · Moving a word or phrase to a new position in the sentence, usually for target-language style. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Jargon
chunks.text: Jargon · لغة الاختصاص · The specialized vocabulary of a profession, differing from the standard language only in its terms. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Lexicalized metaphor
chunks.text: Lexicalized metaphor · الاستعارة المعجمية · A metaphor so settled that dictionaries list it, such as the grim reaper. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Litotes
chunks.text: Litotes · التلطيف بالنفي · Understatement that denies the opposite for emphasis: ‘She’s not the cleverest person I ever met.’ · Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Metonymy
chunks.text: Metonymy · المجاز المرسل / الكناية · Using one word for another it suggests: ‘a man of the cloth’ for a priest; أَهْل البَيْت for the Prophet’s family. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.text: Mood · صيغة الفعل · A category of the verb: indicative (statements), imperative (commands), subjunctive (doubt, supposition). Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.text: Onomatopoeia · المحاكاة الصوتية · Words that imitate natural sounds. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Oxymoron
chunks.text: Oxymoron · الجمع بين المتناقضين · A seeming paradox made by joining contradictory words, such as ‘the honest thief’. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary

chunks.title: Pattern repetition
chunks.text: Pattern repetition · تكرار الأوزان · Repeating Arabic word patterns for rhetorical effect: التَّطْبِيل والتَّزْمِير. Husni & Newman (2015), Glossary
