This is the one that can be true or false, and when a translation is called inaccurate, it is usually this. Expressive — the speaker's attitude. Complain and whine point at the same act; only one of them judges it. Cannot be true or false, and is lost silently.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Presupposed — what the word expects around it. Two kinds: selectional (studious needs a human subject) and collocational, which is arbitrary — in English laws are broken, in Arabic they are contradicted. Evoked — what dialect and register the word belongs to. Register varies by field (what is happening), tenor (who is speaking to whom) and mode (speech, writing, screen). list · Two problems you will meet this week · Frequency. A perfect equivalent can still be the wrong word. Arabic شبر is exactly a span — an obsolete English measure almost no reader knows. Correct and useless. Ambiguity. Dictionary entries run to pages. خط is line, path, track or font, and when the surrounding text does not settle it, nothing else will. Same propositional meaning, different expressive meaning · English · Don't complain. Don't whine. What they share · Both point at the same act, so neither is truer than the other — the propositional meaning is identical · What only one has · لا تشتكِ لا تتذمّر · Whine carries the speaker's judgement that the complaining is irritating; complain carries none. Expressive meaning cannot be true or false, which is exactly why it disappears from a translation without anyone noticing it has gone. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take five words from a text you are working on and, for each, write down its propositional meaning and then anything expressive, presupposed or evoked riding along with it.Then translate them. You will find that two or three of the five cannot carry all four kinds across at once, and that you had to choose which to keep. Write down which you chose. That note is what a translation commentary is made of. Word-level strategies · استراتيجيات مستوى الكلمة · Four named moves for when there is no equivalent — and when each one is the right call. lede · When the word is not there in the target language, you do not improvise: you choose from a small set of known moves, and you can say afterwards which one you used. These are Baker's, and they have names for the same reason the surgical instruments do. card · 1 · A more general word · Also called generalisation, and the most common answer to a gap in propositional meaning. You climb one step up the semantic hierarchy and take the wider term.It works across almost any pair of languages, because the hierarchies themselves are not language-specific — every language has a word for the category above. card · 2 · Substitution · Replace a culture-specific item with a target-language item that does not mean the same thing but lands the same way on the reader. You are trading propositional accuracy for effect, knowingly.Most common with measurements, currency and time. Arabic tells time with thirds of an hour and with ليلاً and فجراً; English does neither, and converting is usually right. card · 3 · Loan word, with or without explanation

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Also called retention or transliteration: carry the source word across in the target script. Standard for culture-specific items, new concepts and technical terms with no settled equivalent.Gloss it the first time and then use it bare. English took alcohol, algebra and algorithm from Arabic this way centuries ago, and hijab recently. card · 4 · Paraphrase · Say what the word means, when no single word will do it. An umbrella for several moves — by a related word, by unrelated words, by a short definition.The cost is length and the loss of any expressive charge the original had. It is the safest strategy and rarely the most elegant one. card · How to choose · Ask what the word is doing in this text. A technical term in a manual wants the loan word and one gloss. A cultural reference in a novel usually wants substitution or paraphrase. A passing mention nobody will remember wants generalisation and no fuss.What you may not do is choose silently. Naming the move is what lets you defend it — and what the commentary in your later courses is assessed on. The loan word, proved by history · Arabic · الكحول الجبر الخوارزمية · Paraphrased instead · a distilled spirit, the reuniting of broken parts, a step-by-step procedure — all accurate, and none of them survived · Borrowed · alcohol algebra algorithm · English took all three from Arabic as loan words, and more recently hijab and jihad. Borrowing is not a failure to translate: for a concept the target language does not yet have, it is often the only move that lets the concept itself arrive. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take four culture-specific items from Kuwaiti life — food, dress, an institution, an occasion. Translate each one four times, once by each strategy.Then decide, for each, which you would actually use and in what kind of text. Sixteen renderings, four decisions, and a reason for each: that is the exercise, and it is also the job. Collocation · التلازم اللفظي · Words keep company. Which company is arbitrary, and it is not the same company in Arabic. lede · Words almost never occur alone, and they are not strung together at random. Some of what governs the stringing is rule — a determiner cannot follow its noun, so beautiful house the is simply wrong. The rest is habit, and habit is where translation goes wrong. card · Why builders do not produce buildings · Authors invent stories and plots, but they do not invent novels. Builders do not produce buildings. No dictionary definition forbids either.Bolinger and Sears gave the only honest reason: we don't say it because we don't say it. That is a collocation — the tendency of certain words to co-occur, semantically arbitrary and not derivable from meaning. list · Near-synonyms do not share company · This is why a thesaurus is dangerous. Each of these is idiomatic on the left and wrong on the right: Break rules — but not break regulations. Waste time — but not squander time. Pay a visit — but not perform a visit. And in Arabic, laws are not broken at all: they are contradicted — يخالف القانون. card · Collocational range

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Every word tolerates a certain spread of company. Shrug has almost none — it takes shoulders and little else. Run has an enormous one: a company, a business, a show, a car, a nose.Two things widen the range. Generality: bury takes people, treasure, a head, a face, feelings, memories, while its hyponym entomb takes only people. And number of senses: each sense of a word attracts its own set of companions. card · What this means at the desk · You do not translate the word. You translate the collocation, and you choose the target equivalent that fits the whole unit.A verb with a wide range in English will not have one wide-ranging counterpart in Arabic. It will have several, and picking between them is the work. One English verb, four Arabic verbs · English · deliver a letter deliver a speech deliver news deliver a blow · One verb, held · deliver looks like a single word with a single equivalent. It is not. What Arabic requires · يسلّم خطاباً يلقي خطبةً ينقل أخباراً يوجّه ضربةً. Four different verbs, because Arabic has no verb with deliver's collocational range. Now try deliver a verdict yourself — and notice that you reached for the collocation, not the dictionary. Do this before the next unit · Take one high-range English verb — run, hold, make, take — and collect eight of its collocations from real text.Translate all eight. Count how many distinct Arabic verbs you needed. That number is the gap between a word and a collocation, and it is why a bilingual dictionary alone cannot do this work. Idioms and fixed expressions · التعابير الاصطلاحية

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Frozen, often opaque, and the place a confident translator does the most damage. lede · Collocations are flexible: deliver a letter, delivery of a letter, a letter has been delivered are all fine. Idioms and fixed expressions sit at the far end of that scale — frozen in form, and often opaque in meaning. list · What you may not do to an idiom · The long and the short of it means the basic facts. Touch it anywhere and it breaks: Reorder it — not the short and the long of it. Delete from it — not spill beans. Add to it — not face the classical music. Swap a word — not the tall and the short of it, not bury a hatchet. Change its grammar — not the music was faced. split · Idiom or fixed expression? Idiom · تعبير اصطلاحي · Frozen and opaque. Bury the hatchet, pull a fast one, fill the bill. You cannot reach the meaning from the words. Fixed expression · تعبير ثابت · Frozen but usually transparent. As a matter of fact, ladies and gentlemen, all the best, and proverbs like practice what you preach. Still taken as one unit. list · How to notice one before you mistranslate it · The first difficulty is not translating the idiom. It is realising there is one. Three signals: It violates truth conditions — it is raining cats and dogs, food for thought. It is ill-formed — by and large, the world and his wife, trip the light fantastic. It opens with like — like a bat out of hell, like two peas in a pod. And the general rule: the less sense an expression makes in its context, the more likely it is an idiom and not a failure of your vocabulary. list · Five strategies

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: In descending order of how much of the original survives: An idiom of similar meaning and similar form. An idiom of similar meaning but dissimilar form — usually the best available. Borrowing the source idiom. Paraphrase — the most common, and the one that loses the flavour. Omission of the whole idiom — legitimate, and the one to be able to justify. card · Why this is the case for translating into your own language. Competence in a foreign language almost never reaches the point where you can feel when an idiom may be bent and when it may not. That sensitivity is a native one, and it is the usual argument for translating into your first language rather than out of it.Even then two problems remain: recognising the idiom, and carrying its meaning across when the target language has no counterpart — because idioms are culturally specific, and even a counterpart that exists may be used in a different register or context. Five idioms to identify before translating · English · I urge you to speak your mind and not to pull any punches. The trap · Word-for-word gives a speech about a mind and an instruction about hitting. Both are grammatical, and both are nonsense. What is meant · أدعوك إلى قول ما تعتقده بصراحة ودون مجاملة · The other four on the slide are driving like a bat out of hell, the world and his wife were there, in a nutshell, and spilled the beans. Identify, then interpret, then translate — always that order. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take the five sentences above. For each: name the idiom, write its meaning in plain English, then translate the sentence into Arabic.Then say which of the five strategies you used, and why. Expect paraphrase most of the time — and notice what the paraphrase costs. Grammatical equivalence · التكافؤ النحوي · Grammar forces you to say things the source never said — and to drop things it did. lede · Vocabulary is not the only thing that shapes what a language can report. Its grammar obliges speakers to mark certain distinctions every time they open their mouths — time, number, gender, person — and every language makes a different selection from that set. card · Why grammar is harder to move than vocabulary. Grammar runs on two dimensions: morphology, the shape of words, and syntax, the order of the parts.A language will absorb a new word overnight. It will not absorb a new grammatical category. So where the two systems differ, the translator cannot borrow — something has to be added to the target text or dropped from it, and that changes the information content. list · The five notions to check · Number. Countability is universal; grammatical number is not. English has singular and plural; Arabic has singular, dual and plural; Chinese marks it lexically or not at all. Gender. English marks it only in the third person. In Arabic the noun's gender also reshapes its verbs and adjectives, so a first-person sentence with no gender in English forces a choice in Arabic.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Person. Participant roles, through a closed set of pronouns. Many European languages add a politeness dimension English does not have. Tense and aspect. Two different things: tense locates the event in time, aspect describes its distribution — finished or not, continuing or momentary. Voice. The relation between verb and subject. Written English uses the passive heavily, and most languages have their own ways of building agentless clauses that do not map onto it. card · The gender problem, in one pair of sentences · I am a student in the English department, and I specialise in Translation Studies. Nothing there tells you the speaker's gender — but Arabic will not let you write the sentence without deciding.Add even though I am a father of four and it is settled. Add even though I was nine months pregnant and it is settled the other way. When the text gives you nothing: read the whole thing for gendered expressions, biological detail, relational nouns (husband, wife) or a title of address. If it still gives you nothing, you are making a decision, and you should know that you are. list · The error your examiner will find first · Literal renderings of am / is / are / was / were into يكون. Arabic does not need the copula: She is kind — not هي تكون طيبة, but هي طيبة. I am leaving now — not أنا أكون مغادراً الآن, but سأغادر الآن. They are put in the same situation — not هم يكونون موضوعين, but يوضعون في الموقف نفسه. The dual, and what English has to add · Arabic · ويختار المحكمان المعيَّنان على هذا النحو المحكَّم الثالث · What English lacks

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: There is no dual in English. The arbitrators alone would lose the count. English, with the addition · and the two arbitrators thus appointed select the third arbitrator. The word two is not in the Arabic. It is carried by the form of المحكمان itself. English has to add a word to say what Arabic says with a suffix — and in an arbitration clause, failing to add it changes the legal meaning. Do this before the next unit · Find an Arabic legal or administrative paragraph containing at least one dual and one passive. Translate it into English.Then mark your own output: every place you added information the Arabic did not state, and every place you dropped information it did. Both lists will be non-empty. That is not a failure — it is what grammatical difference costs, and naming it is the skill. Literary and technical texts · النصوص الأدبية والتقنية · Two kinds of writing that ask for two different kinds of faithfulness. lede · Before the genre units, the distinction they rest on. A literary text is written to convey ideas and to produce a feeling; a ghost story is meant to frighten you. It addresses the mind and the heart at once, and a translation that delivers only the first has failed at the job. list · What literary writing is like · Imaginative, and subjective. Free, less formal, personal — it follows no standard format. Tends to be long, and may be written in first, second or third person. Its genres: prose fiction and non-fiction, novels, novellas, poetry, drama. list · The three hard problems · Each returns in the units after this one:

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Style. In literature the manner is part of the content. Style is what tells one writer from another, so it gets the same attention as meaning — not less. Literal against free. The ideal is to translate everything, no more and no less. No two languages have the same structure, so in practice you will sometimes expand and sometimes condense, and you should know which you are doing. Standard against dialect. A novelist uses dialect on purpose — to place a character geographically, to mark identity, to characterise. Your job is to find how that purpose can survive, not to reproduce the dialect. card · And culture · Every group has its own way of living, eating, dressing and speaking, and the target readers may share none of it. Culture-bound terms are not decoration in a literary text; they are often what the passage is about.The four word-level strategies from unit 5 are the tools here. Which one you reach for depends on whether the item is the subject of the sentence or scenery in it. The same fact, two kinds of text · Technical · Ambient temperature fell to 4 C overnight. Literary · By morning the cold had got into everything. What each one has to keep · The first must keep the number. The second must keep the feeling — and may change the number, or drop it. Both can be faithful. They are faithful to different things, and choosing which kind of faithfulness a text is asking for is the decision this whole course is training. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take one paragraph of a novel and one paragraph of a manual, both in English. Translate both into Arabic.Then write two sentences: what you protected in the first, and what you protected in the second. If the answers are the same, one of the two translations is wrong. Literary translation and style · الترجمة الأدبية والأسلوب · Style is not decoration on top of the meaning. It is a second thing to translate. lede · Style can mean the conventions of a genre — how business or medical writing goes — or it can mean one writer's own way of putting things. In literary translation the second sense is the one that matters: not what the author writes, but the manner of it. The verbal identity of a writer. card · Two definitions worth carrying · Boase-Beier (2006) treats style as the outcome of choice — and argues that the translator's own style will inevitably enter the target text. You do not have the option of not having a style.Baker (2000) calls style a thumb-print expressed in a range of linguistic and non-linguistic features, and insists it is a matter of patterning: recurring habits across a text, not a single striking sentence. list · Where to look for it · Lexical choices · Preferred syntax · How ideas are ordered · Choice of verb tense · Use of metaphor · list · Elements that cause trouble · Each of these carries information about the character or the narrator, which is why flattening it loses more than it looks: Diction, expansive or economical. Tight and efficient, or elaborate and long-winded? When the author switches, ask why. It often marks a character's background.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Vocabulary. Simple or fancy; technical, flowery, colloquial, punning, obscure. It tells the reader what the character's education is without stating it. Sentence structure. A run of short sentences reads as agitation; long ones read as composure. Interruptions and digressions say something about who gets to hold a conversation. Dialogue, tone, figures of speech, allusion and intertextuality. card · The two-sided risk · Stylistic features are language-specific. Following an Arabic word order closely into English produces something unnatural and hard to read — it will be taken as a bad translation, and the fault will be attributed to the author.But ironing the style out entirely gives target readers no sense of how the original reads, which is also a loss. There is no rule that resolves this. There is only the judgement, made consciously, and defended in the commentary. Style as patterning, not a single sentence · English · He waited. The room was cold. Nobody came. Smoothed out · انتظر في غرفة باردة دون أن يأتي أحد — accurate, and the three short sentences have become one composed one · Pattern kept · انتظر. كانت الغرفة باردة. لم يأتِ أحد. Nothing in the first version is wrong. But the clipped rhythm was carrying the character's state, and joining the sentences deletes it without deleting a single word of meaning. That is precisely Baker's point about patterning. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take half a page from a novel you know. Before translating, write five lines on its style using the list above — diction, vocabulary, sentence structure, tone, figures of speech.Then translate, and check your translation against your own five lines. Anywhere they disagree, you changed the author's thumb-print. Decide whether you meant to. Technical translation · الترجمة التقنية · The largest field by volume, and the one where a wrong word has consequences. lede · Almost every technological advance reaches anybody outside the room it was invented in by being translated. Byrne puts it plainly: the inventions that changed ordinary life were accompanied at almost every step by translation in its capacity as a vehicle for disseminating scientific and technical knowledge. card · What counts as technical · Wider than it sounds. The sciences — medicine, physics, astronomy, chemistry. Applied technology — computing, engineering. And subjects nobody calls scientific: geography, economics, architecture.If a field has terms of its own that outsiders use differently or not at all, translating it is technical translation. list · How technical language behaves · It is specialised, and becomes more so over time rather than less. It is economical — it says things in as few linguistic means as it can. It avoids the associations of ordinary language and defines its terms precisely, which is the opposite of what literary language does. card · The same word in three fields

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Depression in psychology is an illness. In economics it is a prolonged contraction. In meteorology it is an area of low pressure.One term, three domains, and a different concept in each. Knowing which field you are in is not background knowledge here — it is the translation. list · Two kinds of lexical trouble · The problems fall neatly into two, and the second is the dangerous one: Terms you do not know at all, because they appear only in technical contexts. Unpleasant, but visible — you know to go and look them up. Terms you do know, from ordinary contexts, being used in a specialised way. You feel no difficulty, translate confidently, and are wrong. Nothing warns you. Two ordinary-looking words in a medical text · English · These tests specify and diagnose the allergenic or harmful substances, as in the case of contact eczema. The ordinary reading · contact read as everyday contact, and allergenic collapsed into allergic — two words that look harmless · The terms · المواد المحسِّسة أو الضارة، كما الحال في أكزيما التماس. Allergic describes the reaction; allergenic describes the substance that causes it. أكزيما التماس is a named condition, not a description. Both are the second kind of trouble: familiar words, specialised use, no warning. Do this before the next unit · Find a short technical paragraph in a field you do not work in. Before translating, list every word you are confident about.Now check five of them in a specialist source. At least one will not mean what you assumed. That word is the whole lesson of this unit — the danger is not the vocabulary you know you lack.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Journalistic texts: the headline · ترجمة العناوين الصحفية · Headlinese is not English. It has its own grammar, and Arabic does not share it. lede · A news text is built from three parts — headline, lead paragraph, news story — and the first of them is written in something that is barely the same language. card · Headlinese · The headline is the most conspicuous thing on a newspaper page, and its difficulty is syntactic, lexical and stylistic at once. The standard description is telegraphic and elliptical: it leaves out everything it can get away with leaving out.English headlines are frequently not complete sentences. Some are nothing but a string of nouns. list · What gets dropped, and what gets used · Articles, the copula, and auxiliaries go first. Simple tenses rather than continuous or perfect ones — US launches air raids in Iraq, not has launched. Noun stacks stand in for whole clauses. Which means the reader is expected to reconstruct the proposition — and so is the translator, before a word is rendered. card · Why the Arabic headline is usually longer · Arabic headlines do not work by the same compression. Rendering an English noun stack word-for-word produces something that is not a headline in Arabic and often not intelligible.So addition is standard practice here, not a liberty: you add what the target reader needs in order to recover what the English reader recovered for free. card · Do this before you translate any headline

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Write out the full proposition in plain English first. Mustang Referral Customer Complaint unpacks to: there is a complaint; the complaint concerns the Mustang customer referral programme.Only then translate. Headlines are the one place where translating before you have paraphrased is almost guaranteed to fail. Four nouns, and what Arabic has to supply · English headline · Mustang Referral Customer Complaint · Word for word · a string of four nouns that names no event and forms no Arabic headline · Arabic, with additions · شكوى زبون فورد موستنج من برنامج الإحالة · Two things were added. Ford, because an Arabic reader may not know Mustang is a Ford. And programme, because referral alone does not say that a scheme is meant. Neither is in the English; both are needed to say the same thing. Do this before the next unit · Take five English headlines from today. For each, write the full proposition in plain English, then translate into Arabic.Underline every word in your Arabic that has no counterpart in the English. Then justify each one in a few words. If you cannot justify it, it is not an addition — it is an invention. Journalistic texts: story structure · بنية الخبر الصحفي · A news story is built to be cut from the bottom. Knowing that changes how you translate it. lede · Beyond the headline, a news story has a shape, and the shape is chosen by the kind of story it is. Three are standard: the inverted pyramid, the hourglass, and straight narrative. card · The inverted pyramid

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: The most basic structure, and older than you would guess: it dates from a time when reporters filed by telegraph and the wire could be cut mid-transmission. Put the most important thing first, and descend from there.It reverses chronological order — the outcome comes first and the background last. list · Why editors like it · The reader gets the important elements at once and can decide whether to continue. An editor can cut from the bottom to fit the space, and lose nothing significant. Online, updates can be added without rebuilding the story. It forces the reporter to rank the elements and write quickly, holding back minor detail. list · What it costs · It gives the reader no reason to reach the end. It discourages well-made endings, and treats the later paragraphs as expendable. It can push the writer towards oversimplifying. card · The hourglass, and narrative · The hourglass is a compromise: the main facts first in descending importance, as in a pyramid, then a turn into chronological narrative with room for detail, dialogue and background. It suits police stories, disasters and trials — anything that has a sequence worth telling.Narrative proper keeps the events in order from the start, and is the structure literary journalism borrows. card · What this means for you

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: The structure is information design, not decoration, and it is a target-language decision as much as a source-language one.Translating a pyramid story faithfully means the Arabic must also survive being cut from the bottom. If your rendering buries the key fact in paragraph three because the Arabic sentence ran better that way, you have translated the words and broken the text. Where the important fact sits · Pyramid lead · Twelve people were rescued yesterday after a fire broke out in a residential tower in Salmiya. Reordered for flow · After a fire broke out in Salmiya, and after crews had worked through the night, twelve people were rescued — natural, and now uncuttable · Pyramid kept · أُنقذ اثنا عشر شخصاً أمس إثر حريق شبّ في برج سكني بالسالمية. Both carry every fact. Only the second can lose its final paragraphs without losing the news. Sentence order in a news translation is not a stylistic preference — it is part of what the text is for. Do this before the next unit · Take an English news story of six or more paragraphs. Identify its structure, then translate it.Now delete your last two paragraphs and read what remains. If it is still a complete, accurate story, you preserved the structure. If something essential has gone, you reorganised the text without noticing. Terminology and translation technology · المصطلحات وتقنيات الترجمة · A discipline about concepts, and the tools that keep decisions from being made twice. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Terminology has no single agreed definition, partly because it borrowed from older fields — semantics, lexicology, lexicography. What forced it into existence is simpler: science and technology produced concepts faster than languages produced words for them. card · Two senses of the word · Originally, terminology meant the technical terms used in an art, a science or a specialised subject — a sense still alive in English.Later it came to mean the study of those terms: the systematic identification of the terms belonging to a field, and of the concepts they stand for. card · The working definition · A discipline that systematically identifies specialised terms in the context where they are used, analyses the concepts they represent in that context, and where necessary creates and standardises terms to meet a real need for expression.It is a linguistic discipline with theoretical guidelines and defined working methods, which is what separates it from collecting vocabulary. list · The three tools · Translation technology is the software around the process. Three things do most of the work: Machine translation. Software translating automatically. Early systems were rule-based, then statistical; neural systems are markedly better. Still not a match for a human on nuance or context — but genuinely faster and cheaper. Translation memory. Stores what you have already translated so it can be reused. Its real value is consistency across a long document or a repeat client, not speed.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Terminology management. Glossaries and termbases, so that a term decided once is used the same way by everyone afterwards. card · The honest position on machines · Machine translation has made real progress and will keep making it. It still cannot match a human on nuance or on sensitivity to context.What follows from that is not that the tools are useless. It is that someone has to be able to tell when the output is wrong — which takes more knowledge than producing it, not less. That is the job the rest of this course is preparing you for. Why a termbase exists · English · informed consent · The near-enough word · موافقة — consent, which is what a patient gives to anything at all · The term · موافقة مستنيرة · These are different things in law: one is agreement, the other is agreement after the risks have been explained and understood. A term decided once, recorded with its source, and reused is the entire argument for terminology management — so that the next translator inherits the decision instead of making it again, differently. Do this before the next unit · Build a ten-term glossary for one field — banking, medicine, aviation, whatever you may translate in. For each: the English term, the Arabic term, a one-line definition, and where you got it.That last column is what makes it a termbase rather than a list. A term without a source is a guess, however confident it sounds. Localisation · الأقلمة · Translation is one part of it. The rest is everything else the product assumes about you. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Localisation is adapting a product, service or piece of content so that it is linguistically and culturally right for a particular market — software, websites, manuals, multimedia, games. card · Locale · The technical term for what you are adapting to. A locale is the set of features of a user's environment that depend on language, country or region, and cultural convention.It settles sort order, keyboard layout, and the formats for date, time, number and currency. None of that is translation, and all of it is wrong if you ignore it. card · Where translation sits · Translation is the linguistic aspect of localisation — a subset of the activities, not the whole of it. Its goal within that process is the same as everywhere else in this course: equivalence of meaning, idiomatic, lexical and conceptual.The rest of localisation is layout that survives right-to-left, images that make sense locally, forms that accept local addresses, and defaults that assume the right things. card · The test · A localised product should not read as a translated one. The user should not be able to tell that it was made somewhere else — which is a higher standard than accuracy, and a different one.It is also the clearest case in the course of a translation being judged by its effect on its reader rather than by its correspondence to its source. The same interface, two locales · English build · Payment due 03/04/2026 $1,250.00 · Translated only · الدفعة مستحقة 03/04/2026 · $1,250.00 — every word rendered, and the date is now ambiguous and the currency foreign · Localised

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: الدفعة مستحقة في ٣ أبريل ٢٠٢٦ ١٬٢٥٠٫٠٠ د.ك · Nothing here is a translation problem. Date order, numeral form, decimal and thousands marks and currency are all locale conventions — and getting them wrong on an invoice is more consequential than any wording choice on the screen. The last one · Take one screen of an app or website you use in English and localise it into Arabic — not just translate it.List everything you had to change that was not a word: direction, alignment, date and number formats, currency, icons, the example names in the form fields. That list is the difference between translation and localisation, and it is the last thing this course has to teach you. 182 · Introduction to Terminology · مقدمة في علم المصطلحات · 142 · A discipline about concepts, which happens to produce words. Not vocabulary learning. Terminology starts from the concept — a thing a field needs to refer to precisely — and asks which term is allowed to stand for it, who decided, and where that decision is written down.Then the practical half: how a termbase or a glossary is built, kept current, and shared, so that the next translator inherits the decision instead of making it again differently. Ministries and courts · Hospitals · Standards bodies · The UN · Any termbase · Precision, and a record. A term without a source is a guess, however confident it sounds. glossary · What terminology is · ما علم المصطلح؟ A discipline nobody quite agrees on, and why it had to exist. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: There is no settled agreement on what terminology is, and the reason is historical: it borrowed from older fields — semantics, lexicology, lexicography — and each of them left a different idea of what the subject is for. card · Why it appeared when it did · Two pressures, both recent. Science and technology pushed the frontier back in genetics, space, information science, telecommunications — and every new concept needs a name.And contact between language communities. The need for terms is real in one language; it multiplies when two or more are in contact, because for every concept named in one, an equivalent has to be found in the others. list · Why practitioners disagree · The disagreement is not academic point-scoring. Each position produces a different kind of work: Those who fear that a flood of new terms will impede communication see terminology as a means of standardising. Many linguists and lexicologists treat it as technical lexicography and nothing more. Some schools set out to produce exhaustive word lists — without defining the terms or classifying the concepts. split · The word has two meanings, and they are not the same size · The terms themselves · المصطلحات · The technical terms and expressions used in an art, a science or a specialised subject. Still the ordinary English sense. The study of them · علم المصطلح · The systematic research and identification of the terms specific to a subject field, and of the concepts they represent. The sense this course means. card · The definition to know

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: A discipline aimed at systematically identifying specialised terms in the context in which they are used, analysing the concepts they represent in that context, and creating and standardising terms, if need be, to meet the user's need for means of expression.It is a linguistic discipline with theoretical guidelines and defined work methods. That is what separates it from collecting vocabulary. list · The four work methods · The whole course is these four, taken in turn: Term identification — finding the terms peculiar to a field: simple, complex and phrasal. Contextual analysis — determining each term's meaning from the context it sits in. Term creation — filling a genuine gap, and only after every source has been searched. Standardisation — settling which term may carry the concept, and recording it. The order matters: identify before you create · The temptation · No Arabic term comes to mind, so coin one. What the discipline says · The terminologist's role is first and foremost to identify existing terms, not to invent new ones. When coining is warranted · Only when every available source has been researched and the evidence shows no term exists in the target language for that concept. This is the single most common error a beginner makes, and it is expensive: a coined term that duplicates an existing one splits the field's usage in two, and both halves then have to be reconciled by somebody later. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Pick a field you know a little — banking, aviation, nursing. Write down ten of its terms in English.Now mark each one: is it a term peculiar to that field, or a general-language word you have assumed belongs to it? Most people find three or four of the ten are general words. Those four are not terminology, and knowing the difference is where this subject starts. Specialized terms and the user · المصطلحات المتخصصة والمستفيد · Who the work is for, and why context decides everything. lede · Almost every field of human endeavour has its own special language — the arts, science, business, economics, law, medicine. The lexicon of a special language holds both general-language words and terms with special reference, and terminology is concerned only with the second. split · Two kinds of context, two levels of difficulty · Situational · السياق الموقفي · The term is connected to the concrete thing it refers to. You can see the object. The meaning becomes clear. Written · السياق النصي · Nothing to point at. You analyse the context, identify the semantic features it contains, and build the concept from those. card · Why this matters most in two languages · In bilingual and multilingual work you must find enough information on the source term's meaning in context to go and research its target-language equivalent in context.Equivalence of semantic features across the two contexts is called textual correspondence, and it is what establishes that two terms are equivalent. Not a dictionary line: matching features in matching contexts. card · The user decides the job

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Terminologists work to the user's communication needs, and those vary enormously — an advertiser's needs are not a scientist's.But every user, whoever they are and whatever language they speak, arrives with the same question: what is this called, or what do I call this? Everything else is method. list · Where the findings go · Research has to end somewhere it can be used and changed: Records, once on paper and now in computerized databases. Multiple access to the same information without reproducing it, huge capacity, very fast retrieval. Vocabularies — for a wide audience or users unfamiliar with terminological method. Alphabetical: source entry, target equivalents, a concise definition, the subfield. Glossaries — an alphabetical list of terms specific to a discipline with their target-language equivalents. Why usage, not correctness, is the test · The rule · Terminologists must be aware of current usage. What happens if they are not · Their work would serve no purpose were they to give the user depreciated or rare terminology. How usage is established · By researching terms in context — not by preference, authority, or what the dictionary printed twenty years ago. A term that is defensible and unused is a failure. This is the point where terminology parts company with prescriptive grammar: the question is never what people ought to say, but what the field actually says now. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take one English term from a specialised field and find it in three different written contexts — not three dictionaries, three real texts.For each, list the semantic features the context supplies. Then compare your three lists. Where they agree you have the concept; where they differ you have either a second sense or a sloppy source, and telling those apart is the work. Semantics and lexicography · علم الدلالة وصناعة المعجم · The two disciplines terminology is mistaken for, and the direction that separates them. lede · Terminology is regularly confused with the other disciplines that deal with the lexicon. It is worth being able to say exactly how it differs, because the difference is not a matter of degree — it is a matter of which end you start from. card · What the semanticist does · Semantics studies the relationship between the linguistic sign and the object it refers to — why a chair is called a chair. Two approaches:Diachronic, the historical one: fish from Old English fisc and Old Frisian fisk, and then how that first meaning branched — the flesh of the fish, a piece of hard wood strengthening a ship's mast, a cold person.Synchronic, the descriptive one: meanings as a system, where one meaning can have several signs and one sign several meanings, and the dates are irrelevant because old and new survive side by side as polysemy. card · What the terminologist does with the same word

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Begins with the context, not the etymology. Researching in biology, the terminologist establishes that a cold-blooded aquatic vertebrate with gills is called a fish.That the word means other things in other fields is interesting and not the point. The semanticist wants the whole semantic range; the terminologist wants the features that fix one label to one concept in one field. split · And the direction of travel · The lexicographer · صانع المعجم · Starts from the sign and investigates the concept or concepts it represents. Researches the entire lexicon. The reader is decoding — they met a word and need its meaning. The terminologist · أخصائي المصطلح · Starts from the concept and researches its sign. Researches only the stock specific to a field. The user is encoding — they have a meaning and need the word for it. list · Three places that difference shows · Nomenclature. The lexicographer takes every word and every meaning in every situation. The terminologist takes the terms of one subject within a stated framework — and takes all its means of expression: simple, complex and phrasal. Analysis. Lexicographical analysis builds a word's complete semantic profile. Terminological analysis determines the characteristics of one concept, so the term can be linked to it and an equivalent found in another language. Definition. A lexicographer's definition covers all accepted uses. A terminologist's condenses the semantic features of the term as used in one real situation. One word, two disciplines, two right answers · The word · fish · The semanticist's answer

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Every meaning it has carried — the animal, the flesh, the mast timber, the cold person — literal and figurative, concrete and abstract, together making its semantic range in modern English. The terminologist's answer, in biology · سمكة — a cold-blooded aquatic vertebrate with gills. The rest exists and is not the question being asked. Neither is wrong. They are answers to different questions, and a translator who reaches for the wrong one brings back either far too much or the wrong sense entirely. Do this before the next unit · Take a polysemous English word that also works as a term — cell, bond, charge, current.Write the lexicographer's entry: every sense you can find. Then pick one field and write the terminologist's: the single concept, its features, and the Arabic term for it. Notice that the second is shorter and much harder. Term and concept · المصطلح والمفهوم · What counts as a term, and what makes a concept that term's own. lede · Terminological inquiry has to make the relation between a term and its concept explicit — between the signifier, a word in the language, and the signified, the object in the world. They are joined through the concept in the mind, and it is the concept that terminology works on. list · Three shapes a term can take · A term designates a concept specific to a subject field. The examples below are all from television production: Simple — one word: a stem with or without affixes. To coproduce, commentator, monochrome. Still simple though they hold several morphemes, because co-, -ator and mono- cannot stand alone as terms.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Complex — two or more words in a grammatical relationship: captive audience, laughmeter, director-producer, closeup, ultrawide-angle lens, to lip sync. Phrasal — a group of words with a higher syntactic function: request for copyright clearance, to preempt a program, filmed on location, on the air. card · One concept, whatever the shape · All three represent a single concept in the field. That is the test, not the word count.And it has a consequence: remove any one element of a complex term and the concept changes. Ultrawide-angle lens is not a long way of saying lens. card · Essential characteristics · A concept is described by the sum of its essential characteristics. Take watch: having a face and hands, being used to tell time, having a movement driven in one of several ways.All true — and not enough, because they do not separate a watch from every other timepiece. Add designed to be worn on a wristband, pin or chain and now they do. The characteristics that are both necessary and sufficient to distinguish a concept from all others are its essential characteristics. They need not come in any particular order. card · A term belongs to its field, not to the language. General-language words are constantly borrowed by disciplines to name new concepts. Their meaning is broadened, narrowed or otherwise changed — they take on a new semantic load.Furniture in the urban-planning term street furniture does not mean what it means at home. Highway in information highway is not a road. Investigate the term in the field it belongs to, or you will translate the wrong concept confidently.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Borrowed word, new semantic load · English term · street furniture · The general-language reading · أثاث الشارع — furniture, outdoors. Grammatical, and not what an urban planner means. The concept · عناصر تأثيث الشارع — benches, bollards, lamp posts, shelters: the fixed public fittings of a street. The English word was borrowed from the general language and given a new load. The Arabic has to carry the concept, not the borrowed word — which is why the equivalent is longer and why the literal version tells the reader nothing. Do this before the next unit · Find five terms in one field and sort them: simple, complex, phrasal.Then take the complex ones and delete one element from each. Write what the remainder now means. In every case it should be a different concept, not a vaguer version of the same one — if it is only vaguer, what you had was probably not a term. Subject-field research · البحث في مجال متخصص · The long kind: exhaustive, systematic, and six stages before you extract a single term. lede · Research carried out on the terms and concepts of a whole subject is subject-field research. It is relatively exhaustive, runs over a long period, and therefore demands a thorough and systematic approach — most of which happens before any term is written down. list · Six stages, all preliminary · Every one of these is completed before scanning for and extracting terms begins: Determining the research objectives · Estimating the necessary resources · Becoming familiar with the subject field · Selecting the documentation · Locating the documentation · Evaluating the documentation

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: card · 1 · Objectives — settled with the client · Three things: purpose, target audience, scope.Purpose varies from filling a total gap to revising and enlarging what exists. Audience runs from layman to specialist — a company manager, a language professional, an enthusiast. And scope follows the need: the basic terminology of a field is a few hundred concepts; the complete terminology of a field or major subfield is a few thousand. list · 2 · Resources — also settled with the client · Three kinds, and the questions to ask about each: Human. How many terminologists? Is there support staff to key in the data? Can one or more subject-field specialists take part? Documentary. Are there original documents — not translations — in both languages? Vocabularies or glossaries in the field or related ones? Bibliographic databases? Does any term bank already hold material on it? Financial. What is required, and is it available? card · Why this front-loading is not bureaucracy · A few hundred concepts and a few thousand are not the same job with a different deadline; they are different jobs. Agreeing the scope after starting means discovering halfway that the work was aimed at the wrong audience, at the wrong depth, from documentation that cannot support it.And the documentary question does the most work: original documents, not translations. Research a term from a translated source and you may be researching the previous translator's guess. The same field, two different assignments · Client A · “We need our staff to understand the basics of Islamic banking in English.” What that is

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: A few hundred concepts. A vocabulary. Audience: non-specialist. Documentation: introductory and regulatory. Client B · “We are drafting contracts and need the complete terminology.” — a few thousand concepts, specialist audience, original contracts and standards as sources. Same subject field, same two languages, and almost nothing else in common. Determining the objective is not a formality before the work — it is the decision that shapes every stage after it. Do this before the next unit · Choose a field and write a one-page research plan through all six stages: purpose, audience, scope in number of concepts, the three resource questions, and a named list of documentation.For the documentation, mark each source original or translated. If more than half your list is translated, the plan is not yet viable — and finding that out now is the point of writing it. Term research · البحث في مصطلح مفرد · The short kind: one term, one client, and often an answer needed today. lede · Research on individual terms or concepts is term research, and it is most of the terminological work done in private organisations and government agencies — answering the questions of everybody from the layman to the expert. card · Why it exists at all · Ideally subject-field research would be done in every field. It would take time and money, both usually scarce — and even with both, it could never keep pace: there would always be new concepts to name, new problems, new users.Term research is what covers the gap, and it is not second-best. It is the form of the work most people actually encounter. list

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Six steps · Discussion with the client · Checking the concept · Consulting a specialist · Researching the solution · Checking the solution · Presenting the solution · card · The best training there is · Clients ask about almost any topic and usually need an answer within four to forty-eight hours. That pressure is the training.You work directly with the user, so you learn what users actually need. You sharpen the habit of assimilating a subject fast. And you come to know your documentation so well that you develop a sense of which source is likely to hold this particular answer — which is a skill no reading list can give you. card · Note the second step · Checking the concept comes before consulting anyone or researching anything.Clients ask for a word. What they have is a concept they cannot name, and it is frequently not the concept their question implies. Establish what they actually mean first, or the following four steps research the wrong thing efficiently. The question asked, and the question meant · The client asks · “What is the English for تعثر?” Answered straight · stumbling, faltering, default — three terms from three fields, offered blind · After checking the concept · It is a loan agreement. The concept is a borrower failing to meet an obligation, so the term is default — and the file says so, with the context it came from. One question to the client turned three guesses into one sourced answer. That question is step two, and skipping it is the most common way a fast answer becomes a wrong one. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Have somebody send you a real term question with no context — just a word and a language pair. Work all six steps, and hold yourself to forty-eight hours.Write down what you asked at step two and what the answer changed. Then present the solution properly: the term, the definition, the context, and the source. An answer without a source is not a solution; it is an opinion delivered promptly. Terminological analysis · التحليل المصطلحي · Where a term begins and ends — and which words around it are actually part of it. lede · Analysis is the centre of subject-field research: identifying the terms of the field and analysing the contexts they appear in. The hard part is not finding candidates. It is deciding how much of the phrase is the term. split · The two parts of a complex term · Determinatum · المُحدَّد · The base word being qualified — advertising in subliminal advertising, editing in film editing. Determinant · المُحدِّد · The element qualifying it — desktop in desktop publishing. Only determinants that fundamentally modify the base are part of the term. card · Essential and inessential, and why the same word can be either. Charitable institution is a term: charitable changes what kind of institution this is. Charitable man is not: charitable merely describes a man.Same determinant, opposite verdicts. Intricate in intricate technology product only says the product is complex. Initial in initial verification technique only says it comes first in a series. Neither changes the concept, so neither belongs to the term. list · Five things to weigh when identifying a unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: The relationship between determinant and determinatum. Degree of lexicalization — how fixed the combination has become. Classification of concepts — where it sits in the field's structure. Collocation — the company it habitually keeps. Typographic indications — italics, capitals, quotation marks, bold: a field flagging its own terms · card · The practical test · Ask whether removing the determinant leaves you with a different concept or the same concept less precisely described.Different concept: the determinant is essential and the term is the whole phrase. Same concept: the determinant is a passing description, the term is the base word alone, and taking the phrase into a glossary would put a sentence fragment there for ever. Same adjective, two verdicts · A term · charitable institution · Not a term · charitable man — charitable describes the man; remove it and you still have the same concept, a man · Why the first is one · مؤسسة خيرية — remove charitable and you have institution, a different concept with a different legal standing. This is the distinction that decides what goes on the record. Put charitable man in a termbase and you have recorded a description; the next terminologist will have to take it out, and will wonder what else in the file is not a term. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Take a specialised page and mark every noun phrase of two or more words. For each, delete the first element and write what remains.Sort them into two piles: different concept and same concept, vaguer. Only the first pile is terminology. Expect the second pile to be larger than you assumed — that over-collection is the standard beginner's fault, and this exercise is the cure. Comparative terminology · المصطلحية المقارنة · Two terms, two languages, and the question of whether they are really equivalent. lede · Every method so far applies to one language or several. In bilingual and multilingual work there is one further step: compare the source and target terms and decide whether they are equivalent — which they frequently are not, in ways a dictionary will not tell you. card · Full equivalence · Two terms from different languages are fully equivalent when they have the same meaning and are used in the same way in a given subject field.They can be fully equivalent while representing the concept from a different point of view. English black out names the darkness; Arabic انقطاع الكهرباء names the interruption of supply. Different angle on the same concept, same use — fully equivalent. list · Partial equivalence, and its two causes · Language communities form and name concepts out of their own experience, so a source term often covers only part of what its supposed equivalent covers: Discrepancies in meaning. One term is generic and the other specific. Or one has shifted or acquired a new sense while the other has not moved.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Discrepancies in usage. Even where two terms cover exactly the same concept, they may differ in register, in geographic area, in age, or in frequency of use. card · What partial equivalence costs you · When two terms are only partly equivalent, the possibility of using one in exactly the same meaning and situation as the other is limited — and the limit is rarely visible in the sentence you are working on.Which is why the record notes it. A term marked partial, with the discrepancy named, warns the next user. A term filed as an equivalent with no qualification asserts something stronger than the research supports. Different point of view, still fully equivalent · English · black out · What the words say · a going-dark — the term is built on the effect · Arabic · انقطاع الكهرباء — a cutting-off of electricity: the term is built on the cause. Two languages describing one concept from opposite ends, and equivalent all the same, because equivalence is tested on meaning and use in the field — not on whether the two terms are built the same way. Do this before the next unit · Take eight English-Arabic term pairs from a glossary you trust. Judge each: full or partial equivalence.For every partial one, name the cause — generic against specific, a shift in one language, or a difference of register, region, age or frequency. Expect at least three of the eight to be partial and filed as though they were not. That is the normal state of most glossaries. Terminological records · البطاقة المصطلحية · Where the research lives so that it can be changed. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Terminologists work with living language, and that is precisely the problem with vocabularies, glossaries and specialised dictionaries: once published, what they contain is fixed and hard to modify. A record is easy to file, change, update or replace, which is why the record — not the publication — is where terminological data is kept. card · What a record is · An electronic document holding readily accessible information on a term specific to a subject field, on the concept it represents, and on the source in which it was found.Three things, and the third is not optional. A record without its source is an assertion; with it, it is evidence somebody else can check. split · Two formats · Sequential · متتابع · Each field appears in turn, in a predetermined order. Used by some computerized management systems. Condensed · مختصر · The whole record visible at a glance. The better format on paper, where records have to be consulted, filed and stored by hand. list · The eleven fields of a monolingual record · Entry — the term itself · Definition · Source · Date of publication · Volume, issue and page number · Grammatical labels · Usage and semantic labels · Context · Fields — and subfields · Authors and dates · card · Read that list again · Four of the eleven fields — source, date, volume/issue/page, authors and dates — exist for one purpose: so that any entry can be traced back and re-checked years later by somebody who was not there.That is the whole difference between a termbase and a list of words somebody was once confident about. The same term, recorded two ways · A list entry

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: informed consent — موافقة مستنيرة · What it does not say · Which field. Which definition. Who said so, where, and when. Whether the equivalence is full or partial. A record · Entry, definition, the context it was found in, the source with its date and page, the field and subfield, and who entered it when. The first can be produced in a minute and has to be re-researched by whoever inherits it. The second takes an hour and never has to be done again — which is the entire economics of terminology work. Do this before the next unit · Build one complete monolingual record, all eleven fields, for a single term in a field you know.Then hand it to somebody else and ask them to verify the entry from your record alone. If they cannot reach your source and confirm your definition without asking you a question, a field is doing no work — find out which one. Definitions · التعريف المصطلحي · Four rules that are easy to state and are broken constantly. lede · A terminological definition exists to give a clear understanding of a term in a given subject field, and it needs only the essential characteristics of that term as used there. That is narrower than a lexicographic or encyclopedic definition, which lists every meaning across every area of application. list · The four rules · Not obscure. Explaining the unknown with more unknown language fails the purpose. What is obscure to the layman but plain to the specialist is justifiably technical — the test is the intended reader, not simplicity for its own sake.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Neither too broad nor too narrow. It must not take in things the term does not apply to, nor leave out things it does. By the old rule of logic it should be able to replace the term in any statement without altering the meaning. Not circular. It may not use the term or any grammatical variant of it. One who studies or specializes in herpetology defines herpetologist circularly, and tells a reader who did not already know precisely nothing. Not negative where it can be affirmative. Say what a term means, not what it does not. Defining chair as not a bed and not a couch explains nothing. card · The exception to the fourth rule · Some terms are essentially negative in meaning and require a negative definition. Undifferentiated means having no special structure or function. Achromatic means having no colour.A negative definition of a negative term works, because its point of reference is an implied alternative — there is a differentiated state, there is colour. That is not the case for chair. split · Two methods · Genus and difference · الجنس والفصل · Name the larger class the concept belongs to, then the characteristic separating it from everything else in that class. Man as a rational animal: the genus is animal, the difference is rationality. The oldest and best-known method, used in both lexicography and terminology. Partition · التعريف بالتجزئة · Specify a whole by its parts. Used in addition to genus and difference when the object consists of several parts. One definition, four rules applied · The term · letter of credit · A definition that fails

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: “A credit given by letter.” — circular, obscure, and too broad all at once · Genus and difference · خطاب اعتماد — a bank undertaking (genus) to pay a seller on presentation of specified documents (difference) Test it against rule two: put the definition in place of the term in any sentence and see whether the meaning survives. It does — which is the check that separates a definition from a description. Do this before the next unit · Write terminological definitions for five terms in one field, by genus and difference.Then audit each against all four rules, in order, and write which rule it broke on the first attempt. Almost everyone breaks the second — too broad — and catching your own is faster once you have named the pattern. Term formation and standardisation · توليد المصطلح وتوحيده · Where new terms come from — and it is almost never from nowhere. lede · Term formation is the creation of new designations in special languages. Neologisms that spring from an inventor's mind with no prior history are rare. Terms are made by adding new meaning to existing words, by changing the morphology or grammatical class of what is already there, and by borrowing. card · It varies by field, and the variation is not random

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: In the biological sciences, where strict rules of nomenclature apply, classical derivation is favoured.In the earth sciences there is a lot of borrowing, because geologists, mineralogists and meteorologists tend to take a substance's term from the language of the place it commonly occurs.In computer science there is almost none, because the field developed almost entirely in English-speaking countries. Knowing which pattern a field follows tells you what its next term will probably look like. list · Three characteristics of modern English term formation. Productive. English has enriched its vocabulary by coining for centuries, in the general lexicon and in special languages alike — and the explosion in telecommunications, computer science, genetics and space exploration has made the need unprecedented. A preference for composition and metaphor. Compounds and derived forms have been the chief source of new words for a thousand years and are first in numerical importance among new terms. They offer precision and transparency — a user can often read the meaning off the parts. Metaphor and analogy are economical and use suggestion to communicate. A tradition of borrowing. Historically from Latin, Greek, French and German — the languages strongly represented in law, medicine, science and technology — and still from anywhere it makes contact with. card · Where the terminologist comes in

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Semantic change — altering the meaning of an established word through analogy, metonymy and the like — is one of the two main ways new terms are formed.The terminologist's contribution is to help ensure new coinages follow the time-honoured patterns of that change. A term formed the way the field's terms have always been formed is guessable, memorable and likely to be adopted. One formed against the pattern has to be learned twice and is often quietly replaced. card · And the rule from unit one still holds · Coining is the last resort, warranted only when every available source has been researched and the evidence shows no term exists for the concept.Standardisation is the other end of the same work: settling which term carries the concept, and recording that decision where the next person will find it. The four work methods close where they started. Transparency, and what it buys · A compound · laughmeter · Why it works · A user who has never met the term can read the concept off its parts — a device that measures laughter · The Arabic problem · مقياس الضحك — transparent in the same way, because the compound was rebuilt rather than transliterated. Had it been borrowed as لافميتر the Arabic reader would have to be told what it means. Composition kept the transparency; borrowing would have spent it. That is the choice term formation is, every time. The last one

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Find five terms coined in English in the last twenty years. For each, identify the process: semantic change, composition, derivation, metaphor, or borrowing.Then propose an Arabic term for each, and say which process you used and why. Finally, check whether an Arabic term already exists. Where one does, you have just demonstrated unit one's rule to yourself: identify before you create. 280 · Translation I · ترجمة ١ · 142 · The first course where the work has your name on it. General texts, in both directions, translated and then defended out loud. Where the framework from 180 stops being something to recite and becomes a series of decisions you have to make and stand behind.Most of the difficulty is not vocabulary. It is that words arrive in company, and a dictionary that hands them over one at a time will mislead you roughly once a paragraph. Correspondence · Journalism · General prose · The ground every specialism stands on · Volume, and the habit of revision. The gap between a first draft and a finished rendering is the course. commentary · colloc · 281 · Translation II · ترجمة ٢ · 142 · The step from a passage to a whole document. Longer texts, harder genres, and revision treated as part of the work rather than as something done if time allows. A file behaves differently from a paragraph: it has to hold together across pages that will be read hours apart.Which makes consistency the new skill. Not elegance — sameness, in the places where sameness is what carries the meaning. Reports · Articles · Contracts · Book chapters

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Consistency across length, and the discipline of reading the draft three times for three different things. errors · commentary · Elective group one · المجموعة الاختيارية الأولى · Choose two · prerequisite 180 · يختار الطالب مقررين، المتطلب السابق ١٨٠ · Elective · 283 · Text Analysis and Translation · تحليل النص والترجمة · 180 · The reading that decides the translation. Taking a text apart before translating a word of it: its field, its tone, its genre, who wrote it, who it was written for, and what it is trying to make happen.The analysis is the decision. The translating carries it out. Most bad translations are not failures of vocabulary — they are failures to have read. Every commission · Especially the ones that look simple · Patience at the start, and the willingness to ask a client a question before beginning. texttypes · context · 284 · Translation and Culture · الترجمة والثقافة · 180 · What to do when the difficulty is not linguistic. Culture-specific items, proverbs, politeness, religion, institutions — the places where both languages are perfectly clear and the reader still will not understand.And the choice underneath all of them: bring the text to the reader, or take the reader to the text. Neither is automatically right, and the reader is entitled to know which one you chose. Literature · Subtitling · Advertising · Diplomacy · News · A decision you can defend — and the honesty to notice when you smoothed something away. cultural · proverb · lineage · What translation is · ما الترجمة؟ Three things decide your strategy before you translate a word. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Translation is the interpretation of a source text's meaning and the production of an equivalent meaning in another language. Peter Newmark (1981) puts it as the attempt to replace a written message or statement in one language by the same message or statement in another — so the focus is the transfer of the meaning the author intended. list · Nida's three factors · Eugene Nida (1964) adds that three things besides the meaning itself determine how the process runs: The nature of the message — which is to say the text type. The purpose of the author, and by proxy of the translator. The type of audience. card · Text type decides the strategy · Translation is a text-based activity, and the type of the source text sets the approach before you make a single choice.Religious and legal texts pull translators towards the literal, because the form is part of what is binding. Spoken passages from films, conferences and official meetings pull them towards the communicative, because the effect on the hearer is what has to survive. card · And the audience decides the register · A story for children is translated in simple, polite language. A medical text for experts or researchers is translated in the highly technical register its readers expect and can read.Same skill, opposite surface. Getting this wrong is not a vocabulary failure — it is having failed to ask who is going to read the thing. split · And the distinction to keep straight · Translator · مترجم تحريري · Written texts. Time to stop, research, revise. Interpreter · مترجم شفوي

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Spoken passages, in real time. Both require deep cultural and linguistic understanding, expert knowledge of the subject matter, and the ability to communicate clearly and appropriately. One event, two readerships, two right translations · Arabic (a Kuwaiti news item) استقبل سمو أمير البلاد رئيس مجلس الوزراء صباح اليوم بقصر بيان. For a Kuwaiti readership · Titles, palace and protocol all kept — because in that setting the form is part of the information · For a foreign wire service · The Amir of Kuwait received the Prime Minister at Bayan Palace this morning. Nothing was mistranslated in either. The second drops honorifics an English reader does not parse and would read as flattery — a decision made on audience, which is Nida's third factor doing real work. Unit nine returns to exactly this. Do this before the next unit · Take one Kuwaiti news item and translate it twice: once for KUNA's English service, once for a British paper.List every difference. Then say, for each, which of Nida's three factors caused it. If a difference answers to none of the three, you made it for no reason, and it should come out. Literal translation · الترجمة الحرفية · It works more often than people admit — and fails in a way you can predict. lede · Literal — also called direct or formal — translation takes existing content in one language and renders it word for word, or sentence by sentence, into the other. It is the simplest type, it is the approach most automated systems use, and it is not automatically wrong. list · When it works

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: When there is no difference between the two languages in manner of expression and in cultural meaning or association. These four cross intact, because the image exists on both sides: To give the green light — يعطي الضوء الأخضر · To fish in troubled waters — اصطاد في الماء العكر · From a different angle — من زاوية مختلفة · Calm before the storm — الهدوء قبل العاصفة · card · When it fails: structure · Between languages of distant sources like Arabic and English the structures do not line up, and the translator has to modify structure and content to meet the reader's expectations.شمس الدنيا becomes It's sunny: the English has a dummy subject it where the Arabic has الدنيا, and an adjective sunny where the Arabic has the noun شمس. Going the other way, on foot becomes على الأقدام — the English singular has to become an Arabic plural. list · When it fails: idiom and proverb · This is the larger failure, and the one with cultural content. Arabic proverbs rendered word for word into English: أنت أرنب — You are rabbit · اللي فات مات — What passed died · يوم لك ويوم عليك — A day for you, a day against you. زاد الطين بلة — It increased the clay moistness · list · And it fails in the other direction too · English idioms rendered word for word into Arabic produce sentences that parse and say nothing: One can't get blood from a stone — الواحد لا يستطيع أن يحصل على الدم من الحجر · Like father, like son — مثل الأب، مثل الابن · Keep it under your hat — اتركها تحت قبعتك · card · Which is why the next unit exists

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Each of those eight is a real saying with a real meaning, and not one of those meanings is in the translation. When the two cultures do not share the image, the literal route is closed and you need a method that carries the effect instead. One proverb, literally · Arabic · زاد الطين بلة · Word for word · It increased the clay moistness — every word correct, and no English reader can recover the meaning · The meaning · It made matters worse. / Add salt to injury. The literal version is not a bad translation of the words. It is a good translation of the words and a failed translation of the proverb — which is the distinction this course is about. Do this before the next unit · Collect six Kuwaiti expressions you use daily. Translate each one literally into English, on purpose.Then sort them: which literal versions would an English reader actually understand, and which are nonsense? The ones that survive share an image with English. Write down what that image is — that is the thing literal translation is carrying. Communicative translation · الترجمة التواصلية · Translate the effect, not the wording — and know what you are giving up. lede · Communicative translation attempts to produce on its readers an effect as close as possible to that obtained on the readers of the original (Newmark, 1981).
