It has a target-language bias: it is free and idiomatic, it tries to make the reading easier for a reader who does not anticipate difficulties, and it emphasises the force of the message rather than its literal form. list · The same sayings, communicatively

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Every pair in the previous unit has an answer. The translator's job is to find the target language's own saying, not to describe the source one: Let bygones be bygones — اللي فات مات · You win some, you lose some — يوم لك ويوم عليك · Add salt to injury — زاد الطين بلة · One can't get blood from a stone — إنك لا تجني من الشوك العنب. Like father, like son — هذا الشبل من ذاك الأسد. Man proposes and God disposes — أنت تريد، وأنا أريد، والله يفعل ما يريد · It is not my cup of tea — هذه ليست لعبتي · A Jack of all trades is a master of none — سبع صنايع والبخت ضايع. Keep your nose out of other people's business — يا داخل بين البصلة وقشرتها ما بطولك إلا ريحتها · card · It also fixes the wording nobody notices · The standard English for شرطة مكافحة الشغب is riot police — not anti-riot police, not riot combat police, both of which are what the Arabic structure would give you.Most communicative translation is not dramatic. It is knowing what the target language actually says. card · The social formula has no words in it · نعيماً is said to someone who has just had a haircut or a bath. Translated word for word it is a blessing; translated communicatively it is nice haircut.That is the whole move. The Arabic performs a social act and the English names the occasion, because English has no formula for the moment and Arabic has nothing else. card · And the formula that changes meaning every time

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: إن شاء الله has no single English equivalent, because its translation depends on what it means in the situation.It can be I hope, I promise, or I am not sure. It can be a way of refusing a promise. It can express dislike or antipathy without saying so. A translator who always renders it God willing has translated the words and missed the act every time but one. The same two words, two different acts · A question and its answer · — بتخلص الشغل بكرة؟‎ — إن شاء الله. Always the same rendering · God willing — which tells an English reader nothing about whether the work will be done · What each one is doing · As a promise: Yes, it'll be ready tomorrow. · As a soft refusal: We'll see. · As genuine uncertainty: I hope so. A Kuwaiti hearer reads which of these is meant from tone, situation and who is speaking. The English reader has none of that, so the translator has to choose — and choosing is not taking a liberty here, it is the only way to be accurate. Do this before the next unit · Two parts.One. Listen for إن شاء الله five times in one day and write down, each time, which act it was performing and the English you would use. You should end with five different renderings.Two. Take the nine pairs above and test them. For each, ask: does the Arabic saying do the same job as the English one, or only sound like it? Proverb pairs circulate widely and some of them do not survive the question. Finding the one that does not is worth more to you than memorising the other eight. Machine translation · الترجمة الآلية · Mechanical substitution, and exactly where it breaks. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Machine translation is a sub-field of computational linguistics investigating the use of software to translate text or speech from one language to another. At a basic level it performs mechanical substitution of words in one language for words in another — and that alone rarely produces a good translation, because what is needed is recognition of whole phrases and their closest counterparts in the target language. card · Arabic into English: two phrases missed at once. A woman describes a problem she took to her mother-in-law. She says she نشرت غسيلها أمام الناس, and that وافق شنٌّ طبقة.The machine gives I spread my laundry in front of people and he agreed to launch a class. The first is a correct rendering of a unit it did not see. The second is not even that — it has read a proverb about two well-matched people as a sentence about launching something. A translator gives I let the cat out of the bag and every Jack has his Jill. card · English into Arabic: a name read as a country. BBC sport news indicated that Jordan's trainers will be sold for a record $560,000.The machine returns الحذاء الرياضي الأردني — the Jordanian trainer. It has taken Jordan for the country. Nothing in the sentence is mistranslated word by word; the whole thing is about the wrong subject. card · Where it is genuinely useful

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: As a draft, and for getting the gist of a document you would otherwise not read at all.What it cannot do is know the subject or read the culture. Which means someone has to be able to tell when the output is wrong — and that takes more knowledge than producing the translation yourself, not less. card · A Gulf case it will always fail · Machine systems are trained overwhelmingly on Modern Standard Arabic and on Levantine and Egyptian usage. Kuwaiti and Gulf vocabulary is thinly represented, and culture-specific items barely at all.Feed one القرقيعان or الديرة and you will get a transliteration or a guess — الديرة flattened to the country when it means one's own town. Neither tells a foreign reader what happened. One sentence, by machine and by hand · English (BBC sport) Jordan's trainers will be sold for a record $560,000. Machine · سيتم بيع الحذاء الرياضي الأردني بمبلغ قياسي قدره ٥٦٠ ألف دولار — the Jordanian trainer, a shoe belonging to a country · Human (communicative) أشارت تقارير رياضية في قناة البي بي سي الإخبارية إلى بيع حذاء أسطورة كرة السلة الأمريكية مايكل جوردن برقم قياسي بلغ ٥٦٠٬٠٠٠ دولار أمريكي. Two things the human did. It resolved Jordan to Michael Jordan — which required knowing who he is, not knowing English. And it added أسطورة كرة السلة الأمريكية, because an Arabic reader may not recognise the name unglossed. That second move is explicitation, and unit six is about it. Do this before the next unit

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Put five Kuwaiti sentences through a machine translator — ones with local vocabulary and at least one proper name, not standard news prose.Mark every error and label it: wrong word, missed phrase, or missing culture. You will find the third is most of them, and it is the one no amount of better software has yet fixed. Cohesion and coherence · السبك والحبك · Arabic joins its sentences aloud. English joins them silently. lede · A stylistic difference that runs through every text in this language pair: English prefers coherence — implicit connectedness — while Arabic prefers cohesion — connectedness made explicit with conjunctions and coordinators. card · What that means at the desk · Translating into English, you do not have to use conjunctions as frequently as Arabic does. Keep them all and the English reads like a chain of clauses with no shape.Translating into Arabic, you may need them more frequently than the English has them. Leave them out and the Arabic reads as a series of disconnected statements — grammatical, and somehow not joined up. card · English splitting where Arabic joins · All requests for leave without pay must be in writing. They must be submitted to the human resources office.Two English sentences, no connector, and the relation is left for the reader to see. The Arabic joins them: تُحرَّر كل الطلبات الخاصة بالإجازة بدون أجر كتابةً، كما يجب تقديمها إلى مكتب الموارد البشرية — and would read oddly without the كما. card · And the reverse

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: An Arabic paragraph built on و after و, with وحيث and ولهذا marking each turn, becomes in English four sentences with the connectors removed and the logic carried by the sequence itself.Nothing is lost. The connection has moved from the words to the arrangement, which is where English keeps it. One event, two ways of joining it up · Arabic · لقد تعرّض معلّم الرياضيات لحادث هذا الصباح، وحيث نُقل على إثره إلى المستشفى، ولهذا لن يقوم بإعطاء محاضرات لهذا اليوم، وحيث سنعود للبيت باكراً اليوم. Every connector kept · The maths teacher had an accident this morning, and he was sent to hospital, and he is not going to give us lectures today, and we will go home early. — childish in English, and the original is not · English coherence · The Math teacher had an accident this morning. He has been sent to hospital. He is not going to give us lectures for today. We will go home early today. Four sentences, four full stops, and every و gone. The cause, the consequence and the sequence are all still there — carried by the order of the sentences instead of by words. That is what implicit connectedness means in practice. Do this before the next unit · Take an Arabic paragraph and count its coordinators. Translate it into English and count them again.The second number should be much lower. Then read your English aloud: if it still sounds like a list, you moved the words and kept the Arabic joinery. Then do it in reverse — take an English paragraph of short sentences and see how many connectors the Arabic wants back. Explicitation · التصريح والشرح الثقافي

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Saying out loud what the source left for readers who already knew. lede · Where source and target readers do not share a cultural presupposition, the translator uses explicitation — also called cultural explanation, substitution, functional equivalence or paraphrase. It is the explanation of the source-text terms and realities: making what is implicit in the source explicit in the target, to keep the target text appropriate and accessible. card · The simplest form: say what the thing is · The Beatles becomes الفرقة الموسيقية البريطانية ذا بيتلز. A Farewell to Arms becomes الرواية الأمريكية المشهورة وداعاً للسلاح.Four words added in each case, and the ambiguity is gone. The Arabic reader now knows that one is a band and the other is a novel — which the English reader knew without being told. card · In literature: the footnote · In Kanafani's Men in the Sun a passage turns on the name Hatim. Kilpatrick's translation keeps the name and adds a note: Hatim, of the bedouin tribe of Tayy, is proverbial among the Arabs for his limitless generosity and hospitality.Without it the sentence still parses and the point vanishes. The reader has no idea why this name settles anything. card · In fiction: the gloss inside the sentence · A Mahfouz narrator fears that anyone overhearing his wife complain would take him for ريا أو سكينة.The English reads: would have thought I was a cold-blooded killer like those dreadful women in Alexandria in Egypt: Rayya and Sakina. Everything after killer is the translator's. It is inside the sentence because a novel's reader will not stop for a footnote.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: list · In news: the headline that has to be unpacked. A local headline assumes the reader's whole context. A foreign one has none of it: الأردنيون في مواجهة مع الحكومة لإلغاء وادي عربة → Jordanians urge their government to scrap Wadi Araba's peace treaty with Israel — the reader is told what Wadi Araba is. دجاج عمرو خالد يثير الجدل وعلماء الأزهر يطالبونه بالتوبة والاعتذار → The Egyptian Muslim activist and television preacher, Amr Khaled, is in hot water over a chicken advertisement. The scholars of the famous Egyptian Islamic university Al-Azhar are urging him to apologize and repent. — the person and the institution both named. صباح الجزائري تنتقد باب الحارة وتتبرأ منه → The famous Syrian actress and star of the Syrian Ramadan TV series Bab Al-Harah, Sabah Al-Jazairi, criticized and disowned the TV series. — where the machine gave only the bare names, which name nobody. card · The cost, and the limit · Explicitations are traces of the translator's attempt to interpret the original and make it easier to process and more cohesive for the target reader (Blum-Kulka, 2000). They ease comprehensibility and readability — and they make the translation longer, flatter and more explanatory than the original ever was.Explain a joke and it is no longer a joke. The judgement is how much the reader needs in order to get what the source reader got — and then stopping. A Kuwaiti reference that means nothing abroad · Arabic · اجتمعوا في الديوانية ليلة القرقيعان. Kept as it stands

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: They gathered in the diwaniyya on Gergean night — two loan words, and a reader who now knows neither what the room is nor what the night is · With explicitation · They gathered at the diwaniyya, the household's regular evening reception room, on the night of Gergean — the mid-Ramadan celebration when children go from house to house collecting sweets. Twice the length, and the only version that works. Note what was not done: neither term was replaced with a Western near-equivalent. Halloween would be shorter, familiar, and wrong about the occasion, the month and the meaning. Do this before the next unit · Find a Kuwaiti news item containing at least three references a foreign reader would not have — a place, an institution, an occasion.Translate it twice: once with footnotes, once with everything glossed in the text. Compare the lengths and decide which you would publish and for whom. Then mark the one reference you would leave unexplained, and say why the reader can live without it. Collocations and idioms · المتلازمات والتعابير · Both languages are clear, both are correct, and only one of them is what people say. lede · A collocation is two or more words that often go together. Collocations and idioms are culturally bound — they do not apply across languages. When words collocate they may give a meaning that is different or unnatural in the target language, which is why literal translation produces unnatural pairings and communicative translation is needed. split · Natural and unnatural English · Natural · المألوف · the fast train · fast food · a quick shower · a quick meal

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Unnatural · غير المألوف · the quick train · quick food · a fast shower · a fast meal · card · Nothing in the meanings explains it · Fast and quick are near-synonyms, and each takes its own company. You catch a bus; you cannot hold one.Arabic does the same. Break the law rendered literally is يكسر القانون — grammatical, and not Arabic. The natural collocation is يخالف القانون. There is no rule to derive; the obligation is to know what the target language says, which is why the target language should be the one you know best. card · Idioms mean what their words do not · He is a black sheep rendered literally is إنه خاروف أسود, which makes no sense in Arabic. Communicatively it is إنه سيّئ الأخلاق.An idiom should be translated communicatively whenever the literal meaning does not make sense on the other side. list · English into Arabic · to break the ice — يمهّد الطريق · he looks blue — يبدو حزيناً · he is in the clouds — هو شارد الذهن · strong tea — شاي ثقيل · to carry coals to Newcastle — يبيع مياه في حارة السقّايين · to kick the bucket — لقي حتفه / مات · when pigs fly — لما ينوّر الصوان · to sweat like a pig — يتصبّب عرقاً · list · Arabic into English · ابتسامة مصطنعة — a forced smile · دم ولحم — flesh and blood · ليل ونهار — day and night · واضح زي الشمس — clear as crystal · مدخّن شره — a heavy smoker · دليل دامغ — a smoking gun · ما بسوى بصلة — not worth a damn · ابن حلال — a good sort · ابن كار — made for the job · ابن سوق — a born businessman. يا خبر أسود — Bloody hell! · يختي عليها — How cute! · يا خيبتك — What a dead loss you are! card · Notice the last row

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Those three are not hard because the meaning is obscure. They are hard because the difficulty is tone: how rude, how affectionate, how mocking, and whether an English reader would take the speaker for a friend or an enemy.A dictionary will not settle it. Only knowing both registers will. card · Replacing an idiom with a different one entirely. In Men in the Sun, Kilpatrick renders ليكسر الفخار بعضه with a verse from the Bible — Let the dead bury their dead — because it carries the same meaning for an English reader.That is a real choice with a real cost: the target reader now hears a scriptural register the Arabic did not have. Sometimes that is the best available trade. It should be a decision, not an accident. card · A whole text of them at once · An English news paragraph on the George Floyd case runs a political hot potato, a stitch in time saves nine and live and learn in three consecutive sentences.The machine gives غرزة في الوقت المناسب تنقذ تسعة — a sentence about sewing. The communicative version replaces it with the Arabic proverb that does the job: درهم وقاية خير من قنطار علاج. Same argument, different image, and an Arabic reader who does not stumble. A Gulf collocation with no English partner · Arabic · الحمد لله على السلامة · Word for word · Praise be to God for the safety — pious, odd, and not what is being done · What the act is · Said to someone back from travel or out of hospital: Welcome back · Glad you're back safely · Thank God you're all right

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: English has no fixed formula for this moment, so there is no counterpart to find — only a choice about which part to keep: the welcome, the relief, or the thanks. Whichever you pick, something in the Arabic is not going with it. This is the same problem as نعيماً in unit three. Do this before the next unit · List ten Kuwaiti social formulae — for a new purchase, a haircut, a safe return, a death, an exam result, a new baby.For each, ask whether English has a fixed phrase for that moment. Where it does, use it. Where it does not, write what you would say instead and what the Arabic loses. Expect more than half to have no English formula at all — that gap is the subject of this whole course. Cultural associations · الإيحاءات الثقافية · The word is right. What it makes the reader feel is wrong. lede · Language and culture are part and parcel of each other and cannot be separated. Language marks cultural identity — language is culture — so translating a language implies translating a culture. And culture is a fuzzy set of attitudes, behavioural conventions, assumptions and values shared by a set of people, which means connotation does not travel with denotation. card · The same animal, opposite meanings

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: ذيب — the wolf — has a positive association in Arab culture and a negative one in English. A good communicative translation is brave or strong, not wolf.The owl runs the other way. As wise as an owl becomes ذكي or حكيم, never حكيم كالبومة, because the owl carries a negative association in Arabic that does not exist in English. Both times: every word correct, and the sentence meaning the opposite of what it meant. list · Where this bites hardest · Loaded history. Crusade campaigns is neutral or admiring in English usage. Rendered as حملات صليبية it imports a charge the English never had, so translators use حملات غربية instead. Behaviour ordinary in one culture and not the other. Let's grab a beer after work becomes لنخرج بعد العمل — the alcohol removed, or substituted with coffee or juice. The act survives; the detail that does not belong is dropped. Political vocabulary. Kilpatrick renders Kanafani's المجاهدين as the Freedom Fighters, and مجاهدو الطيرة as the commandos in Al-Tira — precisely to avoid conveying to an English audience the negative feelings the obvious English word would import. Identity terms. A word naming a people, a faith or an origin can be neutral on one side and a charge on the other, in either direction. This is the case that most needs naming rather than carrying across: the translator's job is to render what was meant, not to deliver a charge the reader will feel and the author never sent. card · What you are actually deciding

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Whether to protect the reader's response or the source's wording. Both are defensible; only one can be had.What is not defensible is not noticing — carrying a word across and leaving the reader to receive a charge the author never sent. A compliment that arrives as an accusation · Arabic (Gulf) فلان جِمَل · Literally · He is a camel — in English an insult, or at best a joke · What it says in the Gulf · He has enormous endurance — he carries what others cannot. The camel is the Gulf's emblem of patience and endurance, and the comparison is praise. English animal vocabulary carries no such association, so the image has to be dropped and the quality named — exactly the move the course makes with ذيب, and the reverse of the one it makes with the owl. Do this before the next unit · Take five animals and five colours. For each, write what it connotes in Kuwait and what it connotes in English.Mark every pair that disagrees. Then find one real sentence containing one of them and translate it — and say in a line whether you kept the image or the effect, and why that was the right trade in that text. Politeness and address · المجاملة وألقاب المخاطبة · What is polite in one language is strange, cold or rude in the other. lede · Communicative translation may involve altering discourse markers, address terms or titles, because translation involves a shift in the audience. What is polite in Arabic may be impolite in English and the reverse, so the translator makes the modifications the target culture's politeness standards require. card · English into Arabic: what comes out

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Vulgar and taboo expressions are routinely deleted, because Arabic culture values politeness far more than faithfulness and accuracy.A line from Wuthering Heights — he cursed and defied: execrated God and man, and gave himself up to reckless dissipation — comes into Arabic as صبّ سخطه على الحياة والناس. You may think that is wrong. It is what the target culture's norms produce, and knowing it is the difference between choosing and drifting. list · Arabic into English: what comes out · Arabic politeness expressions and address terms that are not familiar in English are dropped, to keep the target text appropriate for its audience: قال أبو قيس: الأخ أسعد يحكي الحق → Abu Qais remarked: “Assad's quite right.” — الأخ gone. ما رأي عم الحاج رضا أن يصعد إلى سيارتي؟ → “How would Haj Rida like to get into my lorry?” — عم gone, الحاج kept because it identifies him. بحث جلالة الملك عبد الله الثاني حفظه الله ورعاه مع أخيه فخامة الرئيس المصري… → King Abdullah of Jordan discussed with the Egyptian President El-Sisi… — four honorifics and the word brother all gone, and the sentence has lost nothing an English reader needed. card · A Gulf case English cannot do at all · Teknonymy — addressing someone as أبو أحمد or أم أحمد, father or mother of their eldest son.It is warm, respectful and slightly formal all at once, and it is the ordinary way adults address each other. English has no equivalent register. Abu Ahmad means nothing to the reader; Mr Al-Otaibi is correct and colder; the first name is accurate and loses the respect. There is no right answer, only a choice and a reason.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Court protocol for a foreign wire · Arabic (a Kuwaiti news item) استقبل حضرة صاحب السمو أمير البلاد الشيخ نواف الأحمد الجابر الصباح حفظه الله ورعاه بقصر السيف العامر صباح اليوم سمو الشيخ صباح خالد الحمد الصباح حفظه الله ورعاه. Every honorific carried over · His Highness the Possessor of Highness the Amir of the Country Sheikh… may God preserve and protect him… received His Highness Sheikh… — accurate, and unreadable · As the BBC published it · The Amir Nawaf of Kuwait received this morning the Prime Minister Sabah Al-Sabah at the Kuwaiti ruling palace. Count what went: حضرة صاحب السمو, both instances of حفظه الله ورعاه, most of each name, and the epithet on the palace. What stayed is the office, the name and the fact. A Kuwaiti outlet publishing in English may keep His Highness deliberately — that is an editorial decision about who the paper speaks for, not a translation error. Do this before the next unit · Take one Amiri Diwan statement in Arabic and translate it for three readerships: KUNA English, a British paper, and a Kuwaiti English-language paper.The three will differ mainly in how much honorific survives. Write one line for each explaining who the reader is and what that reader needs — which is the whole of this unit. Ideology in translation · الأيديولوجيا في الترجمة · Six places where beliefs, not language, decide what the translation says. lede

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Translating between English and Arabic involves not only linguistic and cultural considerations but ideological ones. Ideology in translation is the influence of beliefs, values, politics and worldview on how a text is interpreted and represented in another language — and it shapes how translators handle power, religion, gender, colonialism and identity, whether or not anyone intends it. list · Six kinds · Religious. Jesus is the son of God renders literally as يسوع هو ابن الله, which contradicts Islamic doctrine, where Jesus is a prophet and not divine. A translation for an Islamic context typically reframes or footnotes it: يسوع، الذي يُعتقد في المسيحية أنه ابن الله. Gender. A woman can lead a nation — يمكن للمرأة أن تقود أمة — may be ideologically sensitive in conservative contexts, and be rephrased cautiously or avoided in certain media. Colonial and postcolonial. The British brought civilization to the East — جلب البريطانيون الحضارة إلى الشرق — implies cultural inferiority to an Arab readership. A translator may challenge it: ادّعى البريطانيون أنهم جلبوا الحضارة إلى الشرق — claimed, which is a real intervention in the text. Political. Freedom of speech is a universal right is neutral in English and sensitive where speech is regulated. It may be framed more cautiously: حرية التعبير مكفولة في حدود القانون. Media framing. One event, two outlets: قُتل ثلاثة فلسطينيين في اشتباكات مع القوات الإسرائيلية against قامت قوات الاحتلال الإسرائيلي بقتل ثلاثة متظاهرين فلسطينيين. Same report. The framing alone changes the tone and the implication.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Secular against religious. Darwin's theory of evolution challenges the creationist view may be softened and framed with caution: نظرية داروين في التطور تُعد مثار جدل بالنسبة للرؤية الدينية للخلق. card · Why this is on a translation syllabus · Because every choice above is made with grammar: active or passive, who is named as agent, which verb, what gets a qualifier, what gets a reporting frame like claimed or faced accusations.That is your equipment. Ideology is not a topic beside translation technique; it is what technique does when the subject is contested. One event, and where the ideology sits · English news · Israeli forces killed three Palestinian protesters. One outlet · قُتل ثلاثة فلسطينيين في اشتباكات مع القوات الإسرائيلية — no agent, and clashes makes it mutual · The other · قامت قوات الاحتلال الإسرائيلي بقتل ثلاثة متظاهرين فلسطينيين. Neither version contains a false word. The difference is voice, naming and the choice of noun for the parties — three ordinary grammatical choices doing the entire political work of the sentence. This is why a translator cannot become neutral by translating carefully; the careful choices are the political ones. Do this before the next unit · Find one story reported by two outlets with opposing positions, in English and in Arabic.Compare them on four points only: active or passive, who is named as agent, the verb chosen for the action, and what each calls the parties. Write the four differences down. You have just done ideological analysis with nothing but grammar. Self-censorship · الرقابة الذاتية

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: The changes nobody asked for — and the hardest thing to see in your own work. lede · Ideological self-censorship is when translators deliberately alter, omit or soften content to align with the politics, religion or culture of the target audience — often without being explicitly instructed to do so. It is internalised censorship: the translator anticipates what might be considered inappropriate or controversial and adapts pre-emptively. list · Four documented patterns · Theology. God is just a concept created by man becomes لله مفاهيم متعددة تختلف من شخص لآخر — there are multiple concepts of God that vary from person to person. The claim has been replaced by a survey of opinion, to avoid blasphemy or offence. Gender. A woman doesn't need a man to be complete becomes المرأة كيان مستقل يمكنه الاعتماد على ذاته في بعض الأمور — in certain matters. The qualifier is doing all the work, and the empowerment is toned down. Politics. The regime was corrupt and brutally suppressed opposition becomes واجه النظام اتهامات تتعلق بالفساد وتعامله مع المعارضة — statement turned into allegation, often out of real fear of surveillance, professional repercussions or legal trouble. Social norms. She poured a glass of wine and lit a cigarette becomes سكبت لنفسها شراباً وجلست بهدوء. Two culturally disapproved acts removed from a sentence that was characterising someone. card · Notice what these have in common

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Every one is fluent, plausible and defensible in isolation. None reads as censorship. That is exactly what makes it hard to catch in your own work — you do not experience it as changing the text, you experience it as finding the natural phrasing.And the fourth example shows the cost most clearly: the wine and the cigarette were characterisation. Remove them and a specific woman becomes a generic one. card · This is not an instruction to translate provocatively. Real constraints exist. Publishers have policies, countries have laws, and some adaptations are the condition of the book appearing at all.The professional standard is not never soften. It is know that you did, be able to say which constraint you were answering, and tell whoever commissioned the work. A softening you can name is an editorial decision. A softening you cannot see is a loss of control over your own translation. card · Where this course ends · Every unit here has been one version of a single question: what did you change, and can you say why?Literal against communicative, explicitation, the wolf and the owl, the honorifics, the passive voice, the wine. None of them has a rule that decides it. All of them have an answer you should be able to give out loud — and that answer is what a commentary is, and what the rest of the minor will ask you for. A softening you could defend, and the line to put in the file · English source · She poured a glass of wine and lit a cigarette. Self-censored · سكبت لنفسها شراباً وجلست بهدوء — fluent, publishable, and a different woman · The honest options

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Translate it as written, or soften it and record the change: “Alcohol and smoking neutralised for the target market; characterisation affected.” The second option is not a worse translation than the first. It is the same translation with the decision made visible — which is the only thing that separates a professional adaptation from an invisible one. The last one · Take a page you have already translated and read it against the source hunting only for softenings — a qualifier added, an accusation turned into a report, a detail quietly gone.For each, write one line: what you changed, and which constraint you were answering. If you cannot name a constraint, you did not adapt it — you flinched, and the text is now saying something you never decided to say. 285 · Translation for Special Purposes · الترجمة لأغراض خاصة · 180 · Where a wrong word stops being a style problem. Language for specific purposes: legal, medical, technical, commercial. Each field has its own terminology, its own register, its own conventions of layout, and its own idea of what an error costs.Most paid translation work is this. It is also where risk lives, and where risk assessment stops being an academic exercise. Law · Medicine · Engineering · Finance · Certified translation · That you know the subject well enough to know when you do not — and say so rather than guess. register · booth · Elective group two · المجموعة الاختيارية الثانية · Choose two · prerequisite 180 · يختار الطالب مقررين، المتطلب السابق ١٨٠ · Elective · 386 · Literary Translation · الترجمة الأدبية · 180

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: Where what crosses is not only the information. Prose and poetry, in which voice, rhythm, register and effect are not decoration on the meaning — they are part of it. The course where the question of what cannot cross is asked most seriously, and answered least comfortably.It is also the course that asks most of your writing. A literary translator who is not a writer produces information about a book. Publishing · Poetry · Theatre · Literary prizes and translation projects · That you write well in the target language, and that you know when to lose something on purpose. lineage · commentary · 387 · Introduction to Audiovisual Translation · مقدمة في الترجمة السمعية البصرية · 180 · Translation with a stopwatch and a ruler. Translation for screen: subtitling, dubbing, voice-over, and audio description for viewers who cannot see. Its defining feature is constraint — characters per line, seconds on screen, lip movement.And a reader who can hear the original while reading you, which no other kind of translation has to survive. Streaming · Broadcast · Film festivals · Corporate video · Accessibility · Ruthless compression without loss of sense, and the nerve to be checked in real time by an audience that half-understands the source. subtitle · 388 · Introduction to Translation and Technology · مدخل إلى الترجمة والتكنولوجيا · 180 · The tools, and why you are still the one responsible.

chunks.title: Translation Minor (cont.)
chunks.text: What the profession actually runs on: computer-assisted translation, translation memory, terminology management, machine translation and post-editing — and now generative systems, including what they produce when they do not know.Translation memory and a termbase are not optional extras in professional work. They are how consistency and a delivery date are met at once. Agencies · Institutions · Localisation · Post-editing work · That you stay the editor. A tool faster than you is still not responsible for the output — you are. glossary · errors

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: What translation is not
chunks.text: What translation is not · ما ليست الترجمة · Ten things everybody believes, and why the course begins by clearing them away. lede · Almost everyone arrives with the same set of beliefs about this work, and almost all of them are wrong. They are worth stating plainly, because each one, left in place, produces a specific kind of bad translation. split · The first confusion, and the one that matters most · Translation · الترجمة التحريرية · Written text into written text. You can stop, look something up, change your mind, and revise. Interpreting · الترجمة الشفوية · Speech into speech, in real time, often while the speaker is still talking. There is no second pass. list · The rest of them · Each is stated as people state it, with what is actually true underneath: It is an exchange of words. Languages differ in vocabulary, grammar and structure, so what moves across is the sense, not the words. Some things have no counterpart at all and must be conveyed another way. Any bilingual can do it. Two languages is the entry requirement, not the qualification. The work needs training, command of both written registers, and knowledge of the subject. Machines have made it unnecessary. Machine output is a draft. It does not know the subject and does not read the culture. Someone has to be able to tell when it is wrong — which takes more skill than translating, not less. The need is shrinking. It is not. The market has grown, not contracted, alongside the tools.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: What translation is not (cont.)
chunks.text: A translator covers every field. Almost nobody does. Legal, medical and financial translation are separate trades with separate vocabularies. Translators work in many languages. Most work in two. The depth required in each is the reason. You need not understand the material. You cannot translate what you have not understood. It is the one thing with no shortcut. Culture is optional. It is not separable from the language. Idiom, reference and what may be said at all are cultural facts. It can be free. Free tools translate phrases. Documents that carry consequences are paid work, for the same reason the consequences exist. card · Why start here · Every one of these produces a recognisable fault. Believing it is word-exchange produces the word-for-word rendering. Believing bilingualism is enough produces fluent text that is wrong about the subject. Believing culture is optional produces the sentence that is accurate and unsayable.The rest of the course is, in a sense, these errors taken one at a time. One sentence, and the belief it exposes · English · The bill was tabled. Word by word · وُضِع مشروع القانون على الطاولة · What it actually says · أُرجئ النظر في مشروع القانون · In British usage to table a bill is to bring it forward; in American usage it is to shelve it. No dictionary lookup of the individual words reaches this. You need to know which parliament you are in — which is the myth about understanding the material, in one sentence. Do this before the next unit

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: What translation is not (cont.)
chunks.text: Take any news paragraph in English and translate it into Arabic twice: once trying to keep the word order, once ignoring it entirely.Put them side by side. The second is almost certainly better. Write one sentence saying what the first one lost — that sentence is the whole subject of this course.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Translation Studies
chunks.text: Translation Studies · دراسات الترجمة · The practice is ancient. The discipline is about fifty years old. lede · People have translated for as long as there have been neighbours who spoke differently. Studying translation as a subject in its own right is recent — and for most of the twentieth century the academy treated it as a language-teaching exercise rather than a field. card · 1972, and a map · James Holmes set out a map of what a discipline of translation would actually contain, and that paper is usually taken as the point where the field began to be one. Before it, translation was studied inside comparative literature, inside contrastive linguistics, inside workshops — never on its own terms.It is now interdisciplinary by nature: linguistics, literature, culture, and increasingly computing all have a claim on it. list · Jakobson's three kinds · Roman Jakobson divided translation into three, and the division still holds: Intralingual — within one language. Rewording, paraphrase, summary, simplifying a contract into plain Arabic. Interlingual — between two languages. What is usually meant by the word, and the subject of this course. Intersemiotic — between sign systems. A novel into a film, a warning into a pictogram, speech into subtitle. list · Translation as a process, not an act · The word names both the process and its product. As a process it has stages, and skipping any of them shows in the result: Read the source until you understand it, and find out what you do not know. Establish its message, intent, form, type and audience.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Translation Studies (cont.)
chunks.text: Draft, holding that message and intent, for the audience the target text will actually have. Conform to the norms of the target language rather than the shape of the source. Revise and check. The same content, three kinds of translation · Source · No unauthorised entry. Intralingual · Only staff may go past this point — same language, different words · Interlingual · ممنوع الدخول لغير المصرَّح لهم · And intersemiotic: the red circle with a bar through it that says the same thing to somebody who reads neither language. All three are translation under Jakobson; only the middle one is what the profession sells. Do this before the next unit · Find a short legal or official sentence in Arabic — a clause from a contract, a notice on a government site. Do all three of Jakobson's kinds on it: reword it in plain Arabic, translate it into English, and describe the sign or icon that would carry it.Note which was hardest. For most people it is the first, which is the useful surprise.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Where the work came from
chunks.text: Where the work came from · لمحة تاريخية · Four moments, and what each of them moved. lede · The history matters here for one reason: in every period, translation is what carried knowledge across a border it could not otherwise cross. The technique changed. That function did not. card · The ancient world · Egypt, Greece and Rome all ran on translation — for trade, for governance, for law. The Rosetta Stone is the emblem: the same decree in three scripts, which is why Egyptian writing could be read again at all. What moved was science, philosophy and literature, and it moved because somebody carried it. card · The Middle Ages · Latin was the language of scholarship, so Greek and Roman work survived in Europe largely by being translated into it, in monasteries, by hand.The Compass's own Translators in History holds the other half of this period, the one the standard account often leaves out: the Arabic translation movement, and the scholars who preserved and advanced the same inheritance. card · The Renaissance · The classics were translated out of Latin and Greek into the languages people actually spoke. That single move — into the vernacular — put ancient learning in front of a wide readership for the first time, and the consequences were not literary but historical. card · The twentieth century

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Where the work came from (cont.)
chunks.text: Translation became a subject. Eugene Nida, working on Bible translation, brought a systematic account of equivalence to it; Holmes gave the field its map; journals, departments and research centres followed.That is the short answer to why this course exists and why it has a reading list. Why the vernacular move was not a small one · Latin · Vulgus vult decipi. Kept in Latin · readable by perhaps two people in a hundred · Into the spoken language · الناس تحب أن تُخدَع · Nothing about the sentence changed except who could read it — and that is the entire content of the Renaissance as far as translation is concerned. Access is not a side effect of translation. It is the point of it. Do this before the next unit · Pick one translator from Translators in History in this site and answer, in three sentences: what did they move, from where to where, and what would not exist if they had not?Keep the answer. You will be asked to write commentary like this for your own work later in the minor.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Equivalence at word level
chunks.text: Equivalence at word level · التكافؤ على مستوى الكلمة · There is no such thing as one word for one word. This unit says exactly why. lede · Mona Baker's account of equivalence starts at the smallest unit and works upward, and this is the bottom of it. The finding is blunt: there is no one-to-one correspondence between words and units of meaning — not even within a single language. card · Words are not the smallest unit · Rebuild is one word carrying two pieces of meaning. Unbreakable is one word carrying three. The piece that cannot be cut further is the morpheme, not the word.So a count of words tells you nothing. English happiness is one word and so is Arabic سعادة; English tennis player is two words and Turkish tenisçi is one. Nothing follows from the counting. list · The four kinds of lexical meaning · Baker separates what a word carries into four. Most translation arguments are really disagreements about which of these is being preserved: Propositional — what it refers to in the world. This is the one that can be true or false, and when a translation is called inaccurate, it is usually this. Expressive — the speaker's attitude. Complain and whine point at the same act; only one of them judges it. Cannot be true or false, and is lost silently. Presupposed — what the word expects around it. Two kinds: selectional (studious needs a human subject) and collocational, which is arbitrary — in English laws are broken, in Arabic they are contradicted.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Equivalence at word level (cont.)
chunks.text: Evoked — what dialect and register the word belongs to. Register varies by field (what is happening), tenor (who is speaking to whom) and mode (speech, writing, screen). list · Two problems you will meet this week · Frequency. A perfect equivalent can still be the wrong word. Arabic شبر is exactly a span — an obsolete English measure almost no reader knows. Correct and useless. Ambiguity. Dictionary entries run to pages. خط is line, path, track or font, and when the surrounding text does not settle it, nothing else will. Same propositional meaning, different expressive meaning · English · Don't complain. Don't whine. What they share · Both point at the same act, so neither is truer than the other — the propositional meaning is identical · What only one has · لا تشتكِ لا تتذمّر · Whine carries the speaker's judgement that the complaining is irritating; complain carries none. Expressive meaning cannot be true or false, which is exactly why it disappears from a translation without anyone noticing it has gone. Do this before the next unit · Take five words from a text you are working on and, for each, write down its propositional meaning and then anything expressive, presupposed or evoked riding along with it.Then translate them. You will find that two or three of the five cannot carry all four kinds across at once, and that you had to choose which to keep. Write down which you chose. That note is what a translation commentary is made of.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Word-level strategies
chunks.text: Word-level strategies · استراتيجيات مستوى الكلمة · Four named moves for when there is no equivalent — and when each one is the right call. lede · When the word is not there in the target language, you do not improvise: you choose from a small set of known moves, and you can say afterwards which one you used. These are Baker's, and they have names for the same reason the surgical instruments do. card · 1 · A more general word · Also called generalisation, and the most common answer to a gap in propositional meaning. You climb one step up the semantic hierarchy and take the wider term.It works across almost any pair of languages, because the hierarchies themselves are not language-specific — every language has a word for the category above. card · 2 · Substitution · Replace a culture-specific item with a target-language item that does not mean the same thing but lands the same way on the reader. You are trading propositional accuracy for effect, knowingly.Most common with measurements, currency and time. Arabic tells time with thirds of an hour and with ليلاً and فجراً; English does neither, and converting is usually right. card · 3 · Loan word, with or without explanation · Also called retention or transliteration: carry the source word across in the target script. Standard for culture-specific items, new concepts and technical terms with no settled equivalent.Gloss it the first time and then use it bare. English took alcohol, algebra and algorithm from Arabic this way centuries ago, and hijab recently. card · 4 · Paraphrase

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Word-level strategies (cont.)
chunks.text: Say what the word means, when no single word will do it. An umbrella for several moves — by a related word, by unrelated words, by a short definition.The cost is length and the loss of any expressive charge the original had. It is the safest strategy and rarely the most elegant one. card · How to choose · Ask what the word is doing in this text. A technical term in a manual wants the loan word and one gloss. A cultural reference in a novel usually wants substitution or paraphrase. A passing mention nobody will remember wants generalisation and no fuss.What you may not do is choose silently. Naming the move is what lets you defend it — and what the commentary in your later courses is assessed on. The loan word, proved by history · Arabic · الكحول الجبر الخوارزمية · Paraphrased instead · a distilled spirit, the reuniting of broken parts, a step-by-step procedure — all accurate, and none of them survived · Borrowed · alcohol algebra algorithm · English took all three from Arabic as loan words, and more recently hijab and jihad. Borrowing is not a failure to translate: for a concept the target language does not yet have, it is often the only move that lets the concept itself arrive. Do this before the next unit · Take four culture-specific items from Kuwaiti life — food, dress, an institution, an occasion. Translate each one four times, once by each strategy.Then decide, for each, which you would actually use and in what kind of text. Sixteen renderings, four decisions, and a reason for each: that is the exercise, and it is also the job.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Collocation
chunks.text: Collocation · التلازم اللفظي · Words keep company. Which company is arbitrary, and it is not the same company in Arabic. lede · Words almost never occur alone, and they are not strung together at random. Some of what governs the stringing is rule — a determiner cannot follow its noun, so beautiful house the is simply wrong. The rest is habit, and habit is where translation goes wrong. card · Why builders do not produce buildings · Authors invent stories and plots, but they do not invent novels. Builders do not produce buildings. No dictionary definition forbids either.Bolinger and Sears gave the only honest reason: we don't say it because we don't say it. That is a collocation — the tendency of certain words to co-occur, semantically arbitrary and not derivable from meaning. list · Near-synonyms do not share company · This is why a thesaurus is dangerous. Each of these is idiomatic on the left and wrong on the right: Break rules — but not break regulations. Waste time — but not squander time. Pay a visit — but not perform a visit. And in Arabic, laws are not broken at all: they are contradicted — يخالف القانون. card · Collocational range · Every word tolerates a certain spread of company. Shrug has almost none — it takes shoulders and little else. Run has an enormous one: a company, a business, a show, a car, a nose.Two things widen the range. Generality: bury takes people, treasure, a head, a face, feelings, memories, while its hyponym entomb takes only people. And number of senses: each sense of a word attracts its own set of companions. card · What this means at the desk

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Collocation (cont.)
chunks.text: You do not translate the word. You translate the collocation, and you choose the target equivalent that fits the whole unit.A verb with a wide range in English will not have one wide-ranging counterpart in Arabic. It will have several, and picking between them is the work. One English verb, four Arabic verbs · English · deliver a letter deliver a speech deliver news deliver a blow · One verb, held · deliver looks like a single word with a single equivalent. It is not. What Arabic requires · يسلّم خطاباً يلقي خطبةً ينقل أخباراً يوجّه ضربةً. Four different verbs, because Arabic has no verb with deliver's collocational range. Now try deliver a verdict yourself — and notice that you reached for the collocation, not the dictionary. Do this before the next unit · Take one high-range English verb — run, hold, make, take — and collect eight of its collocations from real text.Translate all eight. Count how many distinct Arabic verbs you needed. That number is the gap between a word and a collocation, and it is why a bilingual dictionary alone cannot do this work.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Idioms and fixed expressions
chunks.text: Idioms and fixed expressions · التعابير الاصطلاحية · Frozen, often opaque, and the place a confident translator does the most damage. lede · Collocations are flexible: deliver a letter, delivery of a letter, a letter has been delivered are all fine. Idioms and fixed expressions sit at the far end of that scale — frozen in form, and often opaque in meaning. list · What you may not do to an idiom · The long and the short of it means the basic facts. Touch it anywhere and it breaks: Reorder it — not the short and the long of it. Delete from it — not spill beans. Add to it — not face the classical music. Swap a word — not the tall and the short of it, not bury a hatchet. Change its grammar — not the music was faced. split · Idiom or fixed expression? Idiom · تعبير اصطلاحي · Frozen and opaque. Bury the hatchet, pull a fast one, fill the bill. You cannot reach the meaning from the words. Fixed expression · تعبير ثابت · Frozen but usually transparent. As a matter of fact, ladies and gentlemen, all the best, and proverbs like practice what you preach. Still taken as one unit. list · How to notice one before you mistranslate it · The first difficulty is not translating the idiom. It is realising there is one. Three signals: It violates truth conditions — it is raining cats and dogs, food for thought. It is ill-formed — by and large, the world and his wife, trip the light fantastic. It opens with like — like a bat out of hell, like two peas in a pod.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Idioms and fixed expressions (cont.)
chunks.text: And the general rule: the less sense an expression makes in its context, the more likely it is an idiom and not a failure of your vocabulary. list · Five strategies · In descending order of how much of the original survives: An idiom of similar meaning and similar form. An idiom of similar meaning but dissimilar form — usually the best available. Borrowing the source idiom. Paraphrase — the most common, and the one that loses the flavour. Omission of the whole idiom — legitimate, and the one to be able to justify. card · Why this is the case for translating into your own language. Competence in a foreign language almost never reaches the point where you can feel when an idiom may be bent and when it may not. That sensitivity is a native one, and it is the usual argument for translating into your first language rather than out of it.Even then two problems remain: recognising the idiom, and carrying its meaning across when the target language has no counterpart — because idioms are culturally specific, and even a counterpart that exists may be used in a different register or context. Five idioms to identify before translating · English · I urge you to speak your mind and not to pull any punches. The trap · Word-for-word gives a speech about a mind and an instruction about hitting. Both are grammatical, and both are nonsense. What is meant · أدعوك إلى قول ما تعتقده بصراحة ودون مجاملة

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Idioms and fixed expressions (cont.)
chunks.text: The other four on the slide are driving like a bat out of hell, the world and his wife were there, in a nutshell, and spilled the beans. Identify, then interpret, then translate — always that order. Do this before the next unit · Take the five sentences above. For each: name the idiom, write its meaning in plain English, then translate the sentence into Arabic.Then say which of the five strategies you used, and why. Expect paraphrase most of the time — and notice what the paraphrase costs.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Grammatical equivalence
chunks.text: Grammatical equivalence · التكافؤ النحوي · Grammar forces you to say things the source never said — and to drop things it did. lede · Vocabulary is not the only thing that shapes what a language can report. Its grammar obliges speakers to mark certain distinctions every time they open their mouths — time, number, gender, person — and every language makes a different selection from that set. card · Why grammar is harder to move than vocabulary. Grammar runs on two dimensions: morphology, the shape of words, and syntax, the order of the parts.A language will absorb a new word overnight. It will not absorb a new grammatical category. So where the two systems differ, the translator cannot borrow — something has to be added to the target text or dropped from it, and that changes the information content. list · The five notions to check · Number. Countability is universal; grammatical number is not. English has singular and plural; Arabic has singular, dual and plural; Chinese marks it lexically or not at all. Gender. English marks it only in the third person. In Arabic the noun's gender also reshapes its verbs and adjectives, so a first-person sentence with no gender in English forces a choice in Arabic. Person. Participant roles, through a closed set of pronouns. Many European languages add a politeness dimension English does not have. Tense and aspect. Two different things: tense locates the event in time, aspect describes its distribution — finished or not, continuing or momentary.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Grammatical equivalence (cont.)
chunks.text: Voice. The relation between verb and subject. Written English uses the passive heavily, and most languages have their own ways of building agentless clauses that do not map onto it. card · The gender problem, in one pair of sentences · I am a student in the English department, and I specialise in Translation Studies. Nothing there tells you the speaker's gender — but Arabic will not let you write the sentence without deciding.Add even though I am a father of four and it is settled. Add even though I was nine months pregnant and it is settled the other way. When the text gives you nothing: read the whole thing for gendered expressions, biological detail, relational nouns (husband, wife) or a title of address. If it still gives you nothing, you are making a decision, and you should know that you are. list · The error your examiner will find first · Literal renderings of am / is / are / was / were into يكون. Arabic does not need the copula: She is kind — not هي تكون طيبة, but هي طيبة. I am leaving now — not أنا أكون مغادراً الآن, but سأغادر الآن. They are put in the same situation — not هم يكونون موضوعين, but يوضعون في الموقف نفسه. The dual, and what English has to add · Arabic · ويختار المحكمان المعيَّنان على هذا النحو المحكَّم الثالث · What English lacks · There is no dual in English. The arbitrators alone would lose the count. English, with the addition · and the two arbitrators thus appointed select the third arbitrator

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Grammatical equivalence (cont.)
chunks.text: The word two is not in the Arabic. It is carried by the form of المحكمان itself. English has to add a word to say what Arabic says with a suffix — and in an arbitration clause, failing to add it changes the legal meaning. Do this before the next unit · Find an Arabic legal or administrative paragraph containing at least one dual and one passive. Translate it into English.Then mark your own output: every place you added information the Arabic did not state, and every place you dropped information it did. Both lists will be non-empty. That is not a failure — it is what grammatical difference costs, and naming it is the skill.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Literary and technical texts
chunks.text: Literary and technical texts · النصوص الأدبية والتقنية · Two kinds of writing that ask for two different kinds of faithfulness. lede · Before the genre units, the distinction they rest on. A literary text is written to convey ideas and to produce a feeling; a ghost story is meant to frighten you. It addresses the mind and the heart at once, and a translation that delivers only the first has failed at the job. list · What literary writing is like · Imaginative, and subjective. Free, less formal, personal — it follows no standard format. Tends to be long, and may be written in first, second or third person. Its genres: prose fiction and non-fiction, novels, novellas, poetry, drama. list · The three hard problems · Each returns in the units after this one: Style. In literature the manner is part of the content. Style is what tells one writer from another, so it gets the same attention as meaning — not less. Literal against free. The ideal is to translate everything, no more and no less. No two languages have the same structure, so in practice you will sometimes expand and sometimes condense, and you should know which you are doing. Standard against dialect. A novelist uses dialect on purpose — to place a character geographically, to mark identity, to characterise. Your job is to find how that purpose can survive, not to reproduce the dialect. card · And culture

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Literary and technical texts (cont.)
chunks.text: Every group has its own way of living, eating, dressing and speaking, and the target readers may share none of it. Culture-bound terms are not decoration in a literary text; they are often what the passage is about.The four word-level strategies from unit 5 are the tools here. Which one you reach for depends on whether the item is the subject of the sentence or scenery in it. The same fact, two kinds of text · Technical · Ambient temperature fell to 4 C overnight. Literary · By morning the cold had got into everything. What each one has to keep · The first must keep the number. The second must keep the feeling — and may change the number, or drop it. Both can be faithful. They are faithful to different things, and choosing which kind of faithfulness a text is asking for is the decision this whole course is training. Do this before the next unit · Take one paragraph of a novel and one paragraph of a manual, both in English. Translate both into Arabic.Then write two sentences: what you protected in the first, and what you protected in the second. If the answers are the same, one of the two translations is wrong.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Literary translation and style
chunks.text: Literary translation and style · الترجمة الأدبية والأسلوب · Style is not decoration on top of the meaning. It is a second thing to translate. lede · Style can mean the conventions of a genre — how business or medical writing goes — or it can mean one writer's own way of putting things. In literary translation the second sense is the one that matters: not what the author writes, but the manner of it. The verbal identity of a writer. card · Two definitions worth carrying · Boase-Beier (2006) treats style as the outcome of choice — and argues that the translator's own style will inevitably enter the target text. You do not have the option of not having a style.Baker (2000) calls style a thumb-print expressed in a range of linguistic and non-linguistic features, and insists it is a matter of patterning: recurring habits across a text, not a single striking sentence. list · Where to look for it · Lexical choices · Preferred syntax · How ideas are ordered · Choice of verb tense · Use of metaphor · list · Elements that cause trouble · Each of these carries information about the character or the narrator, which is why flattening it loses more than it looks: Diction, expansive or economical. Tight and efficient, or elaborate and long-winded? When the author switches, ask why. It often marks a character's background. Vocabulary. Simple or fancy; technical, flowery, colloquial, punning, obscure. It tells the reader what the character's education is without stating it.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Literary translation and style (cont.)
chunks.text: Sentence structure. A run of short sentences reads as agitation; long ones read as composure. Interruptions and digressions say something about who gets to hold a conversation. Dialogue, tone, figures of speech, allusion and intertextuality. card · The two-sided risk · Stylistic features are language-specific. Following an Arabic word order closely into English produces something unnatural and hard to read — it will be taken as a bad translation, and the fault will be attributed to the author.But ironing the style out entirely gives target readers no sense of how the original reads, which is also a loss. There is no rule that resolves this. There is only the judgement, made consciously, and defended in the commentary. Style as patterning, not a single sentence · English · He waited. The room was cold. Nobody came. Smoothed out · انتظر في غرفة باردة دون أن يأتي أحد — accurate, and the three short sentences have become one composed one · Pattern kept · انتظر. كانت الغرفة باردة. لم يأتِ أحد. Nothing in the first version is wrong. But the clipped rhythm was carrying the character's state, and joining the sentences deletes it without deleting a single word of meaning. That is precisely Baker's point about patterning. Do this before the next unit · Take half a page from a novel you know. Before translating, write five lines on its style using the list above — diction, vocabulary, sentence structure, tone, figures of speech.Then translate, and check your translation against your own five lines. Anywhere they disagree, you changed the author's thumb-print. Decide whether you meant to.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Technical translation
chunks.text: Technical translation · الترجمة التقنية · The largest field by volume, and the one where a wrong word has consequences. lede · Almost every technological advance reaches anybody outside the room it was invented in by being translated. Byrne puts it plainly: the inventions that changed ordinary life were accompanied at almost every step by translation in its capacity as a vehicle for disseminating scientific and technical knowledge. card · What counts as technical · Wider than it sounds. The sciences — medicine, physics, astronomy, chemistry. Applied technology — computing, engineering. And subjects nobody calls scientific: geography, economics, architecture.If a field has terms of its own that outsiders use differently or not at all, translating it is technical translation. list · How technical language behaves · It is specialised, and becomes more so over time rather than less. It is economical — it says things in as few linguistic means as it can. It avoids the associations of ordinary language and defines its terms precisely, which is the opposite of what literary language does. card · The same word in three fields · Depression in psychology is an illness. In economics it is a prolonged contraction. In meteorology it is an area of low pressure.One term, three domains, and a different concept in each. Knowing which field you are in is not background knowledge here — it is the translation. list · Two kinds of lexical trouble · The problems fall neatly into two, and the second is the dangerous one:

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Technical translation (cont.)
chunks.text: Terms you do not know at all, because they appear only in technical contexts. Unpleasant, but visible — you know to go and look them up. Terms you do know, from ordinary contexts, being used in a specialised way. You feel no difficulty, translate confidently, and are wrong. Nothing warns you. Two ordinary-looking words in a medical text · English · These tests specify and diagnose the allergenic or harmful substances, as in the case of contact eczema. The ordinary reading · contact read as everyday contact, and allergenic collapsed into allergic — two words that look harmless · The terms · المواد المحسِّسة أو الضارة، كما الحال في أكزيما التماس. Allergic describes the reaction; allergenic describes the substance that causes it. أكزيما التماس is a named condition, not a description. Both are the second kind of trouble: familiar words, specialised use, no warning. Do this before the next unit · Find a short technical paragraph in a field you do not work in. Before translating, list every word you are confident about.Now check five of them in a specialist source. At least one will not mean what you assumed. That word is the whole lesson of this unit — the danger is not the vocabulary you know you lack.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Journalistic texts: the headline
chunks.text: Journalistic texts: the headline · ترجمة العناوين الصحفية · Headlinese is not English. It has its own grammar, and Arabic does not share it. lede · A news text is built from three parts — headline, lead paragraph, news story — and the first of them is written in something that is barely the same language. card · Headlinese · The headline is the most conspicuous thing on a newspaper page, and its difficulty is syntactic, lexical and stylistic at once. The standard description is telegraphic and elliptical: it leaves out everything it can get away with leaving out.English headlines are frequently not complete sentences. Some are nothing but a string of nouns. list · What gets dropped, and what gets used · Articles, the copula, and auxiliaries go first. Simple tenses rather than continuous or perfect ones — US launches air raids in Iraq, not has launched. Noun stacks stand in for whole clauses. Which means the reader is expected to reconstruct the proposition — and so is the translator, before a word is rendered. card · Why the Arabic headline is usually longer · Arabic headlines do not work by the same compression. Rendering an English noun stack word-for-word produces something that is not a headline in Arabic and often not intelligible.So addition is standard practice here, not a liberty: you add what the target reader needs in order to recover what the English reader recovered for free. card · Do this before you translate any headline

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Journalistic texts: the headline (cont.)
chunks.text: Write out the full proposition in plain English first. Mustang Referral Customer Complaint unpacks to: there is a complaint; the complaint concerns the Mustang customer referral programme.Only then translate. Headlines are the one place where translating before you have paraphrased is almost guaranteed to fail. Four nouns, and what Arabic has to supply · English headline · Mustang Referral Customer Complaint · Word for word · a string of four nouns that names no event and forms no Arabic headline · Arabic, with additions · شكوى زبون فورد موستنج من برنامج الإحالة · Two things were added. Ford, because an Arabic reader may not know Mustang is a Ford. And programme, because referral alone does not say that a scheme is meant. Neither is in the English; both are needed to say the same thing. Do this before the next unit · Take five English headlines from today. For each, write the full proposition in plain English, then translate into Arabic.Underline every word in your Arabic that has no counterpart in the English. Then justify each one in a few words. If you cannot justify it, it is not an addition — it is an invention.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Journalistic texts: story structure
chunks.text: Journalistic texts: story structure · بنية الخبر الصحفي · A news story is built to be cut from the bottom. Knowing that changes how you translate it. lede · Beyond the headline, a news story has a shape, and the shape is chosen by the kind of story it is. Three are standard: the inverted pyramid, the hourglass, and straight narrative. card · The inverted pyramid · The most basic structure, and older than you would guess: it dates from a time when reporters filed by telegraph and the wire could be cut mid-transmission. Put the most important thing first, and descend from there.It reverses chronological order — the outcome comes first and the background last. list · Why editors like it · The reader gets the important elements at once and can decide whether to continue. An editor can cut from the bottom to fit the space, and lose nothing significant. Online, updates can be added without rebuilding the story. It forces the reporter to rank the elements and write quickly, holding back minor detail. list · What it costs · It gives the reader no reason to reach the end. It discourages well-made endings, and treats the later paragraphs as expendable. It can push the writer towards oversimplifying. card · The hourglass, and narrative

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Journalistic texts: story structure (cont.)
chunks.text: The hourglass is a compromise: the main facts first in descending importance, as in a pyramid, then a turn into chronological narrative with room for detail, dialogue and background. It suits police stories, disasters and trials — anything that has a sequence worth telling.Narrative proper keeps the events in order from the start, and is the structure literary journalism borrows. card · What this means for you · The structure is information design, not decoration, and it is a target-language decision as much as a source-language one.Translating a pyramid story faithfully means the Arabic must also survive being cut from the bottom. If your rendering buries the key fact in paragraph three because the Arabic sentence ran better that way, you have translated the words and broken the text. Where the important fact sits · Pyramid lead · Twelve people were rescued yesterday after a fire broke out in a residential tower in Salmiya. Reordered for flow · After a fire broke out in Salmiya, and after crews had worked through the night, twelve people were rescued — natural, and now uncuttable · Pyramid kept · أُنقذ اثنا عشر شخصاً أمس إثر حريق شبّ في برج سكني بالسالمية. Both carry every fact. Only the second can lose its final paragraphs without losing the news. Sentence order in a news translation is not a stylistic preference — it is part of what the text is for. Do this before the next unit

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Journalistic texts: story structure (cont.)
chunks.text: Take an English news story of six or more paragraphs. Identify its structure, then translate it.Now delete your last two paragraphs and read what remains. If it is still a complete, accurate story, you preserved the structure. If something essential has gone, you reorganised the text without noticing.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Terminology and translation technology
chunks.text: Terminology and translation technology · المصطلحات وتقنيات الترجمة · A discipline about concepts, and the tools that keep decisions from being made twice. lede · Terminology has no single agreed definition, partly because it borrowed from older fields — semantics, lexicology, lexicography. What forced it into existence is simpler: science and technology produced concepts faster than languages produced words for them. card · Two senses of the word · Originally, terminology meant the technical terms used in an art, a science or a specialised subject — a sense still alive in English.Later it came to mean the study of those terms: the systematic identification of the terms belonging to a field, and of the concepts they stand for. card · The working definition · A discipline that systematically identifies specialised terms in the context where they are used, analyses the concepts they represent in that context, and where necessary creates and standardises terms to meet a real need for expression.It is a linguistic discipline with theoretical guidelines and defined working methods, which is what separates it from collecting vocabulary. list · The three tools · Translation technology is the software around the process. Three things do most of the work: Machine translation. Software translating automatically. Early systems were rule-based, then statistical; neural systems are markedly better. Still not a match for a human on nuance or context — but genuinely faster and cheaper.

chunks.where: Learn › Translation Minor › ENGL 180 Principles of Translation
chunks.title: Terminology and translation technology (cont.)
chunks.text: Translation memory. Stores what you have already translated so it can be reused. Its real value is consistency across a long document or a repeat client, not speed. Terminology management. Glossaries and termbases, so that a term decided once is used the same way by everyone afterwards. card · The honest position on machines · Machine translation has made real progress and will keep making it. It still cannot match a human on nuance or on sensitivity to context.What follows from that is not that the tools are useless. It is that someone has to be able to tell when the output is wrong — which takes more knowledge than producing it, not less. That is the job the rest of this course is preparing you for. Why a termbase exists · English · informed consent · The near-enough word · موافقة — consent, which is what a patient gives to anything at all · The term · موافقة مستنيرة · These are different things in law: one is agreement, the other is agreement after the risks have been explained and understood. A term decided once, recorded with its source, and reused is the entire argument for terminology management — so that the next translator inherits the decision instead of making it again, differently. Do this before the next unit · Build a ten-term glossary for one field — banking, medicine, aviation, whatever you may translate in. For each: the English term, the Arabic term, a one-line definition, and where you got it.That last column is what makes it a termbase rather than a list.
