chunks.text: In the English text of the Treaty of Waitangi, Māori chiefs cede “all the rights and powers of sovereignty”. The Māori text most of them signed gives the Queen kāwanatanga — governorship, a word coined from governor — while promising the chiefs tino rangatiratanga, full chieftainship. The two texts do different things. New Zealand is still working out the consequences in its courts and its tribunal. Pixar re-made 28 graphics across 45 shots for different countries — hockey became football in some of them. Domestication, done in the image itself. The joke is “food a child hates”; the food was only the carrier. /Film · https://slashfilm.com/727914/why-inside-out-changed-so-many-scenes-for-its-overseas-release · SoraNews24 · https://soranews24.com/2015/07/24/pixar-alters-inside-outs-visuals-for-japanese-release-removes-broccoli/amp/ · Film · 2016 · Zootopia's newsreader changes species · The news anchor in Zootopia is a moose in the US and Canada, a koala in Australia and New Zealand, a panda in China, a jaguar in Brazil, a tanuki in Japan and a corgi in the UK — each voiced by a local broadcaster. He was treated for an overdose. He had a brain haemorrhage, and was left quadriplegic; the settlement was about $71 million. intoxicado · poisoned, sick from food · intoxicated · drunk or drugged · A false friend, in a setting where nobody had time to check. chunks.text: Collocations · التَّلازُم اللَّفظيّ · English → Arabic · A collocation is a pairing the language has already made for you. Agreement takes a different Arabic verb depending on which verb stands beside it in English, and choosing the wrong one is not a grammar mistake — it is the mistake that marks a text as translated. The English verb does not decide the Arabic verb. The stage of the agreement does: arriving at it, signing it, or entering into it are three different moments, and Arabic names them separately. reach an agreement · يتوصل إلى اتفاق · Arriving at it after negotiation. توصّل إلى carries the sense of getting there. sign an agreement · يوقّع اتفاقية · The physical act, and note the shift to اتفاقية — the formal instrument rather than the understanding. enter into an agreement · يدخل في اتفاق · Becoming party to it. Legal and commercial register. bilateral agreement · اتفاق ثنائي · Two parties. ثنائي is the standard diplomatic adjective. preliminary agreement · اتفاق مبدئي · Agreed in principle, not yet final. binding agreement · اتفاق ملزم · ملزم is the legal term of art for what obliges the parties.

chunks.title: Collocations
chunks.text: Collocations · التَّلازُم اللَّفظيّ · Arabic → English · The same problem, running the other way. Arabic اتخذ covers a range that English splits between make, take and adopt, and no rule predicts which. The object chooses the verb. Rendering every اتخذ as take produces English that is grammatical and wrong: take a decision exists in British usage but make a decision is the unmarked choice, and take a policy is not English at all. اتخذ قرارًا · make a decision · The default. Take a decision is heard in British and institutional English; make is safer. اتخذ إجراءات · take measures · Also take action, take steps. Here English does use take. اتخذ موقفًا · take a position adopt a position · Adopt is the more formal and more diplomatic of the two. اتخذ خطوات · take steps · Fixed pairing; make steps is not English. اتخذ سياسة · adopt a policy · Only adopt. Neither make nor take collocates with policy here.

chunks.title: Discourse markers
chunks.text: Discourse markers · أدَوات الرَّبط · Both directions · Connectors are the joints of an argument. They are rarely one-to-one, they differ sharply in register, and Arabic prose joins clauses far more often than English does — so a marker-for-marker rendering produces English that sounds relentlessly linked. Two habits worth unlearning. First, ومع ذلك and مع ذلك are not interchangeable with every however: English often signals contrast by position and punctuation alone. Second, Arabic will happily open a sentence with و where English simply starts a new sentence — the right rendering is often nothing at all. however · ومع ذلك غير أنّ · Concession. غير أنّ is the more formal. therefore · لذلك ومن ثَمّ · Consequence. ومن ثَمّ belongs to academic and legal prose. moreover · علاوة على ذلك · Adding weight to the same line of argument. nevertheless · مع ذلك ومع هذا · Stronger concession than however; the obstacle is conceded and passed. in contrast · في المقابل · Sets two things side by side rather than conceding. on the other hand · من ناحية أخرى · Expects a on the one hand somewhere before it; Arabic is less strict about the pair. as a result · ونتيجة لذلك · Result, stated plainly. in addition · بالإضافة إلى ذلك · Neutral addition; lighter than moreover. accordingly · وبناءً عليه · Formal, and common in legal and administrative Arabic.

chunks.title: Context-dependent expressions
chunks.text: Context-dependent expressions · تَعابير رَهينة السِّياق · Arabic → English · Some expressions have no translation at all until you know who is saying them, to whom, and when. Storing one equivalence for them is the error — it teaches a phrase that will be wrong most of the times it is used. بالعافية is the clearest case. It is a well-wishing formula built on health, and what it means in English is decided entirely by the moment. بالعافية — said to someone eating · Enjoy your meal Bon appétit · Literal gloss: with health. The function is a table courtesy, and English uses a borrowed French phrase for it as often as an English one. بالعافية — said to someone who has just bathed · — often nothing at all · English has no formula for this moment. The honest rendering may be silence, or a neutral pleasantry, depending on the text. Forcing enjoy your meal here is nonsense. بالعافية — said to someone working hard · Keep it up More power to you · Now it is encouragement. Same three syllables, a different speech act. الله يعطيك العافية · Thank you for your effort Well done Thanks for your trouble. A thanks-and-blessing said to someone who has done work for you. The English depends on the relationship: a colleague, a shopkeeper and a superior take three different renderings.

chunks.title: Speech acts
chunks.text: Speech acts · الأفعال الكَلاميّة · English → Arabic · Ask what the sentence is doing, not what it says. A request, an apology, a refusal and an offer each have their own formulas in each language, and politeness does not map degree for degree. English marks politeness largely by grammatical distance — could you possibly, I was wondering if. Arabic marks it more by lexical choice and by blessing formulas. A literal rendering of English hedging often lands as odd rather than polite. Could you possibly send me the report? هل يمكنك إرسال التقرير؟ Neutral and direct. Appropriate between colleagues; it loses the English hedging, which is usually the right call. Could you possibly send me the report? هل بالإمكان إرسال التقرير؟ More impersonal — the agent disappears. Useful in institutional writing where naming the person would be too pointed. Could you possibly send me the report? هل تتكرم بإرسال التقرير؟ Markedly deferential: تتكرم casts the act as a kindness being granted. Right for a superior; obsequious between equals. I'm afraid that won't be possible. للأسف، هذا غير ممكن · A refusal. English softens with I'm afraid; Arabic with للأسف. The softener is not decoration — removing it changes the act from a refusal into a rebuff.

chunks.title: مال البخيل ياكله العيار
chunks.text: مال البخيل ياكله العيار · ما يجمعه البخيل ويحرم نفسه منه، ينتهي غالبًا في يد غيره، كالمسرف أو المحتال. English has no fixed proverb with this exact point, so the best rendering states it plainly: the hoarding brings the miser nothing, because another person enjoys it. Literally: “the miser’s money is eaten by the rogue”. العيّار is a wastrel or trickster — the opposite of the careful miser. Answer: What a miser hoards, someone else will squander. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اللي ماله أول ماله تالي
chunks.text: اللي ماله أول ماله تالي · من لا يعرف أصله ولا يحفظ ماضيه لا يُرتجى له مستقبل. أول here is a person’s origins and history, تالي what comes after them. The English keeps both halves and the warning. Said of someone who forgets or disowns where they come from. Answer: He who has no past has no future. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: يغطه فبالبحر ويطلعه ناشف
chunks.text: يغطه فبالبحر ويطلعه ناشف · شخص شديد الدهاء يستطيع أن يخدع غيره دون أن يشعر به أحد. Dipping someone in the sea and bringing him out dry is an impossible trick; the proverb uses it for a person who can pull off any deception. Literally: “he dunks him in the sea and brings him out dry”. Usually said with grudging admiration — or as a warning. Answer: He could fool anyone without them ever noticing. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: يا شين السرج عالبقر
chunks.text: يا شين السرج عالبقر · زينة أو منصب يوضع على من لا يليق به، فيزداد منظره سوءًا. A saddle belongs on a horse; on a cow it only looks absurd. Both proverbs say finery does not change what is underneath. Literally: “how ugly the saddle on the cow”. Said when someone is given a role, title or look that does not suit them. Answer: Fine feathers don’t make fine birds. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إذا طاح الجمل كثرت سكاكينه
chunks.text: إذا طاح الجمل كثرت سكاكينه · إذا ضعف القوي أو سقط من مكانته، كثر من يهاجمه ويستغل ضعفه. English has an old proverb with the same picture: once the great thing is down, everybody comes to cut a piece. A camel was only slaughtered once it fell; the knives gather around it. Said when a powerful person loses position. Answer: When the tree falls, everyone runs to it with an axe. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: مد رجولك على قد لحافك
chunks.text: مد رجولك على قد لحافك · عِش في حدود إمكانياتك ولا تنفق فوق طاقتك. This one has a genuine English equivalent: plan what you make by what you have. “Live within your means” says the same in plain words. The Kuwaiti image is a blanket that is only so long: stretch your legs past it and they are in the cold. Answer: Cut your coat according to your cloth. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: اللي ما يعرف الصقر يشويه
chunks.text: اللي ما يعرف الصقر يشويه · من لا يعرف قيمة الشيء يسيء استعماله ويضيّعه. To someone who doesn’t know falconry, a prized hunting falcon is just a bird to cook. The best English states the idea directly. In Kuwaiti and Gulf culture a trained falcon is precious and prestigious; grilling one is the height of ignorance. Answer: Those who don’t know its worth will waste it. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اشعلم المعيدي باكل الزبيدي
chunks.text: اشعلم المعيدي باكل الزبيدي · من لم يعتد الشيء النفيس لا يعرف قيمته ولا يقدّره. The point is that he has never known the fine thing, so he cannot value it. English has no fixed proverb for exactly this, so the meaning is stated. الزبيدي is silver pomfret, Kuwait’s most prized fish. The proverb asks how an outsider to it could appreciate it. Answer: He can’t appreciate what he has never known. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: ما يعرف رأسه من كرياسه
chunks.text: ما يعرف رأسه من كرياسه · شديد الجهل أو الارتباك، لا يميّز أبسط الأمور. English has its own body-part idioms for complete confusion; this one keeps the sense without the crudeness. كرياس is an old word for a latrine. The rhyme رأسه/كرياسه is what makes it stick. Answer: He doesn’t know which way is up. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: ما يعرف كوعه من بوعه
chunks.text: ما يعرف كوعه من بوعه · جاهل جدًا لا يعرف أبسط الأشياء. English has a near-identical idiom built on the same body-part contrast. كوع and بوع are two small bones whose names are easy to mix up; the rhyme makes the confusion sound comic. Answer: He doesn’t know his elbow from his backside. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: واللي بالجدر يطلعه الملاس
chunks.text: واللي بالجدر يطلعه الملاس · ما في داخل الإنسان أو الأمر سيظهر في النهاية. Whatever is in the pot, the ladle brings it up: a person’s true nature shows in the end. English has no fixed proverb with this exact image. الجدر is the cooking pot and الملاس the ladle. Often said of a person’s character showing through. Answer: What’s inside will always come out. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: انطر يا حمار على ما يجيك الربيع
chunks.text: انطر يا حمار على ما يجيك الربيع · انتظار شيء لن يأتي قريبًا، أو وعد بلا جدوى. The proverb is sarcastic: the wait is long and probably pointless. English expresses that with “Don’t hold your breath.” A hungry donkey is told to wait for the spring grass — a long time with nothing to eat. Answer: Don’t hold your breath. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: أقوله ثور يقولي احلبوه
chunks.text: أقوله ثور يقولي احلبوه · شخص لا يفهم ما يُقال له، أو يصرّ على رأيه رغم وضوح الحقيقة. You cannot milk a bull; the reply shows he isn’t listening at all. The English idiom names that frustration. Said in exasperation when someone keeps answering something that wasn’t said. Answer: It’s like talking to a brick wall. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: من قال “ها” سمع
chunks.text: من قال “ها” سمع · من يستفز غيره أو يتكلم عليه فليتوقع الرد بالمثل. The proverb warns that provocation gets an answer. English says it with “dish it out”. “ها” stands for any remark or taunt; whoever starts it will hear one back. Answer: If you dish it out, expect to get it back. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: مع الخيل يا شقرة
chunks.text: مع الخيل يا شقرة · شخص يتبع الجماعة بلا رأي مستقل. Shaqra (a chestnut mare) just runs where the other horses run. English uses the herd for the same idea. Usually said with a smile about someone who joins in without knowing why. Answer: Following the herd. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لا تبوق لا تخاف
chunks.text: لا تبوق لا تخاف · إذا لم ترتكب خطأً فلا داعي للخوف. تبوق is Kuwaiti for “steal”. The proverb says only the guilty need fear being caught. A good example of a Kuwaiti word looking like a different standard Arabic one. Answer: If you have nothing to hide, you have nothing to fear. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: الناس للناس والكل بالله
chunks.text: الناس للناس والكل بالله · الناس يحتاج بعضهم إلى بعض، والاعتماد في النهاية على الله. The English carries the first half: nobody gets by alone. The second half, reliance on God, can be added if the context needs it. Said to encourage helping others, or to thank someone who helped. Answer: No man is an island. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: لا فات الفوت ما ينفع الصوت
chunks.text: لا فات الفوت ما ينفع الصوت · إذا فات الأوان فلا فائدة من الصياح أو الندم. Once the chance is gone, complaining changes nothing. Note that لا here means إذا, a common Kuwaiti use. الفوت is the moment that has passed; الصوت the shouting afterwards. Answer: It’s no use crying over spilt milk. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: أبو طبيع ما يوز من طبعه
chunks.text: أبو طبيع ما يوز من طبعه · صاحب الطبع لا يتخلى عن طبعه بسهولة. Both say a person’s nature does not change. يوز is Kuwaiti for يجوز, here “give up”. Often said with a sigh when someone does the same thing again. Answer: A leopard can’t change its spots. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: لا بغيت صاحبك دوم حاسبه كل يوم
chunks.text: لا بغيت صاحبك دوم حاسبه كل يوم · إذا أردت أن تدوم الصداقة، فسوِّ الحسابات المالية أولًا بأول. English has the exact proverb: settle accounts promptly and friendships last. Another case where Kuwaiti لا means إذا. Answer: Short reckonings make long friends. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: لا حبتك عيني ما ضامك الدهر
chunks.text: لا حبتك عيني ما ضامك الدهر · إذا أحببتك ووقفت معك، فلن يصيبك ضرر ما دمت إلى جانبك. A promise of protection: whoever I love, I stand by. English has no fixed proverb, so the meaning is said directly. عيني here is “I myself”; الدهر is time or fate. Answer: As long as I’m on your side, nothing can harm you. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لا حجت البقر على قرونها
chunks.text: لا حجت البقر على قرونها · شيء لن يحدث أبدًا. Both name an impossible event. “Till the cows come home” is the trap: long, but not never. Again لا means إذا: “when the cows make the pilgrimage on their horns”. Answer: When pigs fly. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: لا صار حبيبك عسل لا تاكله كله
chunks.text: لا صار حبيبك عسل لا تاكله كله · لا تستغل طيبة صديقك وكرمه حتى تستنفده. If your friend is sweet as honey, don’t eat it all: kindness used up is lost. English needs a plain rendering. The first لا is “if”, the second is “don’t” — a classic trap for readers of standard Arabic. Answer: Don’t take advantage of a good friend. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: مداح نفسه يبي له رفسه
chunks.text: مداح نفسه يبي له رفسه · من يمدح نفسه بإفراط يستحق التوبيخ. English has a fixed proverb with the same judgment. The Kuwaiti one adds a rhyme (مداح/رفسه) and a kick. Said, half joking, to someone talking up their own achievements. Answer: Self-praise is no recommendation. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: من طمع طبع
chunks.text: من طمع طبع · الطمع يؤدي إلى الخسارة والهلاك. In Kuwaiti طبع means sank or drowned: the greedy one goes under. The English proverb carries the same warning. A seafaring image: an overloaded boat sinks. Answer: Grasp all, lose all. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: ما يمدح السوق إلا من ربح فيه
chunks.text: ما يمدح السوق إلا من ربح فيه · يمدح الإنسان الشيء الذي استفاد منه. English has an old proverb with the same point: we praise what has served us. Said when someone’s praise is clearly coloured by what they gained. Answer: Everyone speaks well of the bridge that carries them over. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: من طلع من داره قل مقداره
chunks.text: من طلع من داره قل مقداره · من يبتعد عن بيته وأهله يفقد مكانته وقدره. The proverb is about status: at home people know who you are. English has no fixed match. Rhymes on داره/مقداره. Answer: Away from home, you lose your standing. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: إسأل مجرب ولا تسأل طبيب
chunks.text: إسأل مجرب ولا تسأل طبيب · خبرة من جرّب أنفع أحيانًا من المعرفة النظرية. The doctor stands for book knowledge; the proverb prefers lived experience. Used well beyond medicine — for any practical question. Answer: Experience is the best teacher. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إش حادك يا المسمار؟ قال المطرقة
chunks.text: إش حادك يا المسمار؟ قال المطرقة · الإنسان يفعل الأمر الصعب لأنه مُجبر عليه. The nail does not go in by choice — the hammer drives it. English says pressure leaves no choice. Usually the answer to “why did you do that?” Answer: Needs must when the devil drives. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إصرف ما في الجيب يأتيك ما في الغيب
chunks.text: إصرف ما في الجيب يأتيك ما في الغيب · أنفق وكن كريمًا، ولا تقلق كثيرًا بشأن الغد، فالرزق آتٍ. Its meaning shifts with context: as generosity, or as trust that provision will come. The English captures the trust. The rhyme الجيب/الغيب carries it. Answer: Tomorrow will take care of itself. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: أضبط ساعتك على الملا
chunks.text: أضبط ساعتك على الملا · شخص منضبط جدًا في مواعيده. English has an almost identical idiom for someone who is always exactly on time. Literally: “set your watch by the mulla” — someone whose timing never slips. Answer: You could set your watch by him. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إكل اللي تبيه وإلبس اللي يعجب الناس
chunks.text: إكل اللي تبيه وإلبس اللي يعجب الناس · في الأكل اتبع ذوقك، وفي اللباس راعِ ذوق الناس. Benjamin Franklin wrote almost exactly this, so English has a genuine equivalent. What you eat is private; what you wear is seen. Answer: Eat to please yourself, but dress to please others. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إن طاعك الزمان وإلا طيعه
chunks.text: إن طاعك الزمان وإلا طيعه · إذا لم تجرِ الأمور كما تريد، فتكيّف معها. الزمان is circumstance. The advice is to bend rather than break. Said to someone fighting a situation that will not change. Answer: If you can’t change things, adapt to them. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: نام مظلوم ولا تنام ظالم
chunks.text: نام مظلوم ولا تنام ظالم · أن تكون مظلومًا خير من أن تكون ظالمًا. The image is going to sleep at night: better to sleep as the wronged than as the wrongdoer. A moral teaching often said to children. Answer: Better to suffer a wrong than to do one. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لا تكثر الدوس يا خلي تراهم يملونك، لا أنت ولدهم ولا طفل يربونك.
chunks.text: لا تكثر الدوس يا خلي تراهم يملونك، لا أنت ولدهم ولا طفل يربونك. لا تكثر الزيارة فيملّك الناس، فأنت لست من أهل البيت. الدوس is visiting (literally treading the doorstep). English says exactly this. A rhymed couplet. Answer: Don’t wear out your welcome. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: جا يكحلها عماها
chunks.text: جا يكحلها عماها · حاول أن يصلح الأمر فأفسده أكثر. Kohl is meant to beautify the eye; he blinded it instead. English says it plainly. Used about well-meant help that backfires. Answer: He tried to fix it and made it worse. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: بغيناه عون صار فرعون
chunks.text: بغيناه عون صار فرعون · طلبنا منه المساعدة فتسلّط واستبدّ. The helper took over. English uses “an inch and a mile”. عون/فرعون rhyme; Pharaoh is the tyrant figure. Answer: Give him an inch and he’ll take a mile. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: تجيك التهايم وإنت نايم
chunks.text: تجيك التهايم وإنت نايم · قد تُتّهم أو تقع عليك المشاكل وأنت بريء لا شأن لك. Sleeping stands for innocence and doing nothing. Rhymes التهايم/نايم. Answer: Trouble can find you even when you’ve done nothing. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: الحشرة مع الناس عيد
chunks.text: الحشرة مع الناس عيد · الشدة إذا شاركك فيها الناس هانت وصارت محتملة. الحشرة here is a tight spot. Shared with others it becomes as bearable as a feast. Compare المصيبة إذا عمّت هانت. Answer: A trouble shared is a trouble halved. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: خبز خبزتيه يا الرفلة إكليه
chunks.text: خبز خبزتيه يا الرفلة إكليه · تحمّل نتيجة ما فعلته بنفسك. A genuine equivalent: you made it, you live with it. الرفلة is a clumsy woman; the bread came out badly and she must eat it. Answer: You’ve made your bed, now lie in it. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: راعي النصيفة سالم
chunks.text: راعي النصيفة سالم · من يتعامل بالعدل والإنصاف يسلم من المشاكل واللوم. النصيفة is fair dealing — giving everyone their due. Said in disputes and business. Answer: Be fair and you’ll stay out of trouble. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: نوم الظالم عبادة
chunks.text: نوم الظالم عبادة · سخرية من الظالم: نومه خير من يقظته لأنه لا يؤذي أحدًا وهو نائم. Sarcasm: the best thing the oppressor does is sleep. Often said of a bully or harsh boss. Answer: The world is safer while the tyrant sleeps. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: طارت الطيور بأرزاقها
chunks.text: طارت الطيور بأرزاقها · فاتت الفرصة وأخذ كل واحد نصيبه. Everyone has taken their share and gone. English says the chance is gone. Said to someone who arrives too late. Answer: You’ve missed the boat. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: ما للصلايب إلا أهلها
chunks.text: ما للصلايب إلا أهلها · الأمور الصعبة لا يقدر عليها إلا الأقوياء وأهل الخبرة. الصلايب are hard matters. The proverb says leave them to those able. Said when someone steps up to a difficult task. Answer: Tough jobs need people who are made for them. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: الطول طول نخلة والعقل عقل صخلة
chunks.text: الطول طول نخلة والعقل عقل صخلة · شخص كبير الجسم أو المظهر لكنه قليل العقل. Size and sense set side by side. English has a fixed contrast. صخلة is a young goat. The palm and the goat rhyme. Answer: All brawn and no brains. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لا تسرف لو من البحر تغرف
chunks.text: لا تسرف لو من البحر تغرف · لا تبذّر حتى لو كان المورد وفيرًا. لو here means “even if”. A sea-faring people’s image. Answer: Waste not, want not. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: فال الله ولا فالك
chunks.text: فال الله ولا فالك · تُقال لمن تفوّه بكلام متشائم: نرجو ما يقدّره الله لا ما تقوله. A quick reply to an ominous remark. English uses Heaven forbid or touch wood. الفال is an omen; the speaker refuses yours. Answer: Heaven forbid! (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: العين ما تعلى على الحاجب
chunks.text: العين ما تعلى على الحاجب · الأدنى منزلة لا يتعالى على الأعلى منه. The eyebrow sits above the eye. Said to someone overstepping a senior. Often said to younger people. Answer: Know your place. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: فوق شينه قوات عينه
chunks.text: فوق شينه قوات عينه · مخطئ أو سيئ، وفوق ذلك وقح لا يستحي. شين is a fault; قوات عين is boldness. English needs a plain rendering. Rhymes on شينه/عينه. Answer: In the wrong, and brazen with it. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: كثر الدق يفك اللحام
chunks.text: كثر الدق يفك اللحام · كثرة الضغط والتكرار تفكك حتى الأقوى. Both say steady pressure wears down even strong things. Said of nagging, or persistent persuasion. Answer: Constant dripping wears away the stone. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: سو خير وقطه بحر
chunks.text: سو خير وقطه بحر · افعل الخير ولا تنتظر مقابلًا أو شكرًا. Throwing it in the sea means forgetting it, not wasting it. A sea-faring image again. Answer: Do good and expect nothing in return. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: كوم حجار ولا هالجار
chunks.text: كوم حجار ولا هالجار · جار سيئ أسوأ من لا جار. A heap of stones next door is better than this person. Rhymes حجار/جار. Answer: Better no neighbour than a bad one. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: إيد وحدة ما تصفق
chunks.text: إيد وحدة ما تصفق · لا يتم الأمر دون تعاون الطرفين. Some things need both sides. Used both for cooperation and for shared blame. Answer: It takes two to tango. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: البحر ماله أمان
chunks.text: البحر ماله أمان · البحر لا يؤمَن جانبه، ويقال لكل ما يتقلّب ولا يُوثق به. Here the near-literal rendering is the right one: it already works in English. Kuwait’s pearl-diving past. Answer: Never trust the sea. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اللي ما يستحي منك لا تستحي منه
chunks.text: اللي ما يستحي منك لا تستحي منه · عامل الناس بمثل ما يعاملونك به. If someone has no consideration for you, owe them none. Said when someone has been rude. Answer: Treat people the way they treat you. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اللي ما يطول العنب حامضٍ عنه يقول
chunks.text: اللي ما يطول العنب حامضٍ عنه يقول · من لا يستطيع الحصول على شيء يقلّل من قيمته. The same fable, so English has the same idiom. One of the clearest shared images between Arabic and English. Answer: Sour grapes. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: اللي هذا أوله ينعاف تاليه
chunks.text: اللي هذا أوله ينعاف تاليه · إذا كانت البداية سيئة فالنهاية أسوأ. The start tells you how it will end. ينعاف means to be shunned. Answer: A bad beginning makes a bad ending. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: إذا شبع الحمار نهق
chunks.text: إذا شبع الحمار نهق · إذا نال الجاهل ما يريد تعالى وأزعج غيره. Comfort makes the ungrateful loud. Said of someone who forgets themselves once well off. Answer: Give a fool plenty and he grows insolent. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: الوجه بالوجه أبيض
chunks.text: الوجه بالوجه أبيض · المصارحة وجهًا لوجه أفضل من الكلام من وراء الظهر. أبيض means honourable. Said before an honest conversation. Answer: Better to say it to someone’s face. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لو فيه خير ما عافه الطير
chunks.text: لو فيه خير ما عافه الطير · لو كان الشيء جيدًا لما تركه غيرك. Something left untouched is suspect. Often said of a bargain. Answer: If it were any good, it wouldn’t have been left. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اللي يجي من الله حيّاه الله
chunks.text: اللي يجي من الله حيّاه الله · نتقبّل ما يأتي به القدر برضا. A statement of acceptance. حيّاه الله is a welcome. Answer: Whatever God sends is welcome. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: لا تدخل عصك بشي ما يخصك
chunks.text: لا تدخل عصك بشي ما يخصك · لا تتدخل فيما لا يعنيك. English also has “don’t stick your oar in”. عصك is your stick. Answer: Mind your own business. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: لا تأمن على فار شحمه
chunks.text: لا تأمن على فار شحمه · لا تأتمن شخصًا على شيء يطمع فيه. English uses a fox and hens for the same idea. The mouse and the fat are in the Kuwaiti. Answer: Don’t let the fox guard the henhouse. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: القلوب شواهد
chunks.text: القلوب شواهد · المشاعر متبادلة، والقلب يحس بما في القلب الآخر. Feelings are sensed without words, and usually returned. Said when two people feel the same about each other. Answer: Hearts know each other. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: اللي ما يعرفك ما يثمنك
chunks.text: اللي ما يعرفك ما يثمنك · من لا يعرفك جيدًا لا يعرف قيمتك. Worth is seen by those who know you. يثمنك means to put a value on you. Answer: Those who don’t know you can’t value you. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: أستر على ما واجهت
chunks.text: أستر على ما واجهت · طلب ستر زلة أو موقف محرج رآه الآخر. A request for discretion. Said after an embarrassing moment. Answer: Please keep what you saw between us. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: أكل وراحة ونومة في البراحة
chunks.text: أكل وراحة ونومة في البراحة · حياة مريحة بلا تعب ولا مسؤولية. A carefree, idle life. البراحة is the open yard. Answer: Living the life of Riley. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: أحر ما عندي أبرد ما عندك
chunks.text: أحر ما عندي أبرد ما عندك · ما أراه أمرًا ملحًّا ومهمًّا تراه أنت بلا اهتمام. One side burns with concern, the other is indifferent. Said in frustration. Answer: I care about this far more than you do. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: أطعم الفم تستحي العين
chunks.text: أطعم الفم تستحي العين · الإكرام يجعل المُكرَم أكثر حياءً وامتنانًا. A gift makes the receiver hold back. Often about bribes as well. Answer: Generosity buys goodwill. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: طرار ويتشرط
chunks.text: طرار ويتشرط · محتاج ويفرض الشروط. English has the exact proverb. طرار is a beggar. Answer: Beggars can’t be choosers. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: سيل ما يبلك ما يهمك
chunks.text: سيل ما يبلك ما يهمك · ما لا يمسّك لا داعي لأن تهتم به. Said to someone worrying over others’ affairs. The flood is a desert flash flood. Answer: If it doesn’t affect you, don’t worry about it. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: الفرس من خيالها والمره من رجالها
chunks.text: الفرس من خيالها والمره من رجالها · قول تقليدي: الفرس تُعرف بفارسها، والمرأة تُمدح أو تُذم بحسب رجالها. Only the first half travels as an English saying. The second half reflects a traditional view. Reflects older social attitudes. Answer: A horse is known by its rider. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: القطو العود ما يتربى
chunks.text: القطو العود ما يتربى · الكبير يصعب تعليمه أو تغيير عاداته. English swaps the cat for a dog. Same point. العود means old. Answer: You can’t teach an old dog new tricks. (the English equivalent)

chunks.title: الشيفة شيفة والمعاني ضعيفة
chunks.text: الشيفة شيفة والمعاني ضعيفة · المظهر حسن لكن المضمون ضعيف. Good looks, little behind them. Rhymes شيفة/ضعيفة. Answer: All style and no substance. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: تموت الدجاجة وعينها على السبوس
chunks.text: تموت الدجاجة وعينها على السبوس · الطماع يبقى طماعًا حتى النهاية. Even dying, the hen is looking at the feed. السبوس is bran. Answer: Greedy to the very end. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: ردت حليمة لعادتها القديمة
chunks.text: ردت حليمة لعادتها القديمة · عاد الشخص إلى عادته القديمة. A relapse after seeming to change. Halima is a stock name. Answer: Back to old habits. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: من طول الغيبات جاب الغنايم
chunks.text: من طول الغيبات جاب الغنايم · الغائب طويلًا قد يعود بالخير والمكاسب. Said to welcome someone returning from travel. Rhymes الغيبات/الغنايم. Answer: A long absence can bring back rewards. (a natural functional translation)

chunks.title: May the Force be with you.
chunks.text: May the Force be with you. Star Wars (1977) لتكن القوة معك. ليكن معك القوة. القوة · معك · Short source, shorter target. Arabic says this in three words, and there is no reason to spend the whole 32 characters just because they are there — a subtitle that ends early is a subtitle read easily.

chunks.title: I'll be back.
chunks.text: I'll be back. The Terminator (1984) سأعود. سوف أعود. اعود · One second on screen buys twenty characters. The Arabic needs six. The temptation is to add سوف or a pronoun for weight; the line is famous for being flat, and flat is what survives.

chunks.title: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn.
chunks.text: Frankly, my dear, I don't give a damn. Gone with the Wind (1939) بصراحة يا عزيزتي، لا يعنيني الأمر. بصراحة يا عزيزتي، لا أبالي. بصراحه · The line is rude in a register Arabic does not have a single word for, so the rudeness moves into the flatness of لا يعنيني الأمر. Swearing harder in Arabic would be a different character speaking.

chunks.title: To be, or not to be, that is the question.
chunks.text: To be, or not to be, that is the question. Hamlet, Act III · أكون أو لا أكون، تلك هي المسألة. أن أكون أو لا أكون، تلك هي المسألة. اكون · المساله · Some lines arrive already translated: this one has an Arabic form readers recognise, and inventing a fresh rendering would make the most famous sentence in English literature sound like nobody had heard it before. Recognition is part of the meaning.

chunks.title: Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country.
chunks.text: Ask not what your country can do for you; ask what you can do for your country. Kennedy, inaugural address, 1961 · لا تسأل ما يقدمه وطنك لك، بل ما تقدمه أنت لوطنك. لا تسأل ماذا يفعل وطنك لك، بل ماذا تفعل أنت لوطنك. تسال · وطنك · Two lines, and the break is not free: it goes where the sentence turns, after the comma, so each line is a whole thought. Never break a subtitle where the grammar is still open — a reader who reaches the end of line one should not be holding their breath.

chunks.title: All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others.
chunks.text: All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others. Orwell, Animal Farm · كل الحيوانات متساوية، لكن بعضها أكثر تساويًا. الحيوانات كلها متساوية، لكن بعضها أكثر تساويًا. الحيوانات · بعضها · More equal is deliberately broken English and the Arabic must stay broken too: أكثر تساويًا is as wrong in Arabic as the original is in English, which is the whole joke. Repairing it would delete the sentence.

chunks.title: إذا الشعبُ يوماً أراد الحياة · فلا بدَّ أن يستجيب القدر
chunks.text: إذا الشعبُ يوماً أراد الحياة · فلا بدَّ أن يستجيب القدر · أبو القاسم الشابي · If a people wills life, fate must yield. people · live · life · fate · destiny · A full line of verse into forty characters. The metre goes, the rhyme goes, and what must not go is فلا بدَّ — the compulsion. Drop must and the line becomes a hope instead of a law.

chunks.title: وما نيلُ المطالبِ بالتمنّي · ولكن تُؤخَذُ الدنيا غِلابا
chunks.text: وما نيلُ المطالبِ بالتمنّي · ولكن تُؤخَذُ الدنيا غِلابا · أحمد شوقي · Wishing wins nothing. The world is taken. wish · taken · seiz · force · struggl · Two clauses, two sentences, and the full stop in the middle does the work the Arabic caesura does. غِلابا — by struggle — will not fit; taken carries enough of it that the viewer supplies the rest.

chunks.title: قم للمعلّمِ وفِّهِ التبجيلا · كاد المعلّمُ أن يكون رسولا
chunks.text: قم للمعلّمِ وفِّهِ التبجيلا · كاد المعلّمُ أن يكون رسولا · أحمد شوقي · Rise for the teacher, honour him: he is almost a prophet. teacher · prophet · messenger · رسولا is a messenger and a prophet at once, and English must choose. Prophet is the stronger reading and the one the line is quoted for. Note the colon: it holds the two halves together across the line break.

chunks.title: الخيلُ والليلُ والبيداءُ تعرفني · والسيفُ والرمحُ والقرطاسُ والقلمُ
chunks.text: الخيلُ والليلُ والبيداءُ تعرفني · والسيفُ والرمحُ والقرطاسُ والقلمُ · المتنبي · Horse, night and desert know me — so do sword, spear, page and pen. night · desert · sword · pen · Seven nouns and no room for seven. The articles go first — Arabic needs them, a subtitle does not — and that alone buys back the space. Cut grammar before you cut content.

chunks.title: على قَدْرِ أهلِ العزمِ تأتي العزائمُ · وتأتي على قَدْرِ الكرامِ المكارمُ
chunks.text: على قَدْرِ أهلِ العزمِ تأتي العزائمُ · وتأتي على قَدْرِ الكرامِ المكارمُ · المتنبي · Resolve rises to the resolute, and honour to the honourable. resolve · honour · honor · noble · The Arabic repeats a root twice over — العزم/العزائم, الكرام/المكارم. English can do the same trick with resolve/resolute and honour/honourable, so the figure survives. When the target language happens to offer the same move, take it.

chunks.title: أنا الذي نظر الأعمى إلى أدبي · وأسمعت كلماتي من به صممُ
chunks.text: أنا الذي نظر الأعمى إلى أدبي · وأسمعت كلماتي من به صممُ · المتنبي · The blind have seen my verse; the deaf have heard my words. blind · deaf · The boast is in the impossibility, so both halves must stay: keep only the blind and the line is merely proud. The semicolon is doing what the Arabic parallelism does — two halves, one shape.

chunks.title: Here's looking at you, kid.
chunks.text: Here's looking at you, kid. Casablanca (1942) نخبك، يا صغيرتي. في صحتك، يا صغيرتي. نخبك · A toast and an endearment in five English words. نخبك carries the glass; يا صغيرتي carries the affection. Translating kid as طفلة would make him her father instead of her lover.

chunks.title: I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse.
chunks.text: I'm gonna make him an offer he can't refuse. The Godfather (1972) سأعرض عليه عرضًا لا يستطيع رفضه. سأقدم له عرضًا لا يمكنه رفضه. عرض · رفض · The threat is entirely in the politeness, so the Arabic must stay polite too. The line break falls before لا يستطيع, where the sentence turns — the viewer reads a complete offer, then the catch.

chunks.title: There's no place like home.
chunks.text: There's no place like home. The Wizard of Oz (1939) لا مكان يضاهي البيت. لا شيء يعدل البيت. البيت · البيت, not المنزل. One is the place you belong to and the other is the building; English home and house split the same way, and a subtitler who reaches for the building has translated the wrong word.

chunks.title: No, I am your father.
chunks.text: No, I am your father. The Empire Strikes Back (1980) لا، أنا والدك. لا، أنا أبوك. والدك · ابوك · Half the world quotes this as Luke, I am your father, and the film does not say it. A subtitler works from the audio, never from memory — the famous version of a line is very often not the line.

chunks.title: Why so serious?
chunks.text: Why so serious? The Dark Knight (2008) لماذا كل هذا الجد؟ ما كل هذا الجد؟ الجد · Three words, twenty-eight characters to spend, and no reason to spend them. The menace is in how little is said; padding the Arabic to fill the line would soften the one thing that makes it frightening.

chunks.title: Winter is coming.
chunks.text: Winter is coming. Game of Thrones · الشتاء قادم. الشتاء آتٍ. الشتاء · A house motto, so it has to sound like one: short, present, and slightly ominous. قادم does it in one word. Anything explanatory — سيأتي الشتاء قريبًا — turns a warning into a weather report.

chunks.title: I am the one who knocks.
chunks.text: I am the one who knocks. Breaking Bad · أنا من يطرق الباب. أنا الطارق على الباب. يطرق · الطارق · الباب · Arabic has no bare the one who, so من does the work. Note what is not added: no في هذا البيت, no explanation of who he means. The line is a boast made entirely of understatement.

chunks.title: Hakuna Matata! It means no worries.
chunks.text: Hakuna Matata! It means no worries. The Lion King (1994) هاكونا ماتاتا! تعني: لا هموم. هاكونا ماتاتا! معناها: لا تقلق. هاكونا · The Swahili is not translated, because the line translates it for you a second later — render it and the sentence explains a phrase the viewer has not heard. Transcribe what the film treats as foreign, and let the film do the glossing.

chunks.title: Just keep swimming.
chunks.text: Just keep swimming. Finding Nemo (2003) واصلي السباحة فحسب. استمري في السباحة. السباحه · Arabic marks gender where English does not, so the subtitler has to know who is speaking and to whom — Dory to herself, so واصلي. Guess the gender and you have put the wrong person on screen.

chunks.title: Live long and prosper.
chunks.text: Live long and prosper. Star Trek · عش طويلًا وازدهر. طولَ العمر والازدهار. عش · ازدهر · العمر · A formal blessing, and Arabic has a whole register for those. Either rendering works: the imperative keeps the Vulcan formality, the noun phrase sounds like something a person would actually say at a parting. Both fit; the register decides.

chunks.title: Diplomatic and political
chunks.text: Diplomatic and political · سياسي ودبلوماسي · The Charter of the United Nations, in the UN’s own Arabic and English. الجمعية العامة · English: general assembly / the general assembly · مجلس الأمن · English: security council / the security council · المجلس الاقتصادي والاجتماعي · English: economic and social council / the economic and social council · مجلس الوصاية · English: trusteeship council / the trusteeship council · محكمة العدل الدولية · English: international court of justice / the international court of justice · الأمانة · English: secretariat / the secretariat · الأمين العام · English: secretary-general / secretary general / the secretary-general · المساواة في السيادة · English: sovereign equality · التدابير المشتركة الفعّالة · English: effective collective measures · أعمال العدوان · English: acts of aggression · السلطان الداخلي · English: domestic jurisdiction · المحبة للسلام · English: peace-loving / peace loving · حفظ السلم والأمن الدولي · English: maintain international peace and security / to maintain international peace and security / maintenance of international peace and security / the maintenance of international peace and security · بالوسائل السلمية · English: by peaceful means · في حسن نية · English: in good faith · إنماء العلاقات الودية بين الأمم · English: to develop friendly relations among nations / develop friendly relations among nations · بناءً على توصية مجلس الأمن · English: upon the recommendation of the security council · ويلات الحرب · English: the scourge of war / scourge of war · الحقوق الأساسية للإنسان · English: fundamental human rights

chunks.title: Diplomatic and political (cont.)
chunks.text: تقوم الهيئة على مبدأ المساواة في السيادة بين جميع أعضائها. English: The Organization is based on the principle of the sovereign equality of all its Members. organization · principle · sovereign equality · members · يفض جميع أعضاء الهيئة منازعاتهم الدولية بالوسائل السلمية على وجه لا يجعل السلم والأمن والعدل الدولي عرضة للخطر. English: All Members shall settle their international disputes by peaceful means in such a manner that international peace and security, and justice, are not endangered. members · disputes · peaceful means · peace and security · justice · endangered · قبول أية دولة من هذه الدول في عضوية الأمم المتحدة يتم بقرار من الجمعية العامة بناءً على توصية مجلس الأمن. English: The admission of any such state to membership in the United Nations will be effected by a decision of the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council. admission · membership · general assembly · recommendation · security council · إذا أمعن عضو من أعضاء الأمم المتحدة في انتهاك مبادئ الميثاق جاز للجمعية العامة أن تفصله من الهيئة بناءً على توصية مجلس الأمن. English: A Member of the United Nations which has persistently violated the Principles contained in the present Charter may be expelled from the Organization by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council. member · persistently violated · principles · expelled · general assembly · security council · والأمين العام هو الموظف الإداري الأكبر في الهيئة. English: He shall be the chief administrative officer of the Organization. chief administrative officer · organization

chunks.title: Diplomatic and political (cont.)
chunks.text: يرفع مجلس الأمن تقارير سنوية، وأخرى خاصة، إذا اقتضت الحال إلى الجمعية العامة لتنظر فيها. English: The Security Council shall submit annual and, when necessary, special reports to the General Assembly for its consideration. security council · annual · special reports · general assembly · consideration · نحن شعوب الأمم المتحدة وقد آلينا على أنفسنا أن ننقذ الأجيال المقبلة من ويلات الحرب التي في خلال جيل واحد جلبت على الإنسانية مرتين أحزاناً يعجز عنها الوصف. English: We the peoples of the United Nations determined to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war, which twice in our lifetime has brought untold sorrow to mankind. peoples of the united nations · determined · succeeding generations · scourge of war · twice · untold sorrow · يمتنع أعضاء الهيئة جميعاً في علاقاتهم الدولية عن التهديد باستعمال القوة أو استخدامها ضد سلامة الأراضي أو الاستقلال السياسي لأية دولة أو على أي وجه آخر لا يتفق ومقاصد الأمم المتحدة. chunks.title: Human rights and humanitarian
chunks.text: Human rights and humanitarian · حقوق الإنسان والعمل الإنساني · The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, in the UN’s own Arabic and English. حقوق الإنسان · English: human rights · الكرامة · English: dignity · التعذيب · English: torture · الجنسية · English: nationality · الاضطهاد · English: persecution · التمييز · English: discrimination / distinction · الاسترقاق · English: slavery · الحريات الأساسية · English: fundamental freedoms · بروح الإخاء · English: in a spirit of brotherhood · دون أي تمييز · English: without distinction of any kind / without any discrimination · حرية الرأي والتعبير · English: freedom of opinion and expression · حرية الاشتراك في الجمعيات والجماعات السلمية · English: freedom of peaceful assembly and association · حرية التنقل · English: freedom of movement · سواسية أمام القانون · English: equal before the law · لكل فرد الحق في الحياة والحرية وفي الأمان على شخصه. English: Everyone has the right to life, liberty and the security of person. right · life · liberty · security · لا يجوز استرقاق أحد أو استعباده، ويحظر الاسترقاق وتجارة الرقيق بجميع صورهما. English: No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms. slavery · servitude · slave trade · prohibited · لا يعرض أي إنسان للتعذيب ولا للعقوبات أو المعاملات القاسية أو الوحشية أو الحاطة بالكرامة. English: No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. torture · cruel · degrading · treatment · لا يجوز القبض على أي إنسان أو حجزه أو نفيه تعسفاً.

chunks.title: Human rights and humanitarian (cont.)
chunks.text: English: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile. arbitrary · arrest · detention · exile · لكل فرد حق التمتع بجنسية ما. English: Everyone has the right to a nationality. right · nationality · لا يجوز تجريد أحد من ملكه تعسفاً. English: No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property. arbitrarily · deprived · property · لا يجوز إرغام أحد على الانضمام إلى جمعية ما. English: No one may be compelled to belong to an association. compelled · belong · association · يحق لكل فرد أن يغادر أية بلاد بما في ذلك بلده كما يحق له العودة إليه. English: Everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country. leave · country · own · return · يولد جميع الناس أحراراً متساوين في الكرامة والحقوق. وقد وهبوا عقلاً وضميراً وعليهم أن يعامل بعضهم بعضاً بروح الإخاء. English: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood. born free · equal · dignity · reason · conscience · brotherhood · لكل شخص الحق في حرية الرأي والتعبير. ويشمل هذا الحق حرية اعتناق الآراء دون أي تدخل، واستقاء الأنباء والأفكار وتلقيها وإذاعتها بأية وسيلة كانت دون تقيد بالحدود الجغرافية. English: Everyone has the right to freedom of opinion and expression; this right includes freedom to hold opinions without interference and to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers. freedom · opinion · expression · interference · information · frontiers

chunks.title: Human rights and humanitarian (cont.)
chunks.text: لكل فرد الحق أن يلجأ إلى بلاد أخرى أو يحاول الالتجاء إليها هرباً من الاضطهاد. ولا ينتفع بهذا الحق من قدم للمحاكمة في جرائم غير سياسية أو لأعمال تناقض أغراض الأمم المتحدة ومبادئها. English: Everyone has the right to seek and to enjoy in other countries asylum from persecution. This right may not be invoked in the case of prosecutions genuinely arising from non-political crimes or from acts contrary to the purposes and principles of the United Nations. asylum · persecution · non-political · purposes · principles · united nations · لا يعرض أحد لتدخل تعسفي في حياته الخاصة أو أسرته أو مسكنه أو مراسلاته أو لحملات على شرفه وسمعته. ولكل شخص الحق في حماية القانون من مثل هذا التدخل أو تلك الحملات. English: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to attacks upon his honour and reputation. Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks. arbitrary · privacy · family · honour · reputation · protection of the law

chunks.title: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood.
chunks.text: Legal and human rights · All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. They are endowed with reason and conscience and should act towards one another in a spirit of brotherhood. Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 1 (United Nations, 1948). يُولد جميعُ الناس أحراراً ومتساوين في الكرامة والحقوق، وقد وُهبوا العقلَ والضمير، وعليهم أن يعامل بعضُهم بعضاً بروح الإخاء. Start with the verb and join the two sentences with و. Then compare your version with the official United Nations Arabic text — this is one of the few passages in the world with an official equivalent.

chunks.title: الخيلُ والليلُ والبيداءُ تعرفني ... والسيفُ والرمحُ والقرطاسُ والقلمُ
chunks.text: Classical poetry · الخيلُ والليلُ والبيداءُ تعرفني ... والسيفُ والرمحُ والقرطاسُ والقلمُ. al-Mutanabbi. Try to keep the rhythm of the list. The horses, the night and the desert know me, as do the sword, the spear, the paper and the pen. Keep the list of seven nouns; steeds and parchment would sound more classical. This is the line al-Jahiz would have said cannot cross.

chunks.title: Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate.
chunks.text: English poetry · Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day? Thou art more lovely and more temperate. Sonnet 18 (Shakespeare, 1609). أأشبّهكِ بيومٍ من أيام الربيع؟ أنتِ أبهى منه وأكثرُ اعتدالاً. Spring gives Arab readers the pleasant feeling that summer gives English readers — cultural approximation. Arabic must also choose a gender for thee: Sonnet 18 belongs to the sonnets usually read as addressed to a young man, so أأشبّهكَ is equally defensible. Whichever you choose, explain it in the commentary.

chunks.title: Health officials have urged residents to stay indoors between 11 a.m. and 4 p.m. as temperatures are expected to top 50°C this week. “Heatstroke is not something to take lightly,” a Ministry of Health spokesperson said, advising people to drink plenty of water and to check on elderly neighbours.
